News.title: Adam Ramsay-Peaty breaks down in tears after settling for bronze
News.content:
Afterwards, Ramsay-Peaty, whose alleged dispute with his own family became a major distraction during his marriage earlier this year, was visibly emotional as he criticised the media which he insisted had written “rubbish” about his personal life.

“I know the s--- I’ve been through, which is no fault of my own, to be honest,” said Ramsay-Peaty, who lost his 100m breaststroke crown two years ago at the Paris Olympics. “But it does take a toll. The choices I’ve made over the last few months have been hard ones. But I’m happy at the same time that I can get here. I didn’t quit in Paris, but I deserve more.”

He added: “You don’t know who I am and people who comment, people who see the story because you read a headline, they’ve got to look themselves in the mirror,” Ramsay-Peaty told a group of reporters.

“You can’t hurt me. For me, it’s about my family and that does come at a cost. Being able to ignore that and being able to focus on my job – that hasn’t played a part in a sense of what we’re experiencing today.

“I’m still happy with that result. There’s some sense, but it has to, it has to stop. You know, look how many, how many athletes, how many people have to go for this until the media learn [a] lesson?”

Referencing Nowacki, the 18-year-old sensation from Jersey who has long been regarded as Ramsay-Peaty’s breaststroke successor, he added; “You have to learn and do better. You know, and for me, you know, I don’t want a young Filip one day to go through something like that, or these younger athletes.

“For me, that’s part of what I have to go through. I’ve got no control over that. But I think enough is enough. This is away from sport – it’s just about being decent people.”

After receiving his bronze medal, Ramsay-Peaty approached his wife, with whom he is expecting a child in December, and kissed her baby bump.

News.title: Lewis Hamilton hit with penalty in blow to Hungarian GP hopes
News.content:
Lewis Hamilton’s hopes of significantly denting Kimi Antonelli’s championship lead were dealt a blow after he was given a three-place grid penalty for Sunday’s Hungarian Grand Prix.

Hamilton looked to be the man to beat heading into qualifying at the Hungaroring and was on course for a record 10th pole position here before a messy final few minutes cost him.

Ferrari were well placed to end Mercedes’s run of having taken pole position for every grand prix this season. Instead, defending champion Lando Norris snuck in and took a superb pole for McLaren with a lap of 1min 17.207sec.

A poor final lap from Hamilton was compounded by a grid penalty for impeding the McLaren of Oscar Piastri, meaning the seven-time world champion will start fifth for the race at one of his most favoured circuits. The only consolation was that Antonelli was also given a three-place grid penalty for not slowing sufficiently under yellow flags. The Italian will start seventh while Charles Leclerc, Hamilton’s team-mate, will be alongside Norris on the front row.

Heading into the final runs in Q3, Hamilton was 0.101sec ahead of Norris, but did not improve his time. Yet Norris, who was fastest in Q1 and Q2, and was the last of the top three across the line in Q3, had no problem, beating Hamilton’s time by 0.012sec.

Hamilton was critical of his Ferrari team for sending him out first, a decision he said “shocked” him.

“I don’t know why we went first, that was a bit of a shock to me and I definitely wouldn’t have chosen to go first,” Hamilton said. “I had a clean out-lap and when I started my lap and already in turn one I had a snap [of oversteer], I was already a tenth down. The last lap was the worst lap of all... we clearly had the car to be on pole.”

Worse was on the way for Hamilton. The stewards later confirmed the three-place grid penalty to add to the disappointment of missing out on pole.

Replays showed a frustrated Piastri gesturing to Hamilton for blocking him at turn one, ruining the Australian’s final flying lap. Hamilton said he was unaware that Piastri was there, which was proved by video evidence that showed how much he impeded the McLaren. It would have been an easy decision for the stewards to make.

News.title: ‘Always in bloom, a visit really makes one’s day’: Your favourite garden centres
News.content:
Bryan, 86, from the South East, has been a customer of Henry Street Garden Centre in Arborfield, Berkshire for decades: “My wife and I often used to browse and purchase plants and garden furniture.”

But his favourite memory was watching his wife’s “delight at their incredible Christmas displays of decorations. Lights, live reindeer even and the wonderful family atmosphere all around you,” he describes. “It’s still a magical place for me where I can get close to her memory.”

For Mary, 79, from the South East, “a garden centre is special if the plants are in season and healthy and there is great choice of both plants and compost”. She nominates family-run Grovewell Garden Centres at Swingfield near Folkestone, which has three other branches based in Kent.

Not only are their plants “always beautifully displayed”, she explains, they have “an amazing choice of garden supplies, cards and gifts, as well as a nice little coffee shop”. Her favourite memory, however, was at Christmas time a few years ago. “They have a couple of beautiful, nodding and interacting reindeer with a sofa in front of them. We were admiring them and an older guy on the staff asked if we wanted a photo taken, which was so sweet of him.”

“He took my husband’s phone and got a really happy little snap of us and the reindeer, which our girls thought was hilarious,” she says. “Service with a smile.”

Community spirit

News.content:
Newcastle will welcome Liverpool, with whom Keegan enjoyed success in the 1970s, to St James’ Park for their Premier League opener, and the two sides are in talks over a suitable pre-match tribute. Summer signings Sean Steur and Ewen Jaouen were each handed 45 minutes in the behind-closed-doors victory over Darlington, during which Howe used different XIs for the two halves. News.title: How to choose a sports bra, with advice from a netball player, bra fitter and scientist
News.content:
How do you tell if a sports bra is the wrong size?

One of the biggest mistakes shoppers make is assuming that if a sports bra feels tight, that’s enough. In reality, support comes from the right fit rather than simply compressing your chest.

Cardwell advises thoroughly testing a sports bra by moving in it in the same way as you will during the sport you will be doing. “Your breasts don’t just move up and down,” she says. “They move all around – circles, up, down, left, right. We want to try and restrict that as much as possible, but not to the extreme where you’re not able to breathe.”

What is a high impact sports bra?

High-impact sports bras are designed for activities where your breasts experience the greatest movement, such as running, HIIT, tennis and netball. Their job is to minimise breast movement in every direction, helping reduce discomfort while allowing you to move more efficiently.

To measure how high-impact a sports bra is, Wakefield-Scurr asks women to run in a laboratory, both without a bra and while wearing different sports bras. “For a bra to be classed as high support, it has to reduce breast movement above certain thresholds,” she says. “If your breasts move 10 centimetres without a bra and five centimetres in a sports bra, that bra has reduced breast movement by 50 per cent.”

In the lab, Wakefield-Scurr and her team found that “if you run in low support compared with high support, you reduce your stride length by four centimetres. Four centimetres might not sound like a lot, but over the course of a marathon, those four centimetres add up to around a mile.” This proves that wearing a high-support bra doesn’t just keep you comfortable, but it can improve your athletic performance.

Cardwell, who wears a double G cup, says high-impact support has improved dramatically in recent years. “There has been a lot more research into high-impact sports bras, especially for larger-chested women.” She also warns against assuming that every sports bra offers the same level of support. “If it’s the same material as a smaller cup size, it’s probably not going to be sufficient for someone like me with double Gs.”

How often should you replace your sports bra?

There’s no set rule for replacing a sports bra, according to Wakefield-Scurr. This is because its lifespan depends more on how you care for it than how often you wear it. “The lifespan of a sports bra is affected more by how you wash and dry it than by how often you wear it,” she says. In one of her team’s studies, support dropped by around a third after 25 washes. “Always follow the washing instructions,” she advises. “You’d be surprised how many sports bras should be hand washed or washed at a lower temperature.”

Looking after your sports bra properly will help it last longer, but no bra lasts forever. Once the underband loses its elasticity or the support noticeably decreases, it’s time to replace it to ensure you have the right level of support.

Sports.title: Jamie Gittens says £117m Morgan Rogers can win Chelsea the league – even if it pushes him further from starting XI
Sports.content:
MORGAN ROGERS’ British record move can drive Chelsea to win titles – according to the man trying to keep him out of the team.

Jamie Gittens is working back from a hamstring injury which curtailed a frustrating first season for the Blues, so perhaps the last thing he needed was a new £117million signing to compete with.



However, the winger has welcomed the addition of England star Rogers and feels the entire club has been boosted by his arrival alongside new boss Xabi Alonso.

Gittens, who made five England Under-21 appearances alongside Rogers, was training in front of 4,500 fans in Sydney as he and his teammates kickstarted their tour of Australia and Asia yesterday.



Rogers, on holiday after the World Cup, will not join up with Alonso’s squad until they return to London next month, but his move from Aston Villa – confirmed last week – has already sent ripples through the squad.

Gittens said: “We want to win everything – that is our ambition, to win the Premier League, the FA Cup and win anything that we’re in.

“Bringing in a player like Morgan will hopefully raise the bar to win titles. He’s a top player. That’s all I can say. He’s just an amazing player.



“Our quality is there, for sure, as a team we have individuals on the pitch who can do amazing things but we have to try and put that together.

“The squad is very competitive. We have to keep working hard and showing what we’re made of.

“Everyone is very positive, looking forward to the new season and to be better and to succeed, which is the main thing.”

Gittens had experience of facing Alonso’s title-winning Bayer Leverkusen side with Borussia Dortmund, from whom he joined Chelsea last year.

While he only lost to them once in five appearances, a 3-2 defeat in which he scored, the winger says they were a challenging side to face and is delighted to now be working under the Spaniard – who was heavily involved in training down under.

He added: “That was hard! Because of the system, I’d say. It was a back three as well. They had Florian Wirtz, they had Jeremie Frimpong and, Amine Adli when we came off the bench sometimes, they had Piero Hincapie. Granit Xhaka as well. They were a real team.

“He [Alonso] was obviously a top player so for him to come in and teach us is the best thing for us.

“A World class midfielder, he’s probably the best to ever do it. He’s a very nice guy. He talks to us individually, speaks to us about what we can improve on, what we can do better. As a player, that’s all you want.



“He’s told me to keep being positive, to keep on taking on players, to keep on creating chances and to keep on pushing myself to the maximum.”

And how about being on the end of a pin-point Alonso cross in training? Gittens added: “It’s amazing, really. He does have a bit of an aura because he was a top player back in the day and obviously a top coach.”

Gittens himself is confident the energy of Alonso arriving alongside big signings can carry him to a much better season than last year.

Sports.title: Fury as EIGHT ‘greedy’ Prem clubs including Chelsea and Tottenham hike price of replica footie shirts to as high as £90
Sports.content:
EIGHT Premier League clubs — including Chelsea and Tottenham — have increased the price of their replica footie shirts.

Tens of thousands of fans now face forking out up to £90 to back their teams when the new ­season kicks off next month.



Spurs supporters must pay £90 for a replica adult first-team shirt, up £5 from last season. Chelsea has also hiked the price of a shirt by £5 to £89.99.

The biggest price rises, £10 each, are Sunderland and promoted Coventry City — from £60 to £70.



Ipswich Town has hiked prices by £6, or ten per cent, to £65

Leeds, Bournemouth and Hull shirts are all up in price by £5.

The average price of a basic adult shirt has now reached £77.20.

Ten clubs charge £80 or more for a shirt.

Brentford’s kit has a two year-cycle – the only Premier League club to do so — in a bid to keep them affordable.

Fans can also pay more to get names, numbers and badges added

Tottenham’s kids’ shirts are also the most expensive, at £70.

Coventry City children’s shirts are up by 25 per cent to £60.



Consumer expert Scott Dixon warned: “We see this year in, year out, and it smacks of blatant greed and an own goal that could backfire.

“These kits are ­overpriced by anyone’s standards and will leave many fans priced out.

“Fans deserve better. Clubs should be making it easier for the next generation of supporters to feel part of their club, not pricing them out.”

Sports.title: Arsenal will have to smash contract record to secure £400,000-week Vinicius Jr transfer from Real Madrid

ARSENAL will have to break their own contract record to land Real Madrid superstar Vinicius Jr by offering him the highest wages in the club’s history.

The Gunners have launched an audacious bid to land Vinicius, 26, as they look to retain their Premier League title and go up an extra level by winning their first ever Champions League.



The North Londoners have turned their attention to the star forward, whose contract at Real runs out in 2027 and he has yet to agree fresh terms on his whopping £400,000-week deal.

But Arsenal would have to splash the cash to buy the Brazil international from Real, with new manager Jose Mourinho unwilling to part with the team’s biggest names.



The Prem champs would also have to at least match Vinicius’ Madrid salary if they hope to complete this massive transfer coup.

That means Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta would have to revert to extravagant contracts within his squad.

That was something Arteta eradicated upon his first year in charge at the Emirates back in 2019, when he swiftly axed the likes of Mesut Ozil and Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang, who earned north of £350,000 per week.

Sports.title: England DENIED automatic Euro 2028 spot for hosting – despite Argentina qualifying for World Cup by staging one match
Sports.content:
ENGLAND have to qualify for Euro 2028 despite being co-hosts – unlike Argentina at the next World Cup.

With millions of fans signing a petition to have the 2022 Qatar winners BANNED from future tournaments, they are furious to know a place in four years is already guaranteed.



And that comes with Lionel Scaloni’s side only hosting ONE game.

Spain, Portugal and Morocco are the 2030 World Cup hosts and have been given automatic berths.



But more controversially, Argentina, Uruguay and Paraguay have all been given places by virtue of hosting only their countries’ opening matches in the centenary edition.

England, however – who will welcome countries from across Europe for the 24 team Euros – are not in the hat for their own tournament just yet.

Games will be played across Wembley, the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium, the Etihad, Everton‘s Hill Dickinson, St James’ Park, and Villa Park.

International tournament hosts are usually granted immediate entry into tournaments, like USA, Canada, and Mexico were for this summer‘s World Cup.

But new Uefa qualifying rules mean England will go into one of 12 groups of four or five sides along with all 50 other nations for Euro 2028, and won’t get the same degree of special treatment.

They will be kept apart from Scotland, Wales, and Republic of Ireland, who will also be hosting matches.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

And all group winners go through automatically, as well as eight of the best runners up.

That is still only 20 of the 24 spots taken up, though, with two reserved for hosts in case they DO NOT qualify via the groups.

This means that if any two of the other hosts DO get through, England will be guaranteed a place no matter what they do as they will have a reserved space to themselves.

Although failing to get in via finishing top or second would raise serious questions.

And if three or four of hosts fail to qualify through the groups then only the top two highest ranked ones would get the designated host space.



England, again, are among the best in the world so will have a spot almost certainly theirs.

But at a time where Argentina are drawing mass criticism for behaviour on and off the field, their first-class ticket to Spain, Portugal and Morocco has frustrated footie watchers.

Sports.content:
A CO-FOUNDER of social media giant Facebook has been invited to join a consortium with hopes of buying a stake in Liverpool.

Reports emerged earlier this week that a group of wealthy individuals were feeling out the purchase of a portion of the iconic North West club.



Amazon founder and one of the world’s richest men Jeff Bezos was said to be among those pitched the idea.

And now, according to reports from Sky News, it seems he could be joined in the endeavour by Eduardo Saverin, one of the minds behind Facebook‘s early success.



The Brazilian-born businessman helped get the site up and running alongside fellow Harvard student Mark Zuckerberg in 2004.

He left the company acrimoniously years later, but continued to grow his fortune in other endeavours, such as venture capital firm B Capital.

Forbes ranked him as the 68th richest person on the planet earlier this year.

Saverin has reportedly been approached by British-Indian businessman Amit Bhatia, who is spearheading the bid.

Bhatia has experience with professional sports business, serving as a co-owner, and at times Chairman, of QPR since 2004.

But he resigned earlier this week after 18 seasons with the West London outfit.



CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

The syndicate are believed to have hired advisers to put together a deal with current Liverpool owners Fenway Sports Group (FSG).

It is not known how or if Singapore-based investor Saverin has responded to the offer, but he could certainly bring some financial muscle to the table.

And he could potentially team up with Bezos to really bolster the backing of the Anfield outfit, who are trying to put together a deal for Paris Saint-Germain winger Bradley Barcola.

FSG confirmed the approach in a statement to the Financial times, saying: “An investment consortium led, managed, and represented by Amit Bhatia has expressed interest in making a strategic minority investment in Liverpool Football Club.”

Sports.title: Surprise new job for Cristiano Ronaldo as ex-Man Utd ace agrees to star in huge drama about UK football
Sports.content:
ACE Cristiano Ronaldo is behind a major drama series about football — and will even star in it.

The former Man United striker is an executive producer of the show about a fictional agent, played by Homeland star Damian Lewis.



Filming has already started, with British star Damian seen at the home of Barnet FC, in North West London.

Ronaldo, 41, will appear and executive produce — while a TV insider revealed his former Arsenal rival Thierry Henry, 48, will also feature on the show, called Day 1s.



They said: “It’s likely to spark a bidding war between the streamers.

“The sheer calibre of figures behind it, not to mention the cast, means it’s a prestige project — albeit a surprising one for Ronaldo as he crosses into making dramas.”



It will tell the fictional tale of a top football agent called Stanley Dalton, played by Homeland and Billions star Damian Lewis, 55.

It is based on a concept devised by another of the show’s executive producers, real-life agent Darren Dein, 52, who represents Henry.

The insider added: “After the World Cup, there’s a renewed international interest, particularly in the States, in British football. It’s one that’s been growing for some time with shows like Ted Lasso.

“But this isn’t a sitcom. It’s definitely a drama, with some comedic elements, and has some serious names backing it.”



The show will be made by the new UR•Marv Studios, which Ronaldo runs with top director Matthew Vaughn, and will also star British rapper Dave and newcomer Carlotta Banat.

Henry was recently pictured at work on the first day of filming at the football ground of Barnet FC, in North West London.

Vaughn, who directed films including Kingsman and Kick-Ass, formed UR•Marv earlier this year, with the mission statement of disrupting the “conventional” movie-making market.



At the time, he said: “Cristiano has created stories on the pitch that I could never have written, and I look forward to creating inspiring movies with him.”

Ronaldo said: “This is an exciting chapter for me, as I look ahead to new ventures.” The ace, who has more than one billion social media followers, scored three goals for Portugal at the World Cup and still captains Saudi side Al-Nassr.

Sports.title: Liverpool news: Barcola makes call on forcing transfer as new signing ruled out for the season
Sports.content:
Liverpool news: Barcola makes call on forcing transfer as new signing ruled out for the season

Liverpool have received a major update in their transfer chase to sign's PSG and France star Bradley Barcola

View 2 Images Bradley Barcola reportedly will not force an exit from PSG as Liverpool hope to snap up his signing (Image: Getty Images)

Andoni Iraola's first summer transfer window at Liverpool has been a mixed bag thus far but looks like it's set to heat up significantly. And the saga surrounding Paris Saint-Germain forward Bradley Barcola in particular has taken on a new form of late.

‌



The Reds are still heavily invested in sourcing a successor to Mohamed Salah following his exit ahead of schedule this summer. Victor Munoz's £34million arrival from Osasuna has helped replenish the ranks, though more business is widely expected at Anfield.

‌



There's less welcome news on the transfer front after one of this summer's fresh signings has been told he can't play this season. Mirror Football addresses all that in more detail as the Reds continue their pre-season tour of the United States.

‌



FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Barcola 'won't force PSG exit'

Despite the promise of a Premier League move on the other side, France winger Barcola seemingly won't push his luck at PSG. It emerged on Sunday the 23-year-old has told his current employers he has no intention of signing a new contract at the Parc des Princes.

Liverpool sent strong Michael Olise transfer warning by Bayern Munich chief READ MORE :

Liverpool and Arsenal alerted after Bradley Barcola transfer call as PSG seek record fee READ MORE :

That seemingly applies beyond this summer after he rejected PSG's latest offering of fresh contract talks. And the current state of play certainly ramps up the pressure on his club to consider a sale if they're to maximise his sale.

‌



Le Parisien has reported Barcola "will not force a move" from his home of the past three years. Further to that, it's not even clear if he has his heart set on leaving this summer, just that he's not interested in extending his current terms.

It's also alleged Barcola has already turned down an approach from Chelsea earlier this summer. And that too could bode well for the Reds, possibly hinting Barcola has a specific destination in mind.

It may complicate things on Liverpool's end as one of their preferred choices to replace Mohamed Salah may prove even more difficult to recruit as a result. However, it suggests the former Lyon youngster is a man of principles as he seemingly won't pull any old trick to get a move.

The 18-year-old's £2.6m move from Austria Wien was confirmed in January but didn't officially go through until July. However, it may not be long before Ndukwe is heading back out of the exit if he's not allowed represent the Reds.

It's been confirmed Ndukwe hasn't met the threshold to obtain a work permit in the UK. In turn, a loan elsewhere looks all but inevitable for the teenager so that he can attain the necessary experience and become a viable option in the near future.

The development is a particularly damaging one in light of Gomez's injury, with fellow new signing Jeremy jacquet yet to make his debut and youngster Giovanni Leoni on his way back from a serious knee injury. The news also comes in the wake of Ibrahima Konate's free transfer to Real Madrid as Iraola looks to reshape Liverpool's backline this summer.

Sports.content:

Manchester United continue to push for more transfers this summer ahead of the upcoming Premier League season

View 3 Images Manu Kone could be on his way to Old Trafford this summer (Image: Johnny Fidelin/Icon Sport via Getty Images)

Manchester United are pushing for more reinforcements as they continue their pre-season tour of Europe. Michael Carrick has welcomed Youri Tielemans, Karl Darlow and Andrey Santos to Old Trafford.

The United boss needs to build a squad capable of competing domestically and in the Champions League. Paris Saint-Germain are next up for the Red Devils before Leeds and then a reunion with Ruben Amorim against AC Milan.

Carrick could have another transfer through the door before the next fixture as Manu Kone has reportedly agreed personal terms to head to Old Trafford. And another target in Carlos Baleba is desperate to join him as the Brighton star explores the possibility of a United move.

Man Utd given Manu Kone transfer deadline as Roma annoyed at slow deal READ MORE :

View 3 Images Manu Kone has agreed terms with United (Image: Jose Breton/Pics Action/NurPhoto via Getty Images)

It is understood that United are in contact with Roma and plan to submit a bid of around £42.7million (€50m). Real Madrid withdrew from the race for Kone after seeing their £34.1m (€40m) offer rejected.

Sports.title: Arsenal news: Big Vinicius Jr transfer update as target tries to force move

Arsenal news: Big Vinicius Jr transfer update as target tries to force move

Arsenal transfer latest as Mikel Arteta chases Vinicius Jr

View 3 Images Vinicius Jr is set for key talks over his future (Image: Getty Images)

Arsenal's summer business has been completely overshadowed after it emerged they are exploring an audacious bid to sign Vinicius Jr from Real Madrid. The Gunners' interest in the Brazil international, who has one year remaining on his contract, is genuine.

‌



It is believed that a move for Vinicius – who scored 22 times for Real last season and netted four goals at the World Cup – is in its very formative stages as Mikel Arteta looks to land a marquee signing to build on the club's first Premier League title in more than two decades.

‌



The 26-year-old fits that bill, with Atletico Madrid's Julian Alvarez, RB Leipzig's Yan Diomande and Bradley Barcola of Paris Saint-Germain also on their radar.

‌



Arsenal have already bolstered their attacking options with the £34million signing of Christos Tzolis from Club Brugge but landing Vinicius would blow their other dealings out of the water. Here's a round-up of the latest Gunners transfer news…

FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Vinicius' stance

Amid the excitement among Arsenal fans, it has emerged that Vinicius is still leaning towards staying with Real Madrid, despite his contract impasse with the club.

‌



Spanish media share Vinicius Jr to Arsenal transfer truth and if deal will happen READ MORE :

Vinicius has just a year remaining on his current deal and Los Blancos are desperate to avoid losing him for nothing next summer. According to Spanish media, he is asking for an increase that would take his wages to around £17m net per year.

According to AS, talks between player and club will resume in days once he returns from his post-World Cup break. Vinicius and his team want clarity on two key issues: where he fits into returning boss Jose Mourinho's plans and whether he can secure a salary that reflects his global status in the game.

View 3 Images Vinicius Jr is being linked with a sensational move to Arsenal (Image: Lars Baron/Getty Images)

‌



Mourinho, who has signed a three-year deal at the Bernabeu, was criticised for comments he made after Vinicius accused Benfica's Gianluca Prestianni of racially abusing him during a Champions League tie in February.

But Mourinho, who was Benfica's manager at the time, reportedly wants Vinicius and the club's other top stars to stay. AS says the intention of both sides is to agree a new deal, despite the Gunners' interest.

View 3 Images Bradley Barcola is pushing to leave PSG (Image: Getty)

‌



Barcola wants out

Barcola has told PSG he will not be signing a new contract amid Arsenal's interest in the France World Cup star.

Barcola has been key to PSG's success in recent seasons but could fall down the pecking order as Luis Enrique looks to revamp his forward line, which could see them sign the in-demand Diomande.

Whether PSG win the race to sign Diomande or not, it appears Barcola wants out, having told the club he has no intention of extending his contract. The 23-year-old's deal with the European champions has two years left to run.

Sports.title: Marcus Rashford told to release 'almighty statement' to save Man Utd career
Sports.content:
Marcus Rashford told to release 'almighty statement' to save Man Utd career

Marcus Rashford saw a dream move to Barcelona fall through following his loan spell and the forward is expected to return to parent side Manchester United in the coming weeks

View 2 Images Marcus Rashford is due to return to Manchester United after his World Cup commitments (Image: Getty Images)

Marcus Rashford has been told to release an 'almighty statement' in a last-ditch effort to save his Manchester United career - but even that might only be enough for a bit-part role.

‌



The Red Devils academy graduate has fallen down the pecking order at Old Trafford over the past few years. He was initially sent out on loan to Aston Villa, before joining Barcelona on a season-long loan deal last term.

‌



The Spanish giants had an option to sign him permanently but decided against it in the end. That decision will see Rashford return to Manchester over the coming weeks, once he rounds off a holiday following his commitments with England at the World Cup.

‌



However, former England international Micky Gray believes Rashford needs to release a lengthy statement re-affirming his commitment to United.

Jadon Sancho finally receives shock contract offer months after Man Utd exit READ MORE :

Free agent XI including Man Utd flop, Liverpool legend and current England star READ MORE :

Speaking on talkSPORT, he said: "There's a few things here. The most important one is, if Rashford has a future at Man United, he has to do an almighty statement of why he wants to be at Man United and what the reasons were to leave the club in the first place.

“I think that's a priority that he has to do. If he does stay then he's got to get used to being a bit-part player.

‌



"He's not first on the list; he's not going to be playing every week...[Bryan] Mbuemo, [Matheus] Cunha, [Benjamin] Sesko, Amad to name a few. They've caught up to and if not surpassed Rashford.

"Spain is not England. He did very well, but he can play at Barcelona at a different level to what he can at Man United. He can't deny that the Premier League is 100mph – he's going to have to get himself super fit in pre-season.

View 2 Images Marcus Rashford has not played for Manchester United in nearly two years (Image: Getty Images)

"We saw the good and the bad of Rashford for England at the World Cup… can Man United utilise him in a way they can expect to see the good side and bad side? If they do that and he stays… Rashford has got to expect that he isn't going to play every game."

Rashford still has two years remaining on his contract with United, having only penned a new deal in 2023. He reportedly earns around £325,000 per week at Old Trafford.

Sports.title: Eduardo Saverin's huge net worth as Facebook co-founder approached over Liverpool investment
Sports.content:
Eduardo Saverin's huge net worth as Facebook co-founder approached over Liverpool investment

The transfer window is normally focused on the players on the pitch, but a recent report has suggested there may be a change coming in Liverpool's ownership

View 3 Images Eduardo Saverin has reportedly been approached to invest in Liverpool FC (Image: Bloomberg via Getty Images)

Facebook co-founder Eduardo Saverin has been approached by a consortium looking to purchase a share in Liverpool. Saverin, 44, is understood to have a net worth of around £24.3billion.

‌



Were he to involve himself in investing in the club, he would become the third wealthiest owner/co-owner in the Premier League. Only Newcastle United's Saudi Arabian Public Investment Fund owners (£723.3bn) and Manchester City's 'City Football Group' bosses (£24.5bn) would boast a bigger net-worth than Saverin.

‌



In 2022, Saverin was part of a consortium which failed in an attempt to takeover Chelsea after Roman Abramovich was forced to sell the club.

‌



FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

His £24.3bn net worth, according to Bloomberg Billionaires Index, would be more than welcome by the consortium looking to purchase a stake in the club. It's understood the syndicate could look to become the second-largest shareholder at Anfield.

Amazon founder Jeff Bezos was also reported as another potential investor in the aforementioned consortium. At present, nothing has been decided in regards to Saverin being involved in the consortium.

‌



What is known is that it's currently being spearheaded by Amit Bhatia, the son-in-law of steel billionaire Lakshmi Mittal. The figure the consortium may look to purchase is understood to be around 30 per cent.

View 3 Images Eduardo Saverin has an enormous net worth (Image: Bloomberg via Getty Images)

Fenway Sports Group have been the majority stakeholders in Liverpool since 2010. A potential purchase could value the Reds at a whopping $6bn (£4.5bn) which would rank amongst the most lucrative deals in English football history.

‌



At present, Chelsea's takeover by the BlueCo consortium is the largest club purchase in English football history. When they won the bidding process at Stamford Bridge, the purported sale was worth around £4.25bn.

A spokesperson for FSG said last week: "An investment consortium led, managed, and represented by Amit Bhatia has expressed interest in making a strategic minority investment in Liverpool Football Club."

View 3 Images Jeff Bezos has also been approached over investing in Liverpool FC (Image: Anadolu, Anadolu via Getty Images)

‌



In 2023, Dynasty Equity purchased a small stake which valued Liverpool at $4.5bn. This came one year after the club said they were open to a full sale of the club, which was confirmed in a statement.

At the time, they said: "FSG has frequently received expressions of interest from third parties seeking to become shareholders in Liverpool. FSG has said before that under the right terms and conditions, we would consider new shareholders if it was in the best interests of Liverpool as a club."

Jadon Sancho has been without a club since letting his deal at Old Trafford expire but it appears that the former Manchester United might not be out of work for much longer

View 2 Images Jadon Sancho could be Qatar-bound (Image: Getty Images)

Jadon Sancho has been handed the chance to complete a sensational move to Qatar after receiving a contract offer from Al-Rayyan. The former £85m man has been without a club since leaving Manchester United at the end of his contract.

‌



Sancho, 26, has been on the lookout for fresh employment since then but with little luck. But it appears he has now been offered a fresh chance to relaunch his career in the Middle East.

‌



According to the French outlet Foot Mercato, Qatari side Al-Rayyan have offered him a deal to sign him on a free transfer. They want the English wideman to be the leading face of their project to dominate football within the country.

‌



It is not revealed whether Sancho is tempted by the move as it stands, but either way, he appears to be closing in on a new club. The winger has also been linked with a return to German side Borussia Dortmund; Sancho having enjoyed a productive spell in the Bundesliga ahead of his big-money switch to Old Trafford.

Free agent XI including Man Utd flop, Liverpool legend and current England star READ MORE :

Since then, Sancho has had loan spells with his former club, Chelsea and Aston Villa. He has had mixed success with his temporary employers, Chelsea having chosen not to sign him permanently despite agreeing an obligation to buy clause with United.

He scored just five goals at Stamford Bridge, while Sancho only got on the scoresheet once during his time at Villa Park.

‌



Speaking last season, Dortmund managing director Lars Ricken suggested that they were interested in signing Sancho a third time. "We are currently looking at a lot of players and analysing them," Ricken said.

Sports.title: Rising star Koivun holds off Scheffler to win on third PGA Tour start as a pro
Sports.content:
Jackson Koivun held off a charge from world No 1 Scottie Scheffler to win his first PGA Tour title in just his third start as a professional as he triumphed by three strokes at the 3M Open in Minnesota.

The 21-year-old's final-round, five-under 66 came after Scheffler - looking for his first title since the American Express back in January - applied the pressure with an eight-under 63 to post the clubhouse score at 22 under par.

Koivun had carved out a three-shot lead over Emiliano Grillo and Ben Kohles after round three following a stunning, bogeyless 10-under 61 that included two eagles and four birdies on an eight-under back nine.

Image: Scottie Scheffler's eight-under 63 came in vain on Sunday as he finished three shots adrift of Koivun

The youngster's Sunday was not as dramatic but he kept his cool to complete victory, securing the 3M Open scoring record of 25 under par in the process as he finished a blemish-free weekend with a par.

Koivun, who had made 10 starts as an amateur on the tour, turned professional after the US Open in June and missed the cut in his first event - the John Deere Classic - before finishing tied-10th at the Isco Championship.

He made 24 birdies, those two Saturday eagles and just three bogeys all week at TPC Twin Cities during a performance that hinted at an extremely bright future and also pushed him up 124 spots in the FedExCup standings to 70th, the final play-off berth with two regular events remaining.

Image: Koivun won his first PGA Tour title at the age of just 21

Koivun: Golf was love at first sight

He said afterwards: "I played a great round of golf. I definitely had some nerves coming down 18.

"I heard the crowd saying, 'Scottie's coming, Scottie's coming' but I just tried to blank that out and play the golf I knew I could. I was able to find some good putts down the stretch.

"I love this game, it's everything I do. It was love at first sight and I just want to say thanks to my parents for getting me into this and supporting me on my entire journey."

Image: Koivun made just three bogeys throughout the week, all in his second round

'Houdini chipper Koivun will make it to the top'

Sky Sports' Simon Holmes on Jackson Koivun:

"He is turbocharged and ready to perform immediately. He has presence in front of the camera and media. This guy is going to create a lot of fans.

"If you look at some of the talent th.at has come through that college system - Jordan Spieth, Collin Morikawa and Viktor Hovland - you'd say he is at least on a par with all of those players. But there is something in him that sets him apart from that group.

"Spieth had amazing putting but not a great driver. Morikawa, similar, amazing irons.

"With Koivun, you say driver, fantastic - he can play golf from the middle of the fairway. Iron control, amazing. Can he chip? Absolutely, he is a [Harry] Houdini.

"The best parts of his game are his putting and his mindset. He sees himself reaching the top of the pyramid - that is the outcome he expects.

"Let's see him make that journey. It's going to happen."

Sports.title: Craig Overton wins battle with brother Jamie in entertaining Hundred finish
Sports.content:
Craig Overton won his one-on-one battle with twin brother Jamie as Trent Rockets beat London Spirit by four wickets with two balls to spare in The Hundred.

Rockets needed 10 runs from the final five deliveries at Trent Bridge on Sunday night with Craig batting for the hosts and Jamie bowling for the visitors.

Craig (20no off six) earned bragging rights, and two points for his team, by top-edging Jamie for six over deep fine leg and then picking up successive twos to take Rockets to their target of 160, after Ben Duckett had spanked an excellent 75 off 47 balls up top.

Image: The Overton twins shake hands after Sunday evening's match at Trent Bridge

Craig Overton's six-two-two off his sibling had mirrored his efforts off Andrew Tye across the previous three deliveries with a maximum over long-on followed by a brace of two-run hauls, exploits that helped Rockets to a first win of 2026 and condemned Spirit to successive defeats.

Earlier in the game, Overton had caught and bowled Spirit opener Jonny Bairstow for a duck and also dismissed South African biffer Lhuan-dré Pretorius for 24.

Pretorius' compatriot Dewald Brevis top-scored with 39 from 24 balls in Spirit's 159-9, while captain Liam Livingstone contributed 33 off 24 deliveries.

Buttler blasts Super Giants to back-to-back wins

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Watch all of Jos Butler's sixes in Manchester Super Giants' win over Birmingham Phoenix

Elsewhere, Jos Buttler cracked 90 from 50 balls as Manchester Super Giants hammered Birmingham Phoenix by 87 runs to join Welsh Fire in winning their first two matches.

Buttler's knock at Emirates Old Trafford, which featured seven fours and five sixes and helped Super Giants post 187-5, was only 10 runs fewer than Phoenix managed as an entire team, with the visitors bundled out for 100 as Liam Dawson claimed 3-15.

The hosts backed up their narrow seven-run win over Spirit at Lord's on Thursday, while Phoenix slipped to a first loss having edged Rockets by 10 runs in a high-scoring clash at Edgbaston on Friday.

Image: Super Giants seamer Josh Tongue celebrates the wicket of Phoenix's Rehan Ahmed

Buttler was supported by Tom Moores' 39 not out off 17, which included five maximums, but Phoenix's batting never got going with skipper Donovan Ferreria (23) top-scoring.

England pacer Josh Tongue struck twice in two balls to rock Phoenix early, inflicting a golden duck on Rehan Ahmed, and the Midlanders never really recovered.

England quick Sonny Baker and Afghanistan spinner Noor Ahmad also bagged two wickets for Super Giants, who look to have an excellent all-round attack.

What is happening in The Hundred on Monday?

After the four-games-a-day set-up at the weekend, Monday sees a return to a single double-header with Southern Brave's women's side hosting MI London from 3pm before the men's sides square off from 6.30pm. Catch both fixtures live on Sky Sports.

Sports.title: In-form Herbert breaks LIV Golf record with win in UK
Sports.content:
Australia's Lucas Herbert followed an impressive showing at last week's Open at Royal Birkdale with a record-setting victory at the LIV Golf UK event in Staffordshire.

Herbert, who finished tied for sixth in the final men's major of the year, four shots adrift of champion Ryan Fox, romped to the LIV trophy in Rocester with a score of 30 under par.

That was the lowest winning score since the circuit was established in 2022 and left the 30-year-old six strokes clear of Tyrrell Hatton and nine in front of Bryson DeChambeau.

Image: Herbert's win was his second on LIV in 2026, after May's event in Virginia

Herbert also set the LIV record for most birdies in a tournament (30) and most combined birdies and eagles (32) after a 10-under, blemish-free 62 on Sunday.

He had begun the event with an 11-under 61 that contained 10 birdies and an eagle and his worst round all week was a three-under 69 on Saturday.

Herbert shot an eight-under 62 in the second round of the Open earlier this month and said after his victory at Rocester, his second of the LIV season after triumphing in Virginia in May: "I just wanted to carry that into this week the best I could.

"It was good to play like that today when I was being pushed by two of the best players in the world."

Hatton carded a nine under 63 on Sunday and said: "I wanted to get off to a fast start, which I did, but unfortunately Lucas did as well.

"It would have been amazing to win in front of home fans, but I tried my best. Lucas was incredible this week."

Sports.title: Mayo win first All-Ireland title in 75 years as 'curse lifted'
Sports.content:
Mayo claimed a first All-Ireland Senior Football title for 75 years as they beat defending champions Kerry in a thrilling final at Croke Park.

Mayo had lost 11 finals in a row, two of which went to a replay, since their last title in 1951 but secured a 1-20 to 1-17 triumph in emotional scenes on Sunday.

Manager Andy Moran - who lost six finals in a row during his playing days with Mayo - guided the club to silverware in his first season in charge.

Captain Jack Coyne told the BBC after Mayo's fourth title overall: "This is the stuff of dreams. To every Mayo boy or girl around the world, dream big things.

"Everything is possible and we showed that today. The saying is keep the faith. We kept the faith. We're All-Ireland champions."

Legend has it that a curse was placed on Mayo back in 1951 when their homecoming celebrations after winning the title disrupted a funeral.

The priest reportedly said the club would not win another All-Ireland trophy while any member of the team was still alive.

Sports.title: Have we seen the last of Greaves on Women's Series? 'I'm focused on my Tour Card'
Sports.content:
Have we seen the last of Beau Greaves on the PDC Women’s Series? 'Beau 'n Arrow' admits she felt "deflated" and felt "everybody wanted me to lose" after the 2025 edition.

Greaves claimed her third Women's World Matchplay title in four years as she edged out Fallon Sherrock 6-5 in a thrilling final in Blackpool.

The Doncaster arrowsmith kicked off her title bid with an assured 5-1 triumph over Finnish star Kirsi Viinikainen before surviving a scare against Gemma Hayter.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the Women's World Matchplay final between Beau Greaves and Fallon Sherrock in Blackpool

Women's World Matchplay | Roll of Honour

2022: Fallon Sherrock



2023: Beau Greaves



2024: Beau Greaves



2025: Lisa Ashton



2026: Beau Greaves



Greaves set up a winner-takes-all clash with Sherrock in the final with 'The Queen of the Palace' taking back-to-back legs to level at 5-5 and force a decider.

They shared maximums but Greaves came out on top with a checkout of 56 to secure the crown.

Greaves has won a record 57 PDC Women's Series titles and discussing her future, the 22-year-old spoke about the difficulty of spinning between the men's and women's game.

"It's tough really," she said. "I think I've tried to just focus on the men's side, on my Tour Card. I think after the last Women's Series, I felt a bit deflated after it.

"I didn't really enjoy it too much. I just felt a bit like everybody wanted me to lose, so coming out of there I was like 'maybe I should just focus on playing better darts and more competitive darts and my ranking', just give me something to work towards.

"I think in the ladies game gets a bit stale for everybody because you're working towards this target and once you're there, there's nothing else to go towards.

"After the last one I was just thinking, 'I think now I'll concentrate on the Pro Tour and the Euro Tour that I've qualified for', just try and do that.

"I still love that side of the game, but now I think my main goal is the men's side and enjoy that part of it and the challenges that come with it."

Greaves' latest glory is only just the start with the World Youth finalist admitting she has got to focus on improving her stage game.

"I play darts for enjoyment but now it's my job, but I love the game. I cannot get enough of it, and to be able to support the ladies' game is a massive thing," said Greaves, who became the first woman to win a PDC ranking title with a historic 8-7 victory over Michael Smith in the Players Championship 11 final.

"I want to play even better. I win tournaments on the floor, but I think my stage game has got to improve and I know that."

'I'm really enjoying the challenge'

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Greaves made a blistering start to the Women's World Matchplay as she took out consecutive finishes of 148 and 144

Greaves' victory on the Winter Gardens stage also secured her place in the 2026 Mr Vegas Grand Slam of Darts and the 2027 Paddy Power World Darts Championship, after having featured in both tournaments last year.

"Obviously winning a Pro Tour really put me in the rankings. I've done well, quarter-finals, semi-finals, but it's tough," said Greaves.

"I think I'm really enjoying the challenge just to get there, to qualify for them and yeah, it'll be an achievement for me just to play there and just to say I have done it.

"I want to win, I want to do well, I need to work harder, I want to play better. I know I've got a long way to go before I'm really, really competitive with the men.

"I know I can do it, I just have to work harder for it and just put my mind to it, just believe in myself more than anything. I think sometimes I just doubt myself too much and it gets in the way of stuff.

"I enjoy the Pro Tour, the Euro Tour coming up, I look forward to them and it's tough, but it's good."

Beau Greaves | PDC Honours:

3x 🏆 Women's World Matchplay (2023, 24, 26)



1x 🏆 Players Championship (2026)



2x 🏆 Challenge Tour (2025)



4x 🏆 Development Tour (2024-25)



57x 🏆 Women's Series (2022-26)



Reminder: She is still just 22!



'I can beat anybody'

Image: Greaves stormed to a record-extending third Women’s World Matchplay title

Greaves also sent out a warning to her rivals, saying she "never surprises herself" and she can "beat anybody" on her day.

"I think with me, it's just when and where it's going to turn up and that's something that is not a very good point in my game is that I am still very inconsistent, but I can be very consistent. It's just one of those things," said Greaves, who made more history on the PDC Pro Tour after qualifying for both the Hungarian Darts Trophy and Czech Darts Open.

"I know I can do it, I think sometimes I just get very happy in my own life and sometimes I forget that I need to do better, keep winning, keep doing that to prove to get up the rankings. I get very settled and that's my problem really."

"I will definitely take the positives," insisted Sherrock, who fell short in a last-leg decider in the showpiece for the second consecutive year.

"If somebody had said to me I'd get to the final, I'd have bitten their hand off.

"Beau deserved to win. She was the better player, so full credit to her.

"Hopefully this kickstarts my season. My main aim is to get to the World Championship, so if I can regroup my game, you never know, I might go on a run again."

Sports.title: McLaren defend Hungarian GP strategy calls after Piastri radio rant
Sports.content:
McLaren boss Andrea Stella has defended the strategy calls the team made during the Hungarian Grand Prix after Oscar Piastri was initially critical as he lost out to team-mate Lando Norris.

Piastri started third but overtook Ferrari's Charles Leclerc and pole-sitter Norris in the opening corners to take the lead at the end of the first lap.

McLaren attempted to give the Australian, as their lead driver on track, strategic priority, but pressure coming from Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton at the second round of pit stops forced their hand.

Piastri came in to ensure he retained track position over Hamilton but then lost his advantage over Norris due to a combination of the Brit's superior pace and an unfortunate incident that saw him make contact with the Williams of backmarker Carlos Sainz.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from the 2026 Hungarian Grand Prix

Immediately after the Sainz collision, for which the Spaniard was penalised, Piastri expressed his frustration over the radio, before then having a further dig at his team once Norris had stopped and come out on track ahead of him.

Stella said: "If you look at the race trace, you will see that when Hamilton pits, he is in condition to undercut the two McLarens, so we needed to respond.

"Because if that was the right way to take the cars to victory, we needed to have a McLaren in a position of leading that way ahead of Hamilton.

"So, it was either Oscar or Lando. Oscar was in the lead, and we thought that he was the right car to stop for that. And then for Lando, this opened up a different strategy.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Watch Oscar Piastri take the lead from Lando Norris as George Russell has a race start to forget at Hungaroring in Budapest

"So, it's not like you are deviating because you are thinking about Oscar and Lando. You are deviating because we needed to avoid that the Ferrari could take the lead of the race.

"I think then what follows has to do with the pace difference because Lando on used tyres was not much slower than the cars on new tyres. And it's there that he gained the victory today.

"So, I think it's a victory on pace, and Lando had the opportunity to use it, but not because the team kind of wanted to create it. The team needed to cover Hamilton."

Piastri: I was upset in the moment but pit stop timing was fine

Piastri, whose race came to an early end as a result of a gearbox failure when he was running in second, would later accept that the timing of McLaren's stops was fair, and that his request for them to delay Norris' stop after his own collision with Sainz was not "reasonable".

Piastri told Sky Sports F1: "I was crashed into by Carlos and, in the moment, I was hoping maybe they would not pit Lando because of that incident to at least give me the chance to stay in the lead but I think that's not very reasonable.

"I was just more very upset in the moment about what had happened. I think the timing of my pit stop was fine, we wanted to beat Lewis and that's what we needed to do to."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Oscar Piastri reacts to his disastrous day at the Hungarian GP as he was forced to retire when running in second due to a gearbox issue

Before Piastri was left frustrated, it had been Norris applying pressure to the McLaren pit wall as he repeatedly told them he was faster than his team-mate and urged them to let him make a stop first.

Stella explained why he felt McLaren had been correct in rejecting Norris' requests, as well as in making the decision that resulted in their drivers swapping positions.

"When you are at the pit wall, you obviously constantly evaluate all the options," he said. "And you look at that from different angles. You look at that from making sure that you can achieve a victory in a race like that.

"You can look at what's the way to score as many points for the team. But there's also a way, which is being consistent with the way we go racing.

"And I think up until the time Oscar pitted, Oscar had gained the lead in a fair manner in corner one, with the action in corner one and two, so he deserved an opportunity to try and win the race.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Oscar Piastri has a technical failure and stops out on track

"In other tracks, probably, Lando might have overtaken Oscar. But in this case, it's difficult, you need a large pace advantage here to be able to do so.

"So, we were happy to give Oscar the opportunity to fight for the win. And then, at the same time, making sure that we were protecting the way we go racing. So, that's the approach we adopted. Obviously, it's always quite marginal. There's many options that you can consider.

"But I think today was a well-executed race from a racing principles point of view. And I have to thank Oscar and Lando, because it would not be possible to do so without two drivers that accept and support our way of going racing."

Piastri: Sainz should look in the mirror

Despite withdrawing his criticism of his own team, Piastri remained unhappy with Sainz for causing their collision.

After criticising the Spaniard in an expletive-filled radio rant moments after the collision, Piastri later told reporters: "I knew there were blue flags, but there were blue flags on all the marshal signals, I was right behind him for a sector.

"I couldn't believe what happened. Getting crashed into by a lapped car is never one of the things you expect that can go wrong in your race, and today it was, so I don't really care if he didn't see me.

"The fact that he didn't and no one told him, or there was a lack of complete awareness, is unacceptable."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Watch the moment that Lando Norris claims victory at the Hungarian Grand Prix!

Sainz largely defended himself after the race, claiming issues with blue-flag signals and that he had been fighting Aston Martin's Fernando Alonso for position combined to make a "good excuse" for the incident.

Sainz also questioned whether Piastri could have been a bit more cautious given the high stakes of competing for a race win.

Piastri was unimpressed when told of Sainz's comments, responding: "He's quite critical of others, and others have given him some stick before for being frustrating on-track.

"When you go and do something like that, maybe you should look in the mirror a bit."

Sports.title: Kelly wins Senior Open as Gallacher lights up final round at Gleneagles
Sports.content:
Jerry Kelly won the ISPS HANDA Senior Open at Gleneagles by two shots as he claimed a third PGA Tour Champions major of his career.

Kelly, who has twice triumphed at the Senior Players Championship, made birdie at his final hole on Sunday after escaping from a greenside bunker to finish on 10 under.

The 59-year-old shot a final-round two-under 68 in Perthshire with his gain at 18 following three birdies on his front nine and bogeys at six and 11.

Kelly, whose win earns him a spot at next year's 155th Open at St Andrews, said: "The senior Claret Jug is the trophy that I've wanted as an over-50 golfer more than any other.

"To do it in Scotland at the home of golf and to actually win and get into the home of golf at St Andrews, I mean, I'm absolutely speechless."

Sports.title: Sivo injury mars Leeds' win over Bradford as hopes of try record dented
Sports.content:
Maika Sivo's suspected broken arm marred Leeds Rhinos' 42-12 victory over Bradford Bulls that took them two points clear at the top of Super League with the Fijian winger's hopes of breaking the record for the most tries in a season dented.

Rhinos coach Brad Arthur said afterwards that the 32-year-old's forearm will need plating and the former Parramatta Eels star is likely to be sidelined for around six weeks.

Sivo is currently on 29 tries for the Super League campaign with the record number of touchdowns in one season the 40 amassed by Castleford's Denny Solomona in 2016.

Sivo, who is expected back before the end of the regular season, suffered his injury making a tackle during Leeds' seven-try victory at Headingley on Sunday.

Image: Leeds' Maika Sivo has scored 29 Super League tries this season and is hunting Denny Solomona's record of 40

James McDonnell scored twice on his 100th Super League appearance for Rhinos, while Jarrod O'Connor, Tom Holroyd, Brodie Croft, Cooper Jenkins and Kallum Watkins bagged one each as Leeds bounced back from last week's 36-34 defeat to Castleford.

Bradford, who tumbled to a sixth loss in seven top-fight matches, went ahead when Guy Armitage did superbly to score from a Chris Atkin kick but Leeds hit back through McDonnell, despite the enormous blow of losing Sivo.

Jake Connor had an effort ruled out for a double movement but he created a second for McDonnell and O'Connor extended Leeds' advantage to 18-6 at half-time.
