Sports.title: Lucky Lando Norris WINS the Hungarian Grand Prix after team-mate Oscar Piastri's spectacular capitulation - while Kimi Antonelli gains the upper hand on title rivals Lewis Hamilton and George Russell
Sports.content:
Lucky Lando Norris WINS the Hungarian Grand Prix after team-mate Oscar Piastri's spectacular capitulation - while Kimi Antonelli gains the upper hand on title rivals Lewis Hamilton and George Russell

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Lucky, lucky, Lando. Not that world champion Norris was other than often the fastest hound in the Hungarian Grand Prix and should have won it on his own.

But he was helped, first, by a bizarre incident befalling his McLaren team-mate Oscar Piastri handing him the victory chance his pole position deserved and his poor opening lap, sorry, did not.

This first of two pivotal moments in Norris’s triumph came on lap 38 when Piastri, who had pitted for a second time, was trying to make progress back into the lead. Williams’ Carlos Sainz – the villain of the piece – was fighting with Fernando Alonso for 15th and in his path.

Distracted by his skirmish, Sainz was oblivious of Piastri poised to lap him. It was blue-flag time. The Spaniard should have yielded. He did not.

Piastri fumed: ‘Get out of the f***ing way, you idiot.’ They banged tyres. ‘Oh, my God!’

Lando Norris returned to the top step of the podium with a dominant win in Hungary

The British driver was stunned by team-mate Oscar Piastri but wrestled back control

All this confusion was delaying Piastri, obviously, while Norris was making hay out where the sun shone. After Norris was called in at the end of the following lap, he emerged in front of the other papaya car. Job done.

Piastri was furious. Obviously with Sainz. But also, it seemed, with his McLaren team for granting Norris freedom to open up an advantage for seven laps after his own stop.

Piastri’s race engineer Tom Stallard came on the radio, to pacify him, saying: ‘Oscar, it’s Sainz that cost us. Target is to get to the end on these tyres.’

Piastri rejoined: ‘Oh, mate, just don’t talk to me now.

‘Nice of you guys to factor that one (the traffic) in by the way, thanks.’

If he believes the team pull for Norris, their hand-reared champion, rather than him, this reverse would hardly have put his mind to rest.

The second and final slice of luck working for Norris came as Piastri, who seemed set to finish second, conked out with a gearbox problem, his race over on lap 56 of 70.

Thus, without any concerns at all, Norris went on to claim the first win of his title defence, indeed since the Sao Paulo Grand Prix last November.

Now more drama ensued as a virtual safety car was enlisted. Lewis Hamilton, on a unravelling weekend for him given what riches it promised, had succeeded the stricken Piastri in the running order.

This was not to last. Norris came in for new tyres and so did Hamilton. For Norris, fine, back out in top spot. But Hamilton emerged from the pits virtually level with third-placed Kimi Antonelli, and, although the seven-time world champion pushed himself ahead of the Italian into and out of the first corner, it was not legit.

Was he speeding in the pits? He was placed under investigation for the suspected offence and handed a five-second penalty a few minutes later. ‘They are handing out penalties like crazy,’ said Hamilton, though he later relented in his criticism of the beak.

He had already been told by his pit wall to hand the place back to Antonelli, but that is not quite how it stayed: yes, Norris took the flag first, Max Verstappen second (because he did not stop under the VSC) and Antonelli third. But Hamilton’s penalty dropped him below team-mate Charles Leclerc and into fifth place.

What a headache for Hamilton, who had started where he was condemned to finish after being demoted three places on Saturday for inadvertently blocking Piastri in qualifying. Instead of clipping Antonelli’s championship lead by six points, as he was due to do prior to the Australian’s retirement, he fell five points back. He is 50 behind Antonelli heading into the sport’s summer holidays.

A thought: why didn’t Ferrari slow down Leclerc? Do they not want to win the drivers’ title?

George Russell, seventh on the day, is now 59 adrift, nine points down on his starting position. Not great for the Briton, but not the worst outcome given how he watched the field fly by him at the start as anti-stall kicked in on his Mercedes. He went down to 19th at the end of lap one, but, helped by a new engine fitted after qualifying, came through the midfield.

‘I am past the point of disappointment now,’ said Russell, with a resigned smile. ‘If I continue to be disappointed with everything that goes on, I’ll be disappointed every day of the week.

‘My pace was as strong as anyone out there, and I haven’t been there for the past two or three races, so I will take the positives there. But it is unbelievable the list of things that have gone wrong this season.

Norris benefited from Oscar Piastri's spectacular capitulation on Sunday afternoon

Lewis Hamilton fell further back in the championship race to Kimi Antonelli

‘I was on the throttle holding the revs, and four seconds before the lights went out the engines started revving all over the place – the engine wasn’t reacting to the throttle. It is a brand new engine. No idea.’

There was little overtaking to savour, though Verstappen made a brilliant pass on Hamilton at the first corner – named after his (Verstappen’s) de facto father-in-law Nelson Piquet. He caught the Briton by surprise, a typical Max mugging.

Piastri did not need to exert such virtuosity as an old Norris habit came back to haunt him, namely his weakness on first laps that has repeatedly cost him wins from promising starting positions, especially in 2024 when he had an outside chance of claiming the title a year before he did.

Norris was very smartly away from pole and took the first corner in command. But he drifted wide at the second bend, named after Hamilton, and Piastri assumed the lead.

Norris possessed more pace than his team-mate and harried him, but Piastri held track position until his afternoon unknotted itself. Norris finally streaked away, finishing 15 seconds up the road and out of sight, a smile back on the champion’s face after a welcome victory of persistence and pace as well as good fortune.

Sports.title: Chelsea ready to demand major fee for Pedro Neto amid Liverpool and Man City interest - as former boss Enzo Maresca eyes reunion
Sports.content:
Chelsea are not surprised by the reported interest in Pedro Neto, though would not allow their winger to leave on the cheap after noting the rising valuations of other wide men in this window.

The Premier League club are not actively touting their Portuguese 26-year-old for sale, but Blues insiders are aware of the asking prices being issued elsewhere in Europe, and specifically for RB Leipzig’s Yan Diomande and Paris Saint-Germain's Bradley Barcola.

Diomande and Barcola are both considered £100million-plus players by their respective clubs, and while Neto would struggle to fetch such a large fee, it does give Chelsea an idea of their own wide man’s worth. The Blues have not quoted a valuation on Neto as of yet.

Manchester City and Liverpool, along with sides in Saudi Arabia, have been linked with Neto.

Chelsea sources believe it is only natural that Neto has attracted interest because of a lack of top wingers in the current market.

City are also now managed by Enzo Maresca, who favoured Neto as his right winger while in charge at Stamford Bridge.

Chelsea are not surprised at interest in Pedro Neto but will not allow him to leave on the cheap

New Man City boss Enzo Maresca favoured Neto on the right wing while in charge of Chelsea

Join the discussion Should Chelsea cash in on Pedro Neto or hold out for a massive transfer fee amid rising winger prices?

Neto is not currently on Chelsea’s tour, which has started in Sydney, Australia, as he is still having downtime after representing Portugal at the World Cup.

Chelsea’s other Portuguese right winger, Geovany Quenda, is due to join up with his team-mates after the Australian leg of this tour as they move on to Asia.

Quenda, 19, picked up a ‘small injury’, per sources close to the player. Chelsea's new striker from Strasbourg, Emmanuel Emegha, will return to training at a later date after suffering a hamstring issue during their behind-closed-doors friendly win over Bromley.

As revealed by Daily Mail Sport, Chelsea beat Bromley 3-0 and also Crawley 3-1 in secret training matches at Cobham, with Emegha scoring in both games.

Sports.title: Chelsea sent strong transfer warning by Premier League boss after failed bid
Sports.content:
Chelsea sent strong transfer warning by Premier League boss after failed bid

Sunderland rejected an £8million bid from Chelsea earlier this summer for Granit Xhaka and Black Cats boss Regis Le Bris has now offered an update on the midfielder's future

View 2 Images Xabi Alonso is overseeing his first transfer window as Chelsea boss (Image: Getty Images)

Sunderland boss Regis Le Bris has confirmed Granit Xhaka will be going nowhere, weeks after turning down a move to Chelsea. The former Arsenal man was considering a sensational swithc Stamford Bridge earlier this summer.

‌



Chelsea manager Xabi Alonso was also keen on a deal that would have seen him reunited with the former Bayer Leverkusen star. But an agreement could not be found between the two clubs and Le Bris has announced that there is no chance of a revival in talks.

‌



Asked about Xhaka’s future after his side’s pre-season defeat to Liverpool, the Frenchman said: “No, this topic is closed.

‌



“He has been really clear about his future. He loves Sunderland, he wants to stay in Sunderland. He wants to make the future of Sunderland. He is a good captain. A great leader.”

Free agent XI including Man Utd flop, Liverpool legend and current England star READ MORE :

Le Bris’ comments come just weeks after Xhaka appeared to perform a U-turn about his future. Speaking during the World Cup, the Swiss midfielder said: "That's not my job [to talk about a potential move to Chelsea]. I have my management for that. I want to concentrate fully on the World Cup."

But just shortly after, he committed his future to the Black Cats. Xhaka said: "Sunderland has been my home since day one. We are all very happy. I've decided to stay where I am; the most important thing is family. I'm ready to make history with them."

‌



Xhaka, 33, only joined Sunderland last summer from Leverkusen, having helped the German side to the Bundesliga title. It also signalled his first return to the Premier League following a rollercoaster spell with Arsenal.

View 2 Images Granit Xhaka was the subject of a bid from Chelsea (Image: Getty Images)

Xhaka made 36 appearances and scored one goal for Sunderland across what was an impressive debut campaign at the Stadium of Light. His performances helped the club secure a spot in the Europa League for the forthcoming season.

‌



Sunderland’s summer window has been relatively low-key this term, having only signed Thomas Meunier on a free transfer. Asked if fans could expect any more business, Le Bris added: “It’s going to be quiet.

“Under the radar, right? Because I think we are working hard behind the scenes, and it's really important to be quiet because otherwise, it's a mess.

“And we are looking at probably a different transfer window if you compare with last season. We had to sign 14 new players. That won't be the case this year. We'll see what will happen.”

Sports.title: Federico Chiesa confirms Liverpool future stance and reveals new role under Andoni Iraola
Sports.content:
Federico Chiesa confirms Liverpool future stance and reveals new role under Andoni Iraola

Federico Chiesa was tipped for the exit door under Arne Slot, but Andoni Iraola's appointment marks a fresh start for the Liverpool forward, who's being used in a new position in pre-season

View 2 Images Federico Chiesa wants to earn the trust of Andoni Iraola (Image: Andrew J. Clark/ISI Photos/ISI Photos via Getty Images)

Liverpool star Federico Chiesa says that he isn't thinking about a transfer and has revealed that new manager Andoni Iraola wants him to play as a striker. Chiesa, 28, has only started two Premier League games since his £10million move from Juventus in 2024 and has frequently been linked with a move away.

‌



The forward wasn't trusted by former boss Arne Slot, who was sacked in May following a disappointing season, and wants to put a marker down in pre-season under Iraola. Chiesa got off to a good start by scoring in Liverpool's 4-2 victory over Sunderland in Nashville, and he helped set up another.

‌



Post-match, the Italian made it clear that wants to make a success of his career with Liverpool after a frustrating first couple of years, adding that he's set to play centrally under Iraola rather than on the wing. "Right now, at the moment, I am happy here at Liverpool," Chiesa affirmed.

‌



"I love the club, I love the fans, I love everything. I am doing the best I can to have a chance here. And then we will see. At the minute, the only thing I am thinking about is Liverpool. I don't know, it is difficult to say [if this is a fresh start].

FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Liverpool sent strong Michael Olise transfer warning by Bayern Munich chief READ MORE :

"It is always a fresh start at the beginning of the year. Maybe there have been too many fresh starts. But I don't care, I am trying to do my best for this new manager. Last season under Arne Slot, I was trying to do my best.

‌



"Last year I felt ready for a bigger role, then it depended on the coach whether he wanted me to play or not. Of course, I wanted to play more but it is what it is. The gaffer decided to do so, he had his game plans, he took his decisions, I have nothing to say about that. It is football.

"This year, let us say it is a new chapter. There is a new manager and I have to focus on that. He put me striker today and he wants me there. The only conversations I've had [with Iraola] were about pressing and tactics."

Should Liverpool sell Federico Chiesa? Have your say in the comments section.

‌



View 2 Images Federico Chiesa played - and scored - as a striker against Sunderland (Image: Andrew J. Clark/ISI Photos/ISI Photos via Getty Images)

Chiesa feels a responsibility to make amends for Liverpool's 'lucky' fifth-place finish last season, as the Reds narrowly qualified for the Champions League on the final day. "Liverpool deserves more," the 28-year-old declared.

"Two years ago, we were Premier League champions. Last year, we almost went out of the Champions League spots. We were battling for fifth, which was enough at the time but as we know usually only four go in. We were lucky."

Sports.title: Wantaway Tottenham star emerges on Arsenal and Chelsea radar in transfer twist
Sports.content:
Wantaway Tottenham star emerges on Arsenal and Chelsea radar in transfer twist

Rarely do Premier League rivals look to do transfer business with each other, but it's been claimed Chelsea and Arsenal are eying one of Tottenham's biggest stars

View 3 Images Xabi Alonso and Mikel Arteta's clubs may battle each other for one Tottenham star (Image: David Price, Arsenal FC via Getty Images)

Tottenham Hotspur captain Cristian Romero is on Arsenal and Chelsea's transfer radar. This claim has been made by Italian media, after Romero was reportedly offered to Inter Milan.

‌



The 28-year-old is expected to depart this summer, after finding himself in the firing line of Spurs fans toward the end of the season. His decision to fly back to Argentina for medical treatment on a knee injury did not go down well with the north Londoners' fans, particularly when it was claimed he would be absent for their win or relegation final Premier League clash against Everton.

‌



Thinking better of the situation, Romero did fly back to see his team-mates save their skin against the Toffees, but after Spurs brought in Jan Paul van Hecke and Marco Senesi his future is looking uncertain.

‌



While Inter emerged as early contenders for his signature, Italian outlets understand they may have to battle Chelsea and Arsenal to sign him.

FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Corriere dello Sport claims that both Mikel Arteta and Xabi Alonso's sides are among those vying for the former Atalanta defender. The Gunners are actively seeking reinforcements at centre-back, with William Saliba set to miss a significant chunk of the season after undergoing back surgery.

‌



Meanwhile, Chelsea are poised to confirm the capture of Crystal Palace defender Maxence Lacroix, yet are also thought to be pursuing an additional centre-half. Free agent John Stones, who departed Manchester City at the end of last season, has similarly been linked with both clubs.

View 3 Images Cristian Romero found himself on the wrong side of Tottenham fans towards the end of last season (Image: Alex Pantling, Getty Images)

It would be an intriguing development if either Arsenal or Chelsea secured a deal for Romero. Mundo Deportivo have suggested that Spurs are seeking approximately £25.9m despite previously placing his value at around £60.3m.

‌



Atletico Madrid and Barcelona have also been linked with interest in Romero this summer. Spurs rejected an approach from the former last season when they made enquiries about his availability.

View 3 Images Cristian Romero is being chased by Inter Milan (Image: George Wood, Getty Images)

Despite his change of heart, Romero's future at the club still appears destined to conclude this summer, one way or another. Inter sporting director Piero Ausilo also virtually confirmed they are keen on signing him.

Sports.title: Michael Carrick meets Ole Gunnar Solskjaer after beating Man Utd legend to manager's job
Sports.content:
Michael Carrick meets Ole Gunnar Solskjaer after beating Man Utd legend to manager's job

Michael Carrick is currently in the midst of preparations for his first full season as Manchester United boss and has been reunited with another former Red Devils manager

View 2 Images Michael Carrick served as Ole Gunnar Solskjaer's assistant at Old Trafford (Image: Getty Images)

Michael Carrick was reunited with Ole Gunnar Solksjaer in Norway this week, just months after beating him to the manager’s job at Old Trafford. The Premier League side have been in Norway over the past few days as part of their pre-season preparations.

‌



The Red Devils took on Rosenborg on Friday and secured a 5-0 success, with Shea Lacey, Joshua Zirkzee, Jacob Devaney, Harry Amass and Ethan Williams all finding the net.

‌



Away from taking on the Norwegians, United boss Carrick also had more on his mind. As per the Manchester Evening News, he met up with former head coach Solskjaer.

‌



The pair are thought to have a close relationship, despite Carrick having beaten the former forward to the top job at Old Trafford last season. It was suggested that Solskjaer was in talks regarding a second stint in charge.

But Red Devils chiefs opted for Carrick instead and he was handed the job on a permanent basis after 12 wins from 17 games - form that was good enough to see United seal a spot back in the Champions League.

Free agent XI including Man Utd flop, Liverpool legend and current England star READ MORE :

Carrick’s reunion with Solskjaer comes after he admitted that he had sought after advice from the Norwegian ahead of officially taking the reins at Old Trafford.

‌



Speaking earlier this year, he said: “Yeah, yeah I’ve spoken to him. We’re close, we’ve been through a lot together. He’s been fully supportive, as you’d expect. He’s some man, I respect him an awful lot. He wished us all the best, and he was happy that we got the right result.

“I think, friendships, you have conversations… I’ve got a lot of friends in places that I can pick on if I need to. I’m not that one that bothers a lot of people to be honest, but… He’s certainly there if ever I need.”

Speaking after United’s emphatic victory against Rosenborg, Carrick said: “Clean sheet, scoring goals, and everyone, by the looks of it, coming through injury-free is what you want at this stage, really.

‌



View 2 Images Michael Carrick has met with Ole Gunnar Solskjaer during United's time in Norway (Image: Getty Images)

“As much as we want everything to improve and performances to be better all the time, I think keeping players fit and progressing through pre-season is as important as anything.

“So, two games in, two weeks in, I think we can take where we are and we’re pretty happy. The second half, the younger players coming on, I thought they were fantastic. They played as a team really well and deserve what they got second half.”

‌



He added: “It’s important to build through this pre-season, some players need more minutes than others as they go and we’re managing some players a little bit more than others. I've said it before the game, it's never going to be perfect, two weeks in and you're kind of building towards that.

“So, I thought there was a lot of good things, some of the goals were fantastic goals and it’s just as pleasing to keep a clean sheet. So yeah, we’re moving forward nicely.”

Sports.title: Tyson Fury's X-rated two-word response to Anthony Joshua with fight on
Sports.content:
Tyson Fury's X-rated two-word response to Anthony Joshua with fight on

After Anthony Joshua came close to losing his must win fight against Kristian Prenga, Tyson Fury only had two words for the bout

View 2 Images Tyson Fury has made his thoughts onrival Anthony Joshua's recent performance clear (Image: YouTube/Boxing King Media)

Tyson Fury only had two words after seeing Kristian Prenga deal Anthony Joshua one of the biggest scares of his career - "Wow, wtf?"

‌



Fury commented those words on social media after Ring Magazine chief and Zuffa boxing co-founder Turki Alalshikh uploaded a highlights package of Joshua's win over Prenga. The Albanian scored two huge knockdowns over AJ in the first round, the biggest of which coming in the opening exchanges.

‌



Prenga stepped inside Joshua and caught him with a perfect uppercut which sent the two-time unified heavyweight champion tumbling to the canvas, before catching him with another huge shot later in the round. However, Joshua got his bearings and knocked the 35-year-old out in round two with a vicious combination.

‌



JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! All the best sports news and much more on our dedicated Facebook page

Oleksandr Usyk, whose team has been training Joshua since December, breathed a huge sigh of relief after Joshua's victory was confirmed. Meanwhile, Fury only let his thoughts be known on Instagram by commenting "Wow, wtf?" on the video on Alalshikh's post.

At present, that's the Gypsy King's only comment on Joshua's brush with disaster against Prenga. The Olympic gold medallist needed to be victorious to ensure the blockbuster clash with Fury would take place.

‌



The night before, Fury held up his end of the bargain by easily stopping Mariusz Wach in their non-televised clash in Pattaya, Thailand. The 46-year-old Pole gave up on his stool at the end of the seventh round after his team decided he had taken enough punishment from Fury.

Content cannot be displayed without consent

The boxing world held its breath in anticipation for Fury to turn up ringside in Jeddah to confront Joshua. The latter also instantly looked for Fury in the arena straight after beating him, only for him not to be there.

‌



Channelling his inner Mike Tyson, Joshua took the microphone and said: "Wait a minute - have we got Tyson Fury in the room? Wait, wait, wait, to more important matters - is he here or not? Fair do’s.

"Im'ma rip his heart out. I'm the meanest and vicious champion's ever been. Listen, all jokes aside, you see, there’s two sides of this thing. One is fire. You have to have that vim, that grrr. But also respect.

View 2 Images Joshua was knocked down twice in the first round (Image: Matchroom Boxing/Getty Images)

‌



"I respect everything he has done. And everything that he has achieved. As someone who who has been calling for the fight for a long time, we're here now. Shout out to his Excellency. Shout to Eddie Hearn for making these opportunities possible, and I hope the fans will be in for a lovely treat.”

Joshua's promoter Hearn has insisted all of the contracts have been signed, but a date or location is yet to be confirmed. UK boxing fans have been hoping for the clash to be in London, but Madison Square Garden in New York has also emerged as a potential venue.

Arsenal are reportedly set to hold further talks with Newcastle United over a deal to sign Bruno Guimaraes

Arsenal are reportedly about to move a step closer to securing the signing of Newcastle United star Bruno Guimaraes. The Brazil international has been heavily linked with a move away from St James’ Park, with the Gunners mentioned as the most likely destination.

‌



The 28-year-old remains under contract at Newcastle until the summer of 2028, and there has been speculation for several weeks that Arsenal could make an official bid to try and bring Guimaraes to the Emirates Stadium.

‌



Midfield has been an area of the squad that Arsenal are looking to bring in reinforcements this summer, and now there has been a fresh update on their pursuit of Guimaraes.

‌



Transfer specialist Fabrizio Romano has revealed that Arsenal are expected to make an offer exceeding £70million in an attempt to sign Guimaraes in the coming weeks.

Arsenal learn fee and transfer conditions to sign Vinicius Jr from Real Madrid READ MORE :

The report suggests that the Gunners will conduct further negotiations with Newcastle regarding a prospective agreement for the Brazilian within the next few days, with Arsenal already understood to have reached personal terms with the player.

It has additionally been stated that the resolution surrounding whether or not Guimaraes becomes an Arsenal player will hinge on whether or not Newcastle will approve a departure, alongside what valuation they would place on the player.

‌



The development follows reports that surfaced on social media claiming that Arsenal had lodged a bid exceeding £80m in an effort to secure Guimaraes' services.

However, ChronicleLive has reported that no such offer was submitted by Arsenal, with it also emerging that the Gunners would be unwilling to meet an £80m asking price to prise Guimaraes away from Tyneside.

Sports.title: Newsboy's horseracing tips for Monday's five meetings including Windsor NAP
Sports.content:
Newsboy's horseracing tips for Monday's five meetings including Windsor NAP

There are four meetings in Britain plus the Galway Festival opens in Ireland and our tipster has selections for all the cards with his double from Windsor and Ripon

View Image Newsboy's Nap runs at Windsor (Image: Getty Images)

HARRY KNOWS's (6.20, NAP) wait for an overdue first victory can come to an end at Windsor tonight.

‌



The Richard Hughes-trained youngster has been nothing but consistent in four starts this season, finishing second three times and fourth on his other appearance.

‌



Three of his defeats came as a short priced favourite but the 6f novice race on the banks of the Thames represents his best chance yet to open his account. He has gone down by a head in two runs under Oisin Murphy and the return of the champion jockey and the fitting of first time cheekpieces can make the difference.

‌



At Ripon COMMAND THE STARS (8.10, NB) can show what he is capable of on his first appearance since a gelding operation.

The three-year-old recorded his only win at Listed level last season but has been well beaten in three appearances this season, but if the surgery has done its job and help settle him down, George Scott’s challenger could make his presence felt.

Sports.title: Liverpool identify Bradley Barcola transfer alternative as ‘contact made’ with agent
Sports.content:
Liverpool identify Bradley Barcola transfer alternative as ‘contact made’ with agent

Liverpool are among the clubs linked with Paris Saint-Germain star Bradley Barcola as they attempt to find a replacement for Mo Salah but a deal could be very costly, forcing the Reds to look elsewhere

View 2 Images Liverpool have been told to pay £140m for Bradley Barcola (Image: Getty Images)

Liverpool are looking at Juventus star Francisco Conceicao as an alternative to Bradley Barcola, who could cost as much as £140million. The Reds are keen to add to their wide options this summer following Mohamed Salah’s exit a year before the end of his contract.

‌



Liverpool completed a deal for Spanish wideman Victor Munoz for £34.5m last month, albeit they still want to sign another forward. Bayern Munich’s Michael Olise has been linked, albeit the German giants are not keen on selling.

‌



Leipzig’s Yan Diomande was also an option but he now appears set for a move to Real Madrid. Paris Saint-Germain’s Barcola has also emerged as a priority target, but the French club’s £140m price tag is putting the Merseysiders off.

‌



That has forced Liverpool to look elsewhere. According to reports in Italy, Juventus’ Conceicao is seen as a cheaper option and they have already got in touch with his representatives regarding a deal.

Liverpool sent strong Michael Olise transfer warning by Bayern Munich chief READ MORE :

As it stands, Juventus are not keen on selling, having only spent £27.3m to sign him permanently last summer following an initial loan move from Porto. But it is thought that an offer in the region of around €50m (£42.6m) could be enough to seal his services.

It is not the first time that Liverpool have been linked with a swoop for Conceicao. His name was also mentioned during last season but the Portuguese international remained tight-lipped on his future.

‌



He said: “I know people talk about a big club, but I play for a big club where I am happy. At the moment I am only focused on these two games with the national team and then I will focus on the final stretch of the season to help my club as much as possible.”

View 2 Images Francisco Conceicao has been linked with Juventus on a number of occasions (Image: Getty Images)

“I am at a big club where the pressure to win is very high. I just have to keep working and contribute with goals and assists.

‌



“My objective is to help with goals and assists, that is what I try to do. I must continue every day to show that I have the ability to help the national team and be helped by them to keep improving.”

Conceicao, 23, has made 82 appearances for Juventus in all and has scored 11 goals in all competitions. His contract with the Italian giants is set to run until the summer of 2030.

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"

In spite of that, Babb's memories of the tournament are largely positive.

"I enjoyed it, I have to admit! I'd rather play in the searing heat than a wet Tuesday night in Hull," he says.

"I was a fit lad and it was quite easy for me playing alongside Paul McGrath, who was imperious in that tournament. I learned a lot from him and how he conserved his energy.

"I felt I got stronger because I got used to it. I guess our 0-0 draw against Norway would probably attest to the heat and the style of play.

"It all comes down to the individual. Footballers are supreme athletes now and they leave nothing to chance, so I think they'll cope a lot better than we did in the mid-90s."

The methods may have moved on since Charlton was throwing water onto the pitch, but Babb's memories from USA '94 provide a reminder this World Cup will be a battle against more than just the opposition.

Sports.title: Ogbene earns Republic of Ireland draw with Canada
Sports.content:
Chiedozie Ogbene's equaliser ensured the Republic of Ireland continued their good run of results as they drew 1-1 with World Cup co-hosts Canada in Montreal.

Canada went ahead in the 24th minute from an own goal by defender Jake O'Brien, heading a failed clearance into his own net from Stephen Eustaquio's corner.

Ireland were then awarded a penalty in the second half after Cyle Larin - who signed a two-year deal with Southampton earlier in the day - took out Jamie McGrath.

Canada goalkeeper Maxime Crepeau saved Troy Parrott's initial attempt, but Ogbene was on hand to slam home the rebound and tie the game in the 60th minute.

Image: Ireland's Jake O'Brien heads the ball into his own net

Ireland, who failed to qualify for this summer's World Cup, went close to a winner but Crepeau denied a charging run from Mason Melia late on.

The Orlando City goalkeeper missed out on the 2022 World Cup in Qatar after breaking his leg while playing in the MLS Cup final.

Canada, managed by former Leeds boss Jesse Marsch, officially open the World Cup on June 12 in Toronto against Bosnia and Herzegovina, before facing Qatar on June 18 and Switzerland on June 24.

They remain without captain Alphonso Davies, who is still nursing a hamstring injury he sustained while playing for Bayern Munich.

Sports.title: Republic of Ireland edge past Qatar in friendly as both sides end with 10
Sports.content:
Captain Nathan Collins headed the Republic of Ireland to a 1-0 friendly victory over World Cup-bound Qatar as both sides were reduced to 10 men.

Collins ensured Ireland got the better of a side managed by his former Wolves boss Julen Lopetegui with an early header.

However, just how the evening might have panned out had Jack Moylan not been dismissed as half-time approached, a sparse crowd inside the Aviva Stadium will never know.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, whose hopes of making it to the World Cup finals were dashed in heartbreaking fashion in March when they lost their play-off semi-final to the Czech Republic on penalties, were in complete control until Moylan's premature exit.

Qatar substitute Almoez Ali suffered the same fate 12 minutes from time.

Image: Jack Moylan was sent off before half-time at the Aviva Stadium

The game was played out against the backdrop of ongoing unease at the forthcoming Nations League clashes with Israel, and play was interrupted on several occasions during the first half as 'Stop the Game' protesters among a crowd of 28,981 repeatedly hurled tennis balls on to the pitch.

Ireland will now head for Montreal and their friendly against World Cup co-hosts Canada on June 6, while Qatar continue their preparations for the finals - they launch their Group B campaign against Switzerland in San Francisco on June 13 - against El Salvador in Los Angeles on the same day.

The Republic took the lead with just five minutes gone when, having been fouled by Ayoub Al-Oui wide on the left, Moylan curled the resulting free-kick on to the head of Collins, who glanced the ball effortlessly past 'keeper Mahmoud Abunada.

Image: Qatar's Almoez Ali was also sent off

There was a brief interruption after the protesters made their presence felt for the first time as Qatar's Pedro Miguel underwent treatment for injury, but once order had been restored, Troy Parrott whipped a first-time shot wide after being picked out by Seamus Coleman.

The Qataris simply could not get anywhere near Hallgrimsson's men and a mid-half drinks break did little to improve matters for the visitors with Abunada having to field Jayson Molumby's deflected 24th-minute shot from distance.

Lopetegui could not hide his frustration on the sideline and only the bravery of defender Ahmed Fathi denied Chiedozie Ogbene a second goal as he attempted to latch on to Liam Scales' header back across goal.

But the home side's night took a turn for the worse on the stroke of half-time when Northern Irish referee Jamie Robinson deemed Moylan's challenge on Jassem Gaber worthy of a red card, much to the Lincoln frontman's clear astonishment.

Image: Former Wolves and West Ham boss Julen Lopetegui is now in charge of Qatar

With defender James Abankwah having replaced Dara O'Shea at half-time, the 10 men found themselves under pressure for the first time on their return, although Coleman very nearly caught Abunada off his line with an audacious 52nd-minute attempt from the right wing.

Edmilson Junior dragged a long-range effort wide two minutes later after Molumby went down in midfield under Fathi's challenge and it took a fine 71st-minute reaction save by Caoimhin Kelleher - his first of the night - to keep out Yusuf Abdurisag's deflected shot.

However, Qatari hopes of salvation were dashed with 12 minutes remaining when Ali struck out at Molumby off the ball on several occasions and was also sent off.

Sports.title: Parrott out of luck as Republic of Ireland draw with North Macedonia
Sports.content:
Troy Parrott had two goals disallowed as the Republic of Ireland played out a stalemate against North Macedonia on the night on which they had hoped to book a trip to the World Cup finals.

Five days after their dreams came to an end for another four years in Prague, Ireland drew 0-0 with the Macedonians in a friendly encounter neither side wanted as the Czech Republic and Denmark fought for the big prize.

Even a third successive home victory for the first time since the 2015-16 campaign would have provided scant consolation for Thursday night's disappointment but Heimir Hallgrimsson's men had to make do with a disappointing draw.

AZ Alkmaar striker Parrott came closest to breaking the deadlock as 37-year-old defender Seamus Coleman received a standing ovation from a crowd of 39,560 at the Aviva Stadium when he was replaced during the second half of what could yet prove to be his final appearance for his country.

Nevertheless, the squad will reconvene for a series of friendlies at the end of the season ahead of next season's Nations League campaign and later Euro 2028 qualification having restored a measure of pride and established a momentum they hope will serve them well when they return to competitive action.

The hosts went on to the offensive from the off, although they were unable to find the final ball to allow either Parrott or Chiedozie Ogbene to threaten.

John Egan could not direct an 11th-minute corner at goal and Ogbene saw his snapshot deflected over three minutes later, but goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher had to parry Enis Bardhi's 21st-minute free-kick after it flicked off the defensive wall, with Bardhi volleying high over after the resulting corner had been only half-cleared.

Macedonia keeper Stole Dimitrievski saved Parrott's 23rd-minute header comfortably after Dara O'Shea and Finn Azaz had sparked a concerted attack, and Azaz failed to make the most of a free-kick two minutes later after he had been tripped just outside the penalty area.

Parrott was played into a promising position by Knight nine minutes before the break, only to miss the target by some distance.

The in-form striker - he scored his sixth goal in three games in Prague - might have done better again two minutes later after Azaz's clipped pass had caused problems for the Macedonian defence but he snatched at his attempt and fired high and wide.

Parrott twice had the ball in the net as time ran down but an offside flag stalled his celebrations on each occasion.

Ireland were unfortunate not to take the lead with 52 minutes gone when Azaz accepted Seamus Coleman's pass and found Parrott, who turned smartly before shooting against the upright.

Azaz curled an effort just wide and Tihomir Kostadinov denied Parrott a clear run on goal as the hosts began to turn the screw but it was veteran Coleman's 61st-minute departure as

Hallgrimsson made changes which attracted the biggest cheer of the night to that point.

Wholesale changes did not help the flow of the game, which rather petered out as the whistle approached, although Ireland substitute Johnny Kenny passed up a glorious opportunity to win it at the end with a weak shot at the keeper.

Sports.title: Szmodics out of hospital and 'on the mend' after collision
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland forward Sammie Szmodics has been released from hospital in Prague after being knocked unconscious during Thursday's World Cup play-off defeat by the Czech Republic.

The 24-year-old, who is currently on loan at Derby from Ipswich, was hurt in a collision with defender Stepan Chaloupek just two minutes after his introduction as an extra-time substitute at the Fortuna Arena, sparking concerned medics to rush to his aid.

Szmodics was carried from the field on a stretcher and taken straight to hospital, where Ireland head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson later revealed he would spend the night under observation.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Danyal Khan looks back on the heartbreaking result for the Republic of Ireland who lost their World Cup qualifying play-off against Czech Republic on penalties

A Football Association of Ireland spokesperson said on Friday morning: "Sammie Szmodics was transferred to hospital yesterday having sustained a head injury during extra time of the play-off against Czechia.

"Following further tests and a period of observation, he has been safely discharged from hospital and will continue his recovery under the care of the Republic of Ireland and Derby County medical teams."

Szmodics, who Hallgrimsson confirmed would have taken a penalty in the shoot-out which Ireland ultimately lost 4-3, took to social media to express his thanks to those who had helped him.

He posted on X: "Gutted the way it ended. Fans and boys immense all evening!! Appreciate everyone's messages. And thank you to the medical staff who acted so quickly to help me. On the mend."

Collins: Ireland must build on World Cup near miss

Ireland captain Nathan Collins is confident his side have laid the foundations to qualify for future tournaments having seen hopes of reaching this summer's World Cup finals come to an end.

Collins and his team-mates were agonisingly close to the play-off final when they led the Czech Republic 2-1 in Prague on Thursday evening with just four minutes of normal time remaining.

Image: A dejected Nathan Collins and head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson

However, Czech skipper Ladislav Krejci's late equaliser took the tie to extra-time and ultimately to penalties, where the hosts prevailed 4-3 to extend Ireland's wait for a first return to the big stage since 2002.

Asked about their progression to the play-offs, which was secured by back-to-back wins over Armenia, Portugal and Hungary, Brentford defender Collins said: "I'm not seeing many positives right now because we're in the gutter.

"But what we've created, the environment created with the fans and country, has been special. That's something we need to keep growing, to get even better at.

"That can help us get better on the pitch. We can push that and get fans to more tournaments."

Ireland had hoped to return to the Aviva Stadium on Tuesday for a showdown with either Denmark or North Macedonia for a place in the finals, but the Czechs will now host the Danes, who were 4-0 winners in Copenhagen.

Instead, Heimir Hallgrimsson's side face a friendly against the Macedonians.

Collins said: "The motivation has to be the same. We've to win to keep improving as a team and country. Any game we play at home is a big game."

Sports.title: 'Pain' - Irish heartbreak as Czech Republic win on penalties
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland's World Cup hopes were cruelly and heartbreakingly dashed as Czech Republic came from 2-0 down - to then beat them on penalties.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, who went two goals up after 23 minutes in Prague, were four minutes plus stoppage-time away from victory - before Wolves defender Ladislav Krejci headed in a corner to force extra-time.

Ireland were also a handful of penalties away from going through, as penalty saving expert Caomhin Kelleher saved from Mojmír Chytil in the shoot-out to give them a momentary advantage.

But Finn Azaz and Alan Browne both missed their spot kicks, allowing Patrick Schick and then Jan Kliment to win it for the hosts.

As a result, Czech Republic will go on to face Denmark on Tuesday for a spot at the World Cup - as Ireland's wait for a first World Cup appearance since 2002 goes on.

After Wales and Northern Ireland's semi-final exits, it also means England and Scotland will be the only teams from Great Britain and Ireland at the World Cup this summer.

Image: Ireland's players walk off the pitch after defeat

World Cup play-off finals - Europe Bosnia & Herzegovina vs Italy

Sweden vs Poland

Kosovo vs Turkey

Czech Republic vs Denmark

How Ireland threw away their lead

Ireland came flying out the blocks flying in Prague. Four shots in the opening ten minutes, including Nathan Collins crashing a shot off the bar from range, set the tone for a brilliant display - and they got their rewards.

A long throw caused chaos and Nathan Collins was deemed to have been caught slightly late by Vladimir Darida by VAR, who sent referee Glenn Byberg to the monitor for a review.

Troy Parrott, who else, crashed in the penalty for his sixth goal in the last three Ireland matches. And it got better for Ireland four minutes later.

Ryan Manning's corner found Dara O'Shea at the back post and his header across was cleared off the line by Vladimir Coufal - but off goalkeeper Matej Kovar and over the line.

Image: Czech Republic goalkeeper Matej Kovar scores an own goal to give Ireland a 2-0 lead

Ireland were in dreamland but a moment of Manning madness brought the Czech Republic back into it. The defender's needless tug back on Krekci - when the ball was heading out of play - was penalised by referee Byberg, with Patrick Schick pulling one back from the spot.

Ireland did, however, manage to settle the nerves down - right throughout the second half. Despite sustained Czech pressure in the second half, they barely threatened.

It was Ireland who had the better chances after the break, with Jayson Molumby striking the post and Parrott denied by a solid Kovar save at a corner. But then heartbreak struck with four minutes of normal time remaining, as Krejci bundled the ball in at the near post from a set piece.

Krejci could have even won it with the last kick of the game but scuffed his finish, as extra-time came.

Substitute Tomas Soucek missed a glorious chance for the hosts, with Adam Idah was denied a one-on-one chance by a goal-saving challenge from Stepan Chaloupek. Penalties came and the lottery fell in the hosts' favour.

Image: Jan Kliment scored the winning goal in the penalty shoot-out

Hallgrimsson confident in Ireland future despite 'pain'

Republic of Ireland boss Heimir Hallgrimsson:

"One word is pain. I feel pain. I feel pride for the performance of the players. They gave it all. I feel gratitude for all the supporters who supported us through the whole game, even after the loss. I feel pride being a part of that group. Personally, I know all the players will feel pain now. Only pain.

"We take with us that we can play teams higher in the FIFA ranking and can punch above our weight: Portugal, Hungary and here. We can compete with these teams. We came here with three wins in a row, a long time since that happened for this national team.

"So there's growth in this squad. It's maturing. These are been the biggest game most of these players have played. That's encouraging to know we're growing. It's strange to say that after we lost today.

"I know I'm biased in this, all the statistics and metrics of the team have improved. Big games, being on the line, crunch times all the time, we've managed to go through this. It showed the resilience, character of these players, that's why I feel confident going on."

Sports.title: Wilson key for Wales, NI aim for big upset while history beckons for ROI
Sports.content:
Sky Sports assesses Thursday's 2026 World Cup play-off semi-finals as Wales host Bosnia-Herzegovina, Northern Ireland go to four-time winners Italy and the Republic of Ireland face Czech Republic in Prague.

Thursday 7.45pm: Wales vs Bosnia-Herzegovina (winner will play Italy or Northern Ireland)

Harry Wilson is not the new Gareth Bale, but he's doing the job of Bale at his best, especially for Wales.

Fans have long been excited about Wilson's natural talent, but are now seeing his influence in the Premier League on a weekly basis for Fulham. This season, he has 10 goals and six assists for club, while for country, his stats are even better with five goals and two assists in his last five games.

If Wilson starts running the show, his confidence will feed to the other players and to the home crowd, and Wales will be very difficult to stop on their own patch.

Which World Cup group would Wales be in? If Wales qualify for the World Cup they would be in Group B with Canada, Switzerland and Qatar.

Craig Bellamy wanted to create an identity for Wales when he took over as head coach. It's now clear: he wants front-foot football coupled with intensity and energy.

Bellamy doesn't always see that in international football as he finds it slower at times compared with club football, but his Wales side will not be ponderous. You could see during the qualification campaign that Wales' intensity in winning the ball back very quickly and holding possession grew. Now it's about consistently doing it.

Apart from consistency in play, there needs to be consistency in selection. Much is always made about the 'spine' of a good team, from the goalkeeper to the glory hunter! Leeds United provide a fair chunk of Wales' spine with 'keeper Karl Darlow on form and in receipt of the No.1 keeper's jersey. Joe Rodon is the rock at centre-back that success relies upon, while team-mate Ethan Ampadu's versatility means he can link anywhere between defence and midfield. Throw in one of the in-form Premier League stars, Harry Wilson, and a strong spine can take a team a long way.

Ask Bellamy if he has thought about preparing for the play-off final against either Italy or Northern Ireland and you'll get glared at. It's Bosnia, Bosnia and Bosnia. He won't entertain anything beyond Bosnia until the game is over. It's a danger, a banana skin he wants to avoid. Thinking too far ahead isn't good on this occasion.

Geraint Hughes

Thursday 7.45pm: Italy vs Northern Ireland (winner will play Wales or Bosnia-Herzegovina)

On paper, perhaps in reality, it's David vs Goliath.

Northern Ireland enjoy David vs Goliath. Once upon a time it was David (Healy) vs England and David (Healy) vs Spain.

For smaller nations there is comfort in being the underdog. A loss would be met without a major backlash, a win makes you a hero. That's how Michael O'Neill's side will approach Thursday's assignment in Bergamo against Italy.

Which World Cup group would Northern Ireland be in? If Northern Ireland qualified for the World Cup they would be in Group B with Canada, Switzerland and Qatar.

Conor Bradley and Daniel Ballard are out. Between them they represent 50 per cent of the Northern Ireland players currently plying their trade in the Premier League.

The pair's absence is as much a blow to Northern Ireland's attacking prospects as it is defensively. Ballard represents their best aerial threat from set-pieces, Bradley their most dynamic player on the ball.

And yet for some reason that only football can explain, hope remains. The four-time World Cup winners are heavy favourites but far from the Azzurri powerhouse of old.

If Northern Ireland have it their way, it's unlikely to be a pretty spectacle. But can they frustrate their hosts? 0-0 at half-time? Pounce on the sense of angst that will exist among the home support?

To call it a free hit would be to downplay the importance of the game. But Northern Ireland are free from the weight of expectation.

Daring to dream of a result that becomes instant folklore.

Michael Morrow

Thursday 7.45pm: Czech Republic vs Republic of Ireland (winner will play Denmark or North Macedonia)

Image: Republic of Ireland boss Heimir Hallgrimsson and captain Seamus Coleman spoke to the media in Prague

History beckons for the Republic of Ireland here in Prague.

Make no mistake, this will be the biggest game to date for a lot of these Irish players as they attempt to take another step to this summer's World Cup but they must get past Czech Republic to do so.

Which World Cup group would Republic of Ireland be in? If the Republic of Ireland qualified for the World Cup they would be in Group A with co-hosts Mexico, South Africa and South Korea.

Still coming off the euphoria of the incredible back-to-back wins against Portugal and Hungary last November, this is an Irish team full of confidence.

Having spoken to a few people around the Czech Republic team, those results have been noted and they are particularly worried about Irish striker Troy Parrott, who scored five goals in those two games in November - including the 96th-minute winner against Hungary.

Head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson spoke ahead of this game about one of the key aspects is visually and mentally being ready for the challenge ahead of them, he seemed as calm and confident as usual.

However his key selection dilemma is does he bring back the experienced, tried and tested players such as Seamus Coleman, Robbie Brady and Chiedoze Ogbene - all three have had limited game-time this season for a variety of injuries.

Coleman and Brady especially are the only two players in the squad who were part of Ireland's last team in a major tournament which was in 2016 - their experience could prove vital.

Image: Can Troy Parrott recreate his Irish heroics in Prague on Thursday?

Their opponents are in a state of flux.

Czech Republic have a new head coach who takes charge of his first game on Thursday, with West Ham's Tomas Soucek also being stripped of the captaincy after November's internationals having caused shockwaves in the local media - Wolves' Ladislav Krejci has replaced him.

The pressure feels like it's all on the home side which could play into Ireland's advantage as they look to take another step to qualify for this summer's World Cup - their first since 2002.

Danyal Khan
