Sports.title: Dana White Confirms Shakur Stevenson Return Before End Of Year
Sports.content:
“Yeah,” said Dana during the Zuffa Boxing 09 post-event press conference.

Pressed for the opponent for Shakur, Dana kept his cards close to the vest.

“If I did, I would have announced it already.”

White also commented on one of the biggest names linked to Stevenson.

“I love Tank Davis. I’m actually a fan, and we’ve talked to them.”

White stopped short of suggesting that fight is close, making it clear only that communication has taken place.

The opponent is the difficult part. Devin Haney remains on course for a WBO title fight with Keyshawn Davis if the mandatory moves forward, while Ryan Garcia is committed to his September clash with Conor Benn. Teofimo Lopez also has business to finish against Rolando ‘Rolly’ Romero.

Stevenson has previously mentioned Gervonta Davis, Gary Antuanne Russell and Lamont Roach Jr. as opponents he would welcome. The problem for Zuffa is that only Davis has the type of commercial appeal that fits a reported eight-figure investment in one of its marquee signings. Russell would interest hardcore boxing fans, while Roach is a respected champion, but neither matchup carries the same mainstream appeal.

That leaves White facing one of his toughest matchmaking decisions since launching Zuffa Boxing. A fight against a fringe contender would be difficult to sell. White has spent months talking about making the sport’s premier fights. Matching Shakur with an opponent outside the elite level would leave fans asking whether anything has really changed.

Sports.title: Edgar Berlanga Stops Steven Butler in Chaotic Ending
Sports.content:
The finish turned chaotic. After Berlanga rocked Butler with a left hook and straight right, the referee rushed in to stop the fight with Butler still on his feet. Instead of simply separating the fighters, the official grabbed Butler with enough force that both crashed to the canvas together, creating one of the strangest stoppages seen in a major boxing event this year.

As Butler lay tangled with the referee, Berlanga stepped over them and cocked his right hand as though he was about to throw another punch. He never landed the shot, but the gesture drew an immediate reaction because the fight had already been waved off and Butler was under the referee’s protection.

The sequence spread quickly across social media, with many fans criticizing Berlanga’s conduct after the stoppage while others focused on the referee’s awkward intervention. Although the ending looked bizarre, there was little disagreement that Butler was no longer capable of defending himself when the referee ended the bout.

The victory gave Berlanga (24-2, 19 KOs) an important rebound after his previous defeat a year ago against Hamzah Sheeraz. Butler (38-6-1, 32 KOs) enjoyed his best moments early in the fight.

Berlanga boxed effectively in the opening round, using his jab and movement to keep Butler from closing the distance. He stayed on the outside, picked his shots, and appeared confident enough to exchange words with Butler before returning to his corner.

The momentum changed late in the second. Berlanga landed a left hook to the temple followed by a straight right, but Butler answered before the bell with a right hand that sent Berlanga to the canvas. Berlanga quickly climbed to his feet and assured the referee he was clear to continue, while the knockdown energized Butler heading into the third.

Instead of becoming cautious, Berlanga came out firing. Heavy combinations in the third round left Butler hurt, and the New York native continued pressing the action with hard jabs, left hooks, and straight rights. Butler refused to back down, firing back whenever opportunities appeared, turning the fight into an entertaining exchange of power punches.

Berlanga gradually separated himself over the next few rounds. Butler’s toughness kept him competitive, but he struggled to slow Berlanga’s offense or put together sustained attacks of his own. Nearly every successful rally from Butler was answered by another burst from Berlanga.

The tide fully turned in the sixth round. Berlanga dropped Butler near the end of the frame, leaving the Canadian unsteady as he made his way back to the corner. It appeared the finish was close.

The end came early in the seventh. Berlanga trapped Butler and landed a crushing left hook followed by a straight right that left him helpless against the ropes. Butler remained upright but offered little resistance as Berlanga closed in. The referee stepped between them before Butler could absorb more punishment, ending the fight with the Canadian badly hurt.

The win for Berlanga was one of his strongest performances in recent years because of the way he responded to adversity. After suffering an early knockdown, he regained control, broke Butler down with steady pressure, and produced an emphatic stoppage in front of his hometown crowd.

Sports.title: Richardson Hitchins Shuts Out Ricardo Salas in Welterweight Debut
Sports.content:
The judges scored the bout 100-90 across the board after Hitchins controlled every round with his jab, movement, and defensive skills. The victory marked a successful debut at 147 pounds as well as his first appearance under the Zuffa Boxing banner.

From the opening bell, Hitchins established the piston-like jab that carried him to a world title at 140 pounds. Salas tried to work his way inside with body shots, but each advance was met by another stiff jab or straight right. Whenever Salas managed to close the distance, Hitchins circled away or tied him up before the Mexican could work. The tactic kept Salas from building any sustained offense, although it also slowed the pace and produced long stretches with little action.

The Brooklyn native looked physically comfortable despite moving up in weight. His footwork kept Salas chasing, and his shoulder-roll defense caused many punches to miss. Hitchins fought a style familiar to anyone who has watched Shakur Stevenson. He boxed behind the jab, moved whenever Salas closed the distance, then tied him up before another exchange could begin.

Salas continued marching forward over the final rounds, refusing to give up despite taking clean shots. Hitchins never abandoned the game plan. His corner encouraged him to press harder in search of a stoppage, yet he stayed committed to boxing safely from the outside instead of taking unnecessary chances.

After the fight, Hitchins revealed that his right hand began bothering him around the sixth round because of an injury suffered in training camp. Even with the issue, he finished the contest without appearing troubled.

Hitchins later mentioned Gervonta Davis, Ryan Garcia, and Devin Haney as opponents he wants next. His first appearance at welterweight left little doubt about his technical ability, even if the safety-first style won’t appeal to fans looking for action. It produced a complete shutout on the scorecards, showing that Hitchins has already become difficult to solve at 147 pounds.

Sports.title: Jalil Hackett Outboxes Sergiy Derevyanchenko, Survives Late Scare
Sports.content:
Hackett established the pace early by working behind a sharp jab and using quick footwork to keep Derevyanchenko from settling into a rhythm. The veteran patiently looked for openings, landing occasional overhand rights when Hackett lingered too long in range, but he struggled to match the younger fighter’s output.

Hackett became more aggressive in the middle rounds. He landed uppercuts, snapped back Derevyanchenko’s head with straight shots, and backed the veteran toward the ropes.

A crisp uppercut late in the fifth round snapped the veteran’s head back and highlighted Hackett’s growing confidence.

The damage became increasingly visible as cuts opened around both of Derevyanchenko’s eyes. Blood streamed down his face over the second half of the fight, yet the Ukrainian continued pressing forward, showing the durability that has defined his career against many of the sport’s best middleweights.

Although Hackett appeared comfortably ahead entering the final round, Derevyanchenko refused to go quietly. The veteran landed a hard shot that staggered Hackett and briefly gave the crowd hope of a dramatic finish. Hackett recovered quickly, regained his composure, and avoided any further trouble before the final bell.

The closing scare was not enough to erase Hackett’s work over the first nine rounds. His jab, movement, and cleaner punching earned him the unanimous decision over a battle-tested opponent who had previously shared the ring with elite fighters throughout the middleweight division.

Hackett left New York with the biggest victory of his career, but the performance raised as many questions as it answered. Derevyanchenko, a 40-year-old veteran coming off a lengthy layoff, remained dangerous until the final bell and badly hurt Hackett in the 10th round.

Sports.title: Vladyslav Sirenko Knocks Out Otto Wallin With One Second Left
Sports.content:
The Ukrainian’s right hand, followed by a crushing left hook, ended a competitive fight at 2:59 of the last round. Wallin collapsed face-first onto the canvas and remained down long enough that medical personnel entered the ring before he was taken out on a stretcher.

The finish gave Sirenko (23-1, 20 KOs) a signature victory in his first appearance under the Zuffa Boxing banner. Wallin (28-4, 16 KOs) suffered one of the most devastating knockouts of his career.

For much of the fight, neither heavyweight appeared close to producing such a sudden ending. They traded willingly from the opening round, spending long stretches working at close range. Sirenko consistently targeted the body and often forced Wallin backward with his aggression.

Wallin, 35, relied on his experience to keep the fight competitive. The Swedish southpaw used subtle footwork to create punching angles, landed accurate counters, and gradually opened swelling beneath Sirenko’s right eye. His cleaner punching allowed him to bank several rounds as the bout reached the middle stages.

The pace remained high despite obvious fatigue setting in during the closing rounds. Sirenko continued pressing the action even after showing signs of exhaustion, while Wallin matched him with determined exchanges that kept the outcome in doubt entering the final minute.

With only a second remaining before the final bell, Sirenko uncorked a straight right that snapped Wallin’s head back before immediately following with a left hook. The combination landed flush and left Wallin unconscious as he crashed to the canvas, ending the contest without the need for a count.

Sports.title: Edgar Berlanga vs. Steven Butler Live Results and Fight Updates
Sports.content:
Edgar Berlanga overcame an early knockdown to stop Steven Butler in the seventh round of their scheduled 10-round super middleweight main event Sunday night at the Infosys Theater at Madison Square Garden in New York. Butler floored Berlanga in the second round, but Berlanga (24-2, 19 KOs) regained control behind heavy combinations that repeatedly backed his opponent up. Butler (38-6-1, 32 KOs) absorbed punishment through the middle rounds before the referee halted the fight in Round 7 with the Canadian badly hurt and no longer defending himself. The victory gave Berlanga a rebound win after his previous defeat and improved his record to 24-2 with 19 knockouts. The contest was halted at 1:14 of round.

Richardson Hitchins turned in a flawless performance Sunday night, defeating Ricardo Salas by unanimous decision in their 10-round welterweight co-main event at the Infosys Theater at Madison Square Garden in New York. Fighting for the first time at 147 pounds, Hitchins (21-0, 8 KOs) controlled the contest with a sharp jab, accurate straight punches, and disciplined footwork that kept Salas (24-4-2, 19 KOs) from mounting any sustained offense. Salas pressed forward at times but struggled to cut off the ring or land consistently against the former IBF light welterweight champion. All three judges scored the bout 100-90, giving Hitchins a dominant victory in his welterweight debut and Zuffa Boxing debut.

Middleweight Jalil Hackett earned a 10-round unanimous decision over former world title challenger Sergiy Derevyanchenko in the opening bout of the main card. Hackett controlled most of the action with steady pressure and accurate punching, leaving the veteran badly marked around both eyes. Derevyanchenko nearly changed the fight in the 10th round when he staggered Hackett, but the younger fighter recovered and finished the bout. The judges scored it 98-92, 97-93, and 96-94 in Hackett’s favor.

Vladyslav Sirenko produced a dramatic finish by knocking out Otto Wallin with only seconds remaining in the 10th and final round of their heavyweight bout. Sirenko uncorked a right hand followed by a left hook that left Wallin unconscious, bringing an abrupt end to a closely contested fight. Wallin, 35, remained down after the knockout and was removed from the ring on a stretcher. The finish gave Sirenko (23-1, 20 KOs) a knockout victory over former world title challenger Otto Wallin.

Welterweight Emiliano Moreno earned an eight-round unanimous decision over Arnold Gonzalez in a competitive fight. Moreno (13-1, 7 KOs) built momentum after a closely contested start, landing the cleaner punches and applying steady pressure to take control over the second half of the fight. Gonzalez enjoyed success in spots, including a strong rally late in the seventh round, but he was unable to sustain it over the full distance. The judges scored the contest 79-73, 78-74, and 78-74 for Moreno, giving him a successful debut under the Zuffa Boxing banner.

Kashaun Davis outboxed Mihai Nistor over eight rounds to earn a unanimous decision in a clash between unbeaten heavyweight punchers. Davis used quick combinations and fast hands to control the action, while Nistor (8-1, 8 KOs) spent much of the fight trying to slow the pace by tying him up. An accidental head clash opened a cut over Nistor’s right eye, and he later lost a point for repeated holding in the fifth round. The judges scored it 80-71, 80-71, and 79-72 for Davis (12-0, 11 KOs), who picked up the first decision victory of his professional career.

Troy Nash remained unbeaten with an eight-round majority decision over Ethan Perez in a competitive featherweight matchup. Perez (8-1-1, 3 KO) applied steady pressure during the early rounds, but Nash (8-0-1, 1 KOs) answered with a sharp jab and composed boxing that allowed him to control many of the exchanges. Neither fighter was knocked down as both prospects boxed at a high pace through the final bell. The judges scored it 79-73, 79-73, and 76-76 for Nash, handing Perez the first loss of his professional career.

Dominique Francis boxed well early, but Andres Sosa shifted the fight in his favor after dropping him with a left hook in the third round of their eight-round super featherweight opener. Sosa kept coming forward, landing overhand shots plus steady body work that gradually wore Francis down over the second half of the contest. Francis rallied in the final round, looking for a late breakthrough, but Sosa answered back often enough to stay in control. The judges scored it 79-72, 78-73, and 77-73 for Sosa, handing Francis the first defeat of his professional career.

Sports.title: Mike Tyson Destroys Marvis Frazier In Fastest Career Knockout
Sports.content:
Tyson had already fought nine times in 1986, leaving a trail of early knockouts that made him the sport’s most feared young contender. Marvis, the son of former heavyweight champion Joe Frazier, accepted one of the toughest tests in boxing after rebuilding his career with victories over James Tillis and James “Bonecrusher” Smith. Many observers questioned whether the matchup had come too soon for him.

Despite the modest crowd in Glens Falls, ABC’s Wide World of Sports broadcast the fight nationwide. Tyson earned approximately $135,000 for the bout, well below Marvis Frazier’s reported $250,000 purse. It proved to be the last time Tyson made less money than his opponent.

There was no cautious opening. Tyson stormed across the ring behind his trademark pressure, clipped Frazier with a right hand, then trapped him near the corner. A pair of uppercuts followed. The second, a crushing right, left Frazier unconscious before he collapsed to the canvas without landing a meaningful punch.

Referee Joe Cortez immediately realized the fight was over. He halted his count at five after seeing Frazier was unresponsive, later remarking that he “could have counted to 20” because fighter safety came first.

Tyson later revealed he sensed hesitation from Frazier before the opening bell. He expected the fight to end quickly. Once the excitement faded, his attention turned to Frazier’s condition after the stoppage.

The victory became another milestone in Tyson’s unforgettable 1986 campaign. He returned less than a month later to stop José Ribalta, followed with another knockout over Alfonzo Ratliff, then demolished Trevor Berbick in November to become the youngest heavyweight champion in boxing history.

Marvis Frazier never regained his place among the heavyweight contenders. He boxed only three more times before retiring in 1988. Tyson’s 30-second destruction of Frazier remains the fastest knockout of his professional career. Four months later, he captured the heavyweight championship, making the victory one of the defining performances of his rise.

Sports.title: Spencer Brown Says Tyson Fury Beats Anthony Joshua After Prenga Fight
Sports.content:
“I was in shock. I was in a lot of shock,” Brown told Seconds Out. “Wait till he gets in with big Tyson Fury. That’s a different beast. He’s a different beast. That performance was an easy performance yesterday.”

Brown admitted he believed Joshua’s comeback bid had already ended after the opening round.

“Thought we’d lost the fight. It was all over. The dream was over. Thank God he got up and he did what he did,” said Spencer.

Brown’s view matched criticism from several figures in boxing who questioned Joshua’s display despite the knockout victory. Getting dropped twice by a late replacement left many wondering how Joshua would fare against elite opposition after returning from his lengthy layoff.

Brown also rejected criticism that Fury looked sluggish during his own return, suggesting much of it came from Joshua supporters.

“The people criticizing him are Anthony Joshua fans, aren’t they? Simple. Social media. They criticize me, they’ll criticize you, they criticize everybody. That’s what it is,” said Brown.

While Brown was quick to dismiss concerns over Tyson Fury’s own recent outing, the contrast on the canvas is hard to ignore. In his return against 46-year-old Mariusz Wach, Fury offered little of the fleet-footed brilliance that defined his victories over Wladimir Klitschko or Deontay Wilder. Looking slow, heavy, and visibly faded, Fury relied on raw size to wear down Wach over seven grueling rounds before forcing a clubbing stoppage.

The last eight years have exacted a heavy toll on the former champion. Brown may dismiss the sluggish display as simple social media blather, but Fury’s labor against an aging journeyman suggests time has caught up to both heavyweights, making any potential meeting far less predictable than his manager claims.

Ghana News.title: IMF Board set to approve Ghana’s final Programme Review, greenlight post-bailout economic plan
Ghana News.content:
IMF Mission Chief for Ghana, Ruben Atoyan

The Executive Board of the International Monetary Fund (IMF) is expected to meet today to consider and approve Ghana’s sixth and final review under the Extended Credit Facility (ECF) programme.

JOYBUSINESS understands that approval of the review will unlock a final disbursement of about US$318 million for Ghana.

The Board is also expected to consider and approve Ghana’s request for a 36-month Policy Coordination Instrument (PCI), a non-financing arrangement that will guide the country’s economic reforms after the conclusion of the IMF bailout programme.

Unlike the ECF, the PCI does not provide direct funding. Instead, it offers closer policy engagement with the IMF and signals a country’s commitment to reforms, helping to strengthen investor confidence and attract support from development partners.

The PCI is designed to help countries maintain macroeconomic stability, build resilience against external shocks, address structural imbalances and support sustainable economic growth.

Why the Board Is Meeting

Today’s meeting follows the staff-level agreement reached between Ghana and the IMF in April after the Fund’s mission to Accra.

JOYBUSINESS understands that government has since met key quantitative and structural targets required for Board approval.

These include decisions on the recapitalisation and governance reforms of UMB Bank and Prudential Bank, alongside other prior actions agreed under the programme.

Although Ghana is among several countries on the IMF Board’s agenda, approval today would formally conclude the country’s three-year ECF programme.

Earlier this year, IMF Mission Chief for Ghana, Dr Ruben Atoyan, told JOYBUSINESS that once the Board approves the review, the final tranche of more than US$318 million would be released to the Bank of Ghana.

Government Eyes Next Reform Phase

The Finance Minister, Dr Cassiel Ato Forson, has already indicated that Ghana is preparing to transition from the ECF to the PCI to preserve recent macroeconomic gains and deepen structural reforms.

Presenting the 2026 Mid-Year Budget Review, Dr Forson said the PCI would anchor the country’s next phase of reforms, strengthen macroeconomic resilience and support broad-based growth.

According to him, the new programme will focus on six priority areas: growth-friendly fiscal consolidation, debt sustainability, fiscal transparency and governance, stronger monetary and exchange rate policy frameworks, financial sector stability, and economic diversification.

He said the PCI would help preserve the gains achieved under the IMF-supported programme while reinforcing investor confidence and policy credibility.

Background

An IMF staff team led by Dr Ruben Atoyan visited Accra from April 29 to May 15 for Ghana’s 2026 Article IV consultation, the sixth and final review of the ECF programme, and discussions on the country’s request for a PCI.

At the end of the mission, the IMF said Ghana had achieved “substantial stabilisation gains”, including lower inflation, stronger international reserves, improved confidence in the cedi and progress in debt restructuring.

The Fund, however, urged government to press ahead with reforms in the energy sector, particularly efforts to improve efficiency at the Electricity Company of Ghana through private sector participation.

Ghana entered the 36-month ECF arrangement in May 2023 with access to about US$3 billion to help restore macroeconomic stability, implement fiscal reforms and support the country’s debt restructuring programme.

Ghana News.title: Ghana to deploy condom vending machines nationwide by end of 2026 to boost HIV prevention
Ghana News.content:
Ghana will begin deploying condom vending machines across the country by the last quarter of 2026 as part of efforts to improve access to condoms and strengthen the fight against HIV/AIDS, the Ghana AIDS Commission (GAC) has announced.

The machines are expected to be installed at strategic public locations, including lorry stations, mosques, stadia and shopping malls, to enable people to obtain condoms privately without direct interaction with vendors.

The Commission is also seeking to extend the initiative to public institutions, including washrooms in ministries, departments, agencies and financial institutions, under its national HIV and wellness policy.

The announcement was made during a dissemination meeting in Accra on the 2026 HIV Estimates and Projections, which reviewed the state of Ghana's HIV epidemic, identified gaps in the national response and outlined future interventions.

According to the Commission, the condom vending initiative forms part of a broader condom and lubricant strategy aimed at increasing access to prevention tools while adapting distribution methods to the needs of different communities.

Speaking at the event, Director-General of the Ghana AIDS Commission, Dr Kharmacelle Prosper Akanbong, said the machines would be designed differently depending on the characteristics of the communities where they would be deployed.

“The machines will not all be the same. Depending on the peculiar characteristics of a local population, the machine deployed could be electronically operated or manually administered,” he said.

Dr Akanbong recalled that Ghana had previously introduced condom vending machines that dispensed packs of three condoms for 50 pesewas, but the programme eventually collapsed after many of the machines were vandalised.

“People were forcefully emptying the machines to take the coins,” he said, adding that the new generation of machines would be designed to minimise the risk of vandalism.

He also assured the public that concerns about condom shortages reported last year had been addressed, stating that the government had procured additional supplies which are now available nationwide.

Also speaking at the meeting, the World Health Organization Country Office Technical Lead for HIV, Tuberculosis and Hepatitis, Dr Kafui Senya, called for sustained efforts to reduce new HIV infections, eliminate stigma and discrimination, and ensure equitable access to prevention and treatment services.

Programme Manager of the National AIDS and STIs Control Programme, Dr Emmanuel Akwoulo Agyigewe Teviu, urged stakeholders to close persistent gaps in HIV prevention and strengthen integrated, people-centred care, while Governing Board Chair of the Ghana AIDS Commission, Kakra Essamuah, reaffirmed the government's commitment to strengthening Ghana's national HIV response.

Ghana News.title: NDPC briefs Speaker Bagbin on proposed consolidated national development plan
Ghana News.content:
Dr Nii Moi Thompson, Chairman of the National Development Planning Commission (NDPC), has briefed the Speaker of Parliament, Mr Alban Kingsford Sumana Bagbin, on the Commission’s efforts to prepare a Ghana Consolidated National Development Plan to guide economic transformation and shared prosperity.

Dr Thompson said the Commission was compiling four existing but unimplemented development frameworks including the 40-Year Development Plan (2016), Ghana Beyond Aid (2019), Ghana@100 (2019), and Vision 2057 (2024) into a single plan expected to be adopted by Parliament as “the legislated will of the people.”

He explained that the Consolidated Plan forms part of the Commission’s evaluation of Ghana’s “unfinished business of development” over the past 70 years and the preparation of a medium-to-long-term Road Map for Economic Transformation and Shared Prosperity.

According to Dr Thompson, Ghana has remained in a “middle-income trap” since attaining lower middle-income status in 2010, and risks stagnation or reversal unless Parliament legislates the Consolidated Plan as a strategic framework to guide medium-term and annual action plans.

The Speaker welcomed the briefing and pledged Parliament’s support, stressing the importance of governance and institutional reforms in achieving national development aspirations.

He highlighted Ghana’s political progress under the Fourth Republic, noting that the country has become a destination for study tours by legislators from advanced and emerging democracies.

He further underscored the importance of ethics in leadership and public service, urging the NDPC to integrate this into the Consolidated Plan.

As part of stakeholder consultations, the NDPC is expected to brief Parliament’s Committee of the Whole at the invitation of the Speaker.

The Commission will subsequently engage political parties, traditional authorities, faith-based organisations and a public call for submissions.

Ghana News.title: Presbyterian Church launches Disability Policy, urges members to champion inclusion
Ghana News.content:
The Presbyterian Church of Ghana (PCG) has launched its Disability Policy and inaugurated a National Committee on Disability, with a call on all members to make disability inclusion an integral part of the Church’s holistic ministry.

The initiative seeks to promote the full participation of persons with disabilities in all aspects of church life and governance.

Reverend David Aboagye Danquah, Clerk of the General Assembly of the Presbyterian Church of Ghana, called on all levels of the Church, from the General Assembly to local congregations, to embrace inclusion not only in principle but also in practice.

He urged congregations to ensure accessibility in church infrastructure through the provision of ramps, accessible washrooms, and other disability-friendly facilities.

Rev Danquah also advocated sign language interpretation during church services, the production of large-print bulletins and the development of innovative programmes that respond to the diverse needs of persons with disabilities.

He cautioned against the use of language in preaching and teaching that associated disability with sin, curses, or personal deficiency.

“Persons with disabilities must serve as Presbyters, Committee Chairpersons, Coordinators, Sunday School Teachers, Choristers, leaders in every sphere of church life,” Rev Danquah said.

“Disability inclusion is not a favour we extend to others; it is an act of obedience to the God who created all persons in His Image.”

Mrs Gertrude Oforiwa Fefoame, National Focal Person on Disability, acknowledged the logistical and financial challenges associated with implementing the policy but stressed the need for deliberate investments across all levels of the Church.

She appealed to every court of the Church to make budgetary allocations towards disability inclusion initiatives.

“Building the capacity of the Church at all the courts, irrespective of how it is done, will require a dedicated budget from each court. We therefore appeal for this to be made an intentional investment by each court,” she added.

Mrs Fefoame outlined key implementation strategies, including the establishment of Disability Committees in all Presbyteries, cascading training, data collection, and the submission of six-monthly progress reports.

She also announced plans to institute a Presbyterian observance of the National Week of Disability.

Reverend Andrew Shardow, National Director of the Department of Church Life and Nurture (CLAN), said persons with disabilities had historically faced various forms of exclusion and injustice, a situation that must not continue.

He noted that the Church’s commitment to holistic ministry required deliberate efforts to ensure the inclusion of all persons, regardless of disability status.

“The Presbyterian Church pursues holistic ministry, and as a church we must be intentional in pursuing the inclusion of persons with disabilities,” he said.

Rev Shardow said the Church recognised the dignity and worth of persons with disabilities and urged all Presbyterians to adopt disability-friendly attitudes and practices.

Reverend Ebenezer Acheampong Asiedu, National Chairperson of the Committee on Disability, said the committee would work to ensure the active and structural inclusion of persons with disabilities within the Church.

“We will raise a prophetic voice against stigma, discrimination and societal barriers,” he declared.

Rev Asiedu called for the dismantling of theological misconceptions surrounding disability and encouraged pastors to use their pulpits to promote messages of inclusion, acceptance and equal participation.

He further urged church leaders to ensure that worship spaces remained welcoming and accessible to all.

Ghana News.title: GPHA plans sports centre as it marks 40th anniversary
Ghana News.content:
The Ghana Ports and Harbours Authority (GPHA) has announced plans to establish a dedicated sports centre and institutionalise regular health walks to promote the physical, mental and social well-being of its workforce.

The announcement was made during a health and awareness walk organised simultaneously in Tema and Takoradi to officially launch activities marking the GPHA’s 40th anniversary celebration.

The exercise brought together management, staff, retirees, their families, union executives and members of the GPHA community in a display of unity and solidarity.

Addressing participants after the walk at the Junior Club House in Tema Community Two, Mr Tebon Zumah, Director of Port, Tema, commended staff and retirees for their enthusiastic participation and resilience throughout the exercise.

Mr Zumah expressed appreciation to the GPHA workforce for its dedication and commitment over the past four decades, saying their collective efforts had sustained public confidence in Ghana’s ports and contributed significantly to the country’s trade facilitation agenda.

He said management was considering making the health walk a permanent feature on the GPHA’s annual calendar because of its health and social benefits.

He stated that plans were also underway to establish a dedicated sports centre to provide employees with a permanent facility for fitness programmes, sporting activities and other staff engagement initiatives.

Mr Zumah urged employees to remain committed to excellence in their respective roles to ensure that the Ports of Tema and Takoradi continued to strengthen their reputation as efficient and competitive gateways for trade within the sub-region.

Meanwhile, in Takoradi, Captain James Richmond Quayson, Director of Port, Takoradi, described the anniversary as a celebration of the merger that gave birth to the modern Ghana Ports and Harbours Authority.

He said the authority had evolved into a major shipping and logistics hub through the commitment and hard work of its employees.

Captain Quayson also commended the dedication of staff at the Port of Takoradi, noting that every department remained focused on delivering efficient services to customers.

He wished staff continued success and prayed for God’s blessings upon employees, management and the board as the authority celebrated its 40th anniversary.

The anniversary health walks featured music, dancing and health awareness activities, with participants dressed in the authority’s blue, yellow and white colours.

Ghana News.title: Galamsey affecting fish production in Bono Region – Fisheries Commission
Ghana News.content:
Charlotte Ndah, the Wenchi Zonal Director of the Fisheries Commission in the Bono Region, has expressed concern that illegal mining, popularly known as galamsey, around water bodies is causing a decline in fish production across the region.

She said fishermen, particularly those operating on the Bui Dam Reservoir in the Banda District, had consistently complained of reduced fish catches, attributing the situation to illegal mining activities in the area.

“The chemicals being used by the illegal miners have exterminated and also driven the fishes away and seriously affected our waters,” Mrs Ndah stated.

She was speaking to the media on the sidelines of a research project and stakeholders’ engagement organised by the School of Natural Resources of the University of Energy and Natural Resources (UENR) at Fiapre, near Sunyani.

The programme, held on the theme: “Partnering Innovative Research in Natural Resources for Sustainable Development,” brought together industry players, development organisations, professional bodies and institutions, including the Fisheries Commission and the Environmental Protection Authority.

Mrs Ndah said effective law enforcement remained the surest means of curbing illegal mining and safeguarding water bodies.

She explained that the Commission’s law enforcement unit was collaborating with stakeholders to control illegal mining activities and preserve the region’s water resources.

In a speech read on his behalf, Professor Elvis Asare-Bediako, the Vice-Chancellor of the UENR, reaffirmed the University’s commitment to creating an enabling environment for research, innovation and community engagement.

He said the University would continue to invest in strengthening research capacity, promoting interdisciplinary collaboration and building strategic partnerships to advance knowledge and sustainable development.

Professor Daniel Akoto Sarfo, the Dean of the School of Natural Resources, commended the University’s continuous support for research, innovation and academic excellence.

He said the School remained committed to producing graduates who were not only academically competent but also equipped with practical skills, ethical values and innovative thinking to contribute meaningfully to national development.

Ghana News.title: Dambai College of Education appoints new Principal and Vice Principal
Ghana News.content:
Dambai College of Education (DACE) has announced the appointment of Professor Inusah Hussein as the new Principal and Dr Fred Alpha Adams as Vice Principal.

This ushers in a new era of leadership aimed at strengthening academic excellence, innovation and institutional growth.

The appointments are expected to enhance the College’s strategic direction and reinforce its mandate of producing competent and professional teachers to support Ghana’s education sector.

The new management team is anticipated to provide visionary leadership by promoting quality teaching, research, innovation and effective administration while positioning the College as one of the leading teacher education institutions in the country.

Stakeholders, including members of the College community and education sector observers, have welcomed the appointments, describing them as timely and significant for the continued transformation of the institution.

They expressed confidence that Professor Hussein and Dr Adams possess the experience, competence and leadership qualities required to consolidate the gains made by the College and steer it towards greater academic and institutional achievements.

The stakeholders also commended the Minister for Education, Mr Haruna Iddrisu and the Director-General of the Ghana Tertiary Education Commission (GTEC), Professor Ahmed Jinapor Abdulai, for their commitment to strengthening governance, leadership and policy implementation in Ghana’s tertiary education sector.

They noted that effective collaboration between government agencies and tertiary institutions remained essential in improving the quality of teacher education and expanding opportunities for academic excellence.

Appreciation was further extended to the Governing Council of Dambai College of Education and the Search Committee for conducting what stakeholders described as a transparent and credible process that led to the appointment of the new Principal and Vice Principal.

The College community expressed optimism that the appointments would foster stronger collaboration among management, academic and non-academic staff, students, alumni and development partners in pursuing the institution’s long-term vision.

Traditional authorities and community leaders were also acknowledged for their continuous support towards the growth and development of the College and the Dambai community.

Among those recognised were Daasebre Atamafowiese Bonja II, Overlord of the Chonke Traditional Area and Nana Kwaku Beyennor II, Nifahene of the Chonke Traditional Area, whose contributions have been instrumental in promoting peace, unity and educational development within the municipality.

Stakeholders emphasised that the partnership between the College, traditional authorities and the local community would remain vital in advancing infrastructure development, academic programmes and community engagement initiatives.

They expressed the hope that the new leadership would work closely with the Governing Council, faculty, staff, students, traditional authorities, government agencies and other stakeholders to improve academic standards, strengthen research and innovation, expand partnerships and create an enabling environment for teaching and learning.

According to the stakeholders, the appointments present an important opportunity to strengthen institutional leadership, enhance governance and further establish Dambai College of Education as a centre of excellence in teacher education within the Oti Region and beyond.

They wished Professor Inusah Hussein and Dr Fred Alpha Adams success in their new roles and expressed confidence that their leadership would contribute significantly to the continued progress and reputation of the College.

Ghana News.title: Ho West chiefs and queens commend Volta Regional Minister for inclusive leadership
Ghana News.content:
The Congress of Paramount Chiefs and Queens of the Ho West District has commended Mr James Gunu, Volta Regional Minister, for his inclusive and participatory leadership style, which it said had fostered unity and collaboration among stakeholders in the region.

The Congress expressed satisfaction with the Minister’s approach to governance and his ability to bring together key stakeholders behind a common development agenda for the Volta Region.

The commendation was made during a courtesy call on the Minister at the Residency by a delegation of the Congress led by its President, Togbega Atsridom V, Paramount Chief of the Kpedze Traditional Area.

The delegation congratulated Mr Gunu on what it described as his exemplary leadership and commitment to the development of the region.

The Congress noted that the Minister’s dedication to the progress of the Volta region was encouraging and deserved the support of citizens and stakeholders.

It said the inclusive approach being adopted by the Minister was critical to accelerating development and addressing the socio-economic challenges confronting communities across the region.

The delegation therefore urged residents to rally behind the Minister and support efforts aimed at achieving sustainable growth and improving living conditions.

The chiefs and queens also engaged the Minister on a number of development concerns affecting their traditional areas, including the poor condition of some road networks.

They appealed for urgent intervention to improve the roads and help prevent accidents and other challenges associated with deteriorating infrastructure.

Discussions also focused on strategies to strengthen collaboration between traditional authorities and government institutions to promote sustainable economic and social development in the region.

The delegation further presented a formal request for the partitioning of the Ho West District, arguing that the current geographical size of the district was too large and placed a strain on administrative resources, thereby slowing development efforts.

Mr Gunu welcomed the delegation and expressed appreciation for the visit and the confidence reposed in him.

He commended the Congress for its commitment to partnering with the government to advance the socio-economic development of the Volta region.

The Minister reaffirmed the commitment of the Volta Regional Coordinating Council to working closely with traditional authorities to drive sustainable development and improve the livelihoods of people across the region.

World.title: Trump pleads not guilty to 34 felony counts
World.content:
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.

Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.

However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”

Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.

The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”

Trump is now in Manhattan ahead of the arraignment. A grand jury indicted the former president last week.

The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.

The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.

Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.

World.title: Russian authorities detain suspect over St. Petersburg cafe blast
World.content:
A Ukrainian tank is seen near the frontline area amid the Russia-Ukraine war, in Bakhmut, Ukraine, on April 02. (Muhammed Enes Yildirim/Anadolu Agency/Getty Images)

The Ukrainian military has reported little change to the front lines but heavy fire from Russian forces at various parts of the front line in the Donetsk region.

The General Staff said that more than 45 enemy attacks had been repelled over the past day, with the focus on Lyman, Bakhmut, Avdiivka and Mariinka.

It said there were 17 air strikes and more than 20 strikes by multiple launch rocket systems.

“In the Bakhmut direction, the enemy is trying to take full control over the city of Bakhmut and continues to storm it,” the General Staff said.

West of the city, Ukrainian defense forces repelled about 20 enemy attacks, according to the General Staff.

Oleksandr Syrskyi, commander of Ukrainian Land Forces, posted on Telegram that in Bakhmut he had met with “soldiers and commanders who destroyed the myth of invincibility of the Wagner fighters and Russian paratroopers.”

“The enemy is weakening and trying to cover up its failures with new fakes about the capture of Bakhmut,” Syrskyi said.

Syrskyi referenced the possibility of a future counter-offensive, saying that “the forward movement of our entire army depends on what every soldier is doing right now on their section of the front.”

Some of the most intense fighting is to the northwest and west of the city of Donetsk – as the Russians continue months-long efforts to dislodge Ukrainian defenses in Avdiivka and Mariinka. The General Staff said that some 20 assaults had been repelled.

“There are also some operational successes of our military in the Donetsk area. Our military have taken some positions. They have taken a more strategic and favourable position,” said Oleksii Dmytrashkivskyi, spokesperson for the military in that zone.

He also noted that Russian special forces had been introduced in the area.

“The enemy is trying to attack our positions between Avdiivka and Marinka. These attempts do not stop. It should be noted that the enemy has suffered quite significant losses,” Dmytrashkivskyi said.

He also claimed that the Russians “don’t have the same amount of equipment and, as they themselves say, they are on a ‘diet’ of ammunition for assaults.”

Social media video showed both sides engaged in heavy fire in the Avdiivka area, which the Russians have surrounded on three sides.

Denis Pushilin, the leader of the self-declared Donetsk People’s Republic, claimed that Russian forces were still advancing in the Avdiivka direction.

“It is still premature to speak of encirclement, but the situation is being created, if not critical, then extremely difficult for the enemy… After clearing Kamianka, our units are moving further. There are difficulties both with the terrain, which must also be overcome, and there are also similarities with weather conditions. But these difficulties are mutual — both for the enemy and for us,” Pushilin said.

World.title: Suspected Chinese spy balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing
World.content:
Washington —

The Chinese spy balloon that transited the US earlier this year was able to capture imagery and collect some signals intelligence from US military sites, a source familiar with the matter tells CNN.

The balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing in real time, the source said, and the US government still does not know for sure whether the Chinese government could wipe the balloon’s data as it received it. That raises questions about whether there is intelligence the balloon was able to gather that the US still doesn’t know about.

Still, the intelligence community has not been overly concerned about the information the balloon was able to gather, the person said, because it is not much more sophisticated than what Chinese satellites are able to glean as they orbit over similar locations.

A US intelligence official told CNN on Monday that “although analysis of the wreckage of the High Altitude Balloon remains ongoing, thus far, its flight over the United States does not appear to have provided critical new insights to the People’s Republic of China.”

The US also knew what the balloon’s path would be and was able to protect sensitive sites and censor some signals before the balloon was able to pick them up, officials have said.

As CNN has reported, the US intelligence community last year developed a method of tracking what it says is a fleet of these Chinese balloons operating across the globe, controlled by the Chinese military.

The FBI is still examining the balloon, but so far officials have been able to glean additional information about how the device worked, including the algorithms used for the balloon’s software and how it is powered and designed.

CNN has reached out to the National Security Council at the White House and the Pentagon for comment. NBC was first to report on the new intelligence.

Video Ad Feedback Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33 • Source: CNN Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33

The balloon first crossed into US airspace over Alaska in late January before passing through Canada and down into Montana, where it hovered for a few days, leading the US to believe it was trying to surveil sensitive military sites, like Malmstrom Air Force Base in Montana. It was eventually shot down by the US off the East Coast on February 4, and the incident further escalated tensions between Washington and Beijing, including the postponement of a diplomatic visit by US Secretary of State Antony Blinken to China.

A senior State Department official said in February that, as the balloon floated across the US, it “was capable of conducting signals intelligence collection operations.”

Gen. Glen VanHerck, the commander of US Northern Command and NORAD, said at the time that the US “did not assess” that the balloon “presented a significant collection hazard beyond what already exists in actionable technical means from the Chinese.”

The surveillance program, which includes a number of similar balloons, is in part run out of the small Chinese province of Hainan, officials told CNN. The US does not know the precise size of the fleet of Chinese surveillance balloons, but sources tell CNN that the program has conducted at least two dozen missions over at least five continents in recent years.

Roughly half a dozen of those flights have been within US airspace, although not necessarily over US territory, according to one official familiar with the intelligence.

China has maintained that the balloon was actually just a weather balloon thrown off course, and the US has been assessing the possibility that it was not deliberately maneuvered into the continental US by the Chinese government, CNN has reported.

Still, China did maintain some ability to maneuver the balloon, officials believe. And once the balloon was over Montana, China appeared to take advantage of its position to loiter over sensitive sites and try to collect intelligence.

This story has been updated with additional reporting.

World.title: Beijing promised to 'fight back' over Taiwan leader's US visit. But this time it has more to lose
World.content:
Hong Kong —

An anticipated meeting between Taiwan’s President Tsai Ing-wen and US House Speaker Kevin McCarthy in California this week has sparked concerns of a repeat of the pressure campaign China launched last year when then-Speaker Nancy Pelosi visited Taipei.

At that time, Beijing encircled the island democracy with unprecedented military drills – firing multiple missiles into its surrounding waters and sending dozens of warplanes speeding across a sensitive median line dividing the Taiwan Strait.

It also cut off contact with the United States over a number of issues from military matters to combating climate change, in retaliation for what it viewed as a violation of its sovereignty.

This time, Beijing has already threatened to “resolutely fight back” if a Tsai-McCarthy meeting goes ahead.

Video Ad Feedback See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32 • Source: CNN See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32

It also slammed Washington for allowing Tsai to stopover in the US while en route to and from official visits in Central America, warning it could lead to “serious” confrontation between the two powers.

A defiant Tsai staked out her own ground, pledging as she took off on her 10-day trip not to let “external pressure” stop Taiwan from connecting with the world and like-minded democracies.

But the optics of the meeting, taking place in California and not Taiwan, and its timing – at a particularly thorny moment in China’s foreign relations and ahead of a presidential election in Taiwan that could reset the tone of its relationship with Beijing – may see Beijing tread more carefully this time, or at least not escalate further, analysts say.

“This puts the burden on China not to overreact, because any overreaction is only going to push China further away from the world,” said Yun Sun, director of the China Program at the Stimson Center think tank in Washington.

That doesn’t mean, however, that Beijing won’t be closely watching Tsai’s movements as it calibrates its response – and decides how much military might to flex over her meeting with an American lawmaker on American soil.

The opacity of China’s system – and the potential for competing interests within its vast bureaucracy – also make it difficult to accurately predict its response.

“Every time Taiwan does anything that China doesn’t like, the Chinese react with their own military coercion,” Sun said. But in the current situation, “they have to consider the consequences of overreaction,” she added.

House Speaker Kevin McCarthy talks to reporters at the Capitol in Washington on March 24, 2023. J. Scott Applewhite/AP

Rising pressure

The expected meeting, which McCarthy’s office announced earlier this week would take place on Wednesday, also comes at a precarious moment in US-China relations.

Washington and Beijing are struggling to stabilize their communication amid flaring tensions over issues from a downed suspected Chinese surveillance balloon to semiconductor supply chains – raising the stakes of potential damage to that relationship if Beijing lashes out as it did when Tsai met Pelosi.

Taiwan is still feeling the fallout of that response last August, with Chinese military forces now regularly making incursions over what had previously been an informal but largely respected border of control between Beijing and Taipei in the Taiwan Strait. Taiwan’s official Central News Agency also reported Monday that Tsai would meet with McCarthy, citing Tsai’s presidential office.

Video Ad Feedback See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05 • Source: CNN See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05

But a meeting between Tsai and the leader of the Republican majority in the US House of Representatives, who ranks second in line to the Presidency, would mark another symbolic moment for Taiwan and the US, which only maintain unofficial ties.

For Tsai, who is entering the final year of her two-term presidency, “it’s clearly a capstone event,” according to Wen-Ti Sung, a political scientist at the Australian National University’s Taiwan Studies Program. “She has this image as the Taiwanese president who has taken US-Taiwan relations to new heights, and who … has been able to give Taiwan almost unprecedented international visibility,” he said.

That increased visibility – and enhanced cooperation with the US – has followed China’s mounting pressure on the island, which sits fewer than 110 miles (177 kilometers) from the mainland coast.

China’s Communist Party claims the self-governing island democracy as its own despite never having controlled it, and has vowed to take the island, by force if necessary.

The party has undertaken a sweeping expansion of its military capabilities over the past decade under leader Xi Jinping – and ramped up its pervasive economic, diplomatic and military pressure on Taiwan.

That’s driven concerns, among some in Washington, that Beijing is preparing for an invasion, though China’s official language still suggests that scenario is not its preferred option for achieving the claimed goal of “reunification.”

It is those pressures – and how to support Taiwan against unilateral actions by Beijing – that are likely to be on the table when Tsai, McCarthy and a bipartisan group of US lawmakers sit down on Wednesday.

Congress has been a pillar of increasing American support for Taiwan in recent years. Lawmakers regularly visit the island and drive bipartisan legislation enhancing support and cooperation.

While the US switched its diplomatic relations to Beijing decades ago, it maintains unofficial ties with Taiwan and is bound by law to provide the democratic island with the means to defend itself.

Under Washington’s longstanding “One China” policy, the US acknowledges China’s position that Taiwan is part of China, but has never officially recognized Beijing’s claim to the island of 23 million.

Though McCarthy does not have Pelosi’s decades-long record of advocacy regarding China, the California Republican is now a leading voice pushing for closer scrutiny of Beijing, and meeting Tsai could help him to burnish that image.

Last month, McCarthy told reporters that meeting Tsai in the US would not impact whether he travels to Taiwan in the future – something he had earlier said he wanted to do.

Fighter jets of the Chinese People's Liberation Army Eastern Theater Command conduct joint combat training exercises around Taiwan on August 7, 2022 in this photo released by Xinhua News Agency. Gong Yulong/Xinhua/AP

Beijing watching

A meeting in California, on US soil, is widely seen as less likely to provoke Beijing than a McCarthy visit to Taiwan.

Pelosi’s trip – the first from a lawmaker of that rank to the island in 25 years – generated a fever pitch of nationalist and anti-US rhetoric in mainland China.

This time, so far, domestic conversation in China’s heavily controlled media sphere has been significantly muted.

But the stakes remain high – including for Beijing itself – over how it responds, analysts say.

As Taiwan prepares for a presidential election in January, a fierce response could push voters away from Taiwan’s main opposition party Kuomintang (KMT), widely seen as more friendly toward Beijing.

It could also jar with another high profile trip happening now: a tour of mainland China from former Taiwan president and senior KMT member Ma Ying-jeou, the first visit from a current or former Taiwan leader since the end of the Chinese Civil War in 1949.

Ma’s tour is a “once in a half a century opportunity to send a conciliatory message between the two sides, Beijing shouldn’t want to tank that,” said Sung, the political scientist.

China is also acutely aware that its actions toward Taiwan are under a significantly brighter global spotlight following the invasion of Ukraine by Russian President Vladimir Putin, a close diplomatic partner of Xi. Putin’s rhetoric over Ukraine has echoes of how Xi speaks of Taiwan.

Beijing has recently sought to position itself as an agent of peace in that conflict – especially as it aims to repair frayed ties with Europe.

This week, as Tsai is expected to meet with McCarthy, French President Emmanuel Macron and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen will head to China – an important opportunity that Xi may not want to overshadow with military posturing.

An aggressive response also risks stoking confrontation with the US, not yet six months after Xi and US President Joe Biden called to enhance communication during a face-to-face meeting in Bali.

“(A less overtly aggressive response) would imply that Beijing does not wish to escalate tension with the US to a level that can risk getting out of hand,” said Steve Tsang, director of the SOAS China Institute in London.

“A reset in US-China ties is not on the agenda, but an easing of tension is not beyond the realm of possibility.”

World.title: Sudan’s army claims control of major highway linking Khartoum and el-Obeid
World.content:
Capture of Al Sadarat highway will help the Sudanese army block the RSF’s push to seize el-Obeid in North Kordofan.

The Sudanese army has announced that it has regained full control of a major highway linking the capital, Khartoum, with el-Obeid, a city that has been under siege by the rival paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (RSF).

The capture of Al Sadarat highway on Sunday will help the Sudanese army move troops, weapons, fuel and supplies, and will also block the RSF’s push to seize el-Obeid, the capital of North Kordofan state.

About half a million people are trapped in the city, where the United Nations has warned of a humanitarian catastrophe, with residents facing intense RSF drone attacks.

In a statement on Sunday, the Sudanese army said it had recaptured cities and towns between Khartoum and el-Obied following two days of fierce battles with the RSF, which controlled the highway.

The attacks marked the first major offensive against the paramilitary in months.

The army said its troops retook the areas of Um Qurfa and Jarigakh after operations that “inflicted heavy losses in lives and equipment [of RSF fighters], forcing them to flee”.

“With this victory, the forces have taken control of the export route of Omdurman Al-Abyd”, the army said, referring to the Al Sadarat highway.

Improved humanitarian access

Al Jazeera’s AlMigdad Alruhaid said the capture of the highway restores “a direct connection between the capital and Kordofan for the first time in months”.

“This is significant because the highway is a key military supply route,” Alruhaid said.

“It allows the army to move fuel, troops and equipment more quickly to el-Obeid instead of relying on the longer route through the White Nile State. And the move also reduces pressure on el-Obeid, which has been largely isolated by RSF positions, while potentially opening an important trade route for livestock and agricultural products from the Kordofan region,” he added.



“For civilians, securing this road could also improve humanitarian access to communities affected by this ongoing war.”

The RSF had controlled most of the 350km (217-mile) strategic highway since April 2023, when the conflict between the Sudanese army and the RSF erupted due to disagreements about integrating the paramilitary force into the national army.

Losing control of the route will hinder the RSF’s drive to take el-Obeid – a city whose capture would give the paramilitary force control of all of western Sudan.

The conflict has killed an estimated 40,000 people, according to the World Health Organization, and forced more than 14 million people to flee their homes.

In el-Obeid, UN Women said last week that women and girls “now face an impossible choice over something as basic as a bucket of water: risk a drone strike by collecting it in daylight, or risk rape by waiting until dark”.

It added that sexual violence has been used as a weapon throughout Sudan’s three-year war, with testimonies describing rape committed in front of family members alongside brutal physical abuse.

World.title: Russia and Ukraine trade attacks, killing 10, including child in Chernihiv
World.content:
Kyiv says Russian strikes killed six, including a child at a supermarket, as Moscow says Ukrainian strikes killed four.

Russian forces have killed at least six people in Ukraine, according to officials, after launching ballistic missile attacks on the capital, Kyiv, and strikes on other regions, including a supermarket in the northern city of Chernihiv.

The attacks on Sunday came as Russian officials said that Moscow-occupied areas of Ukraine had also come under fire, with four people killed in a Ukrainian drone strike on the occupied city of Horlivka.

Ukraine’s air ⁠force said Russia had launched seven ballistic missiles and 136 drones at Ukraine overnight. Kyiv, Chernihiv, Zaporizhzhia and Kharkiv cities were all hit.

In northern Chernihiv, officials said a Russian drone hit a supermarket, killing two people, including a nine-year-old girl, and wounding 25 others.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy described the attack as a “deeply cynical drone strike on an ordinary supermarket”.

In the eastern city of Kharkiv, one person was killed and 16 others required medical attention after a daytime drone attack, the local mayor said.

“This is deliberate Russian terror with absolutely no military justification,” Zelenskyy said.

Separately, Regional Governor Ivan Fedorov said a glide bomb attack killed one person and wounded six in the southern city of Zaporizhzhia, which has been under heavy bombardment in recent months.

In Kyiv, Mayor Vitali Klitschko said one blaze had broken out on the seventh and eighth floors of a multistorey apartment block in a central district after the overnight missile attack. Three people were wounded in the capital, and images released by the state emergency services showed vehicles in flames.



In Sloviansk, one of several targets of Russia’s slow advance through eastern Ukraine’s Donetsk region, the national oil and gas company Naftogaz said two of its employees died in a Russian attack while trying to help residents affected by an earlier strike.

In Horlivka, a city in the Russian-occupied part of the Donetsk region, Russian-installed Mayor Ivan Prikhodko said four civilians had been killed in a Ukrainian drone strike. Prikhodko later said a Ukrainian drone hit an emergency vehicle, injuring three medics and another resident.

At least 12 people, including two children, were also hurt in a Ukrainian drone attack on Belgorod, a Russian city close to the Ukrainian border, Russian authorities reported.

The attacks came a day after Moscow said a Ukrainian strike on a Russian-occupied town on the Azov Sea killed 12 people.

Both Moscow and Kyiv ‌deny targeting civilians in the war that started with Russia’s full-scale invasion of its neighbour in February 2022. But civilian casualty rates have climbed sharply in 2026 in both Russia and Ukraine, according to the United Nations.

Analysts say this is because of the growing use of short-range drones, glide bombs, and intensified strikes on infrastructure in both Russia and Ukraine.

UN officials say 1,396 civilians have been killed and 7,978 wounded in Ukraine in the first six months of 2026. In Russia, 250 civilians have been killed and 1,596 injured.

United States-led talks on ending fighting have stalled. The Kremlin occupies swaths of eastern and southern Ukraine and has repeatedly said it intends to seize the rest of eastern Ukraine by force.

World.title: Why Mali’s northern conflict has entered a dangerous new phase
World.content:
A separatist–al-Qaeda alliance has shifted the balance of power in northern Mali and complicated efforts to end the war.

Bamako, Mali – An unprecedented battlefield partnership between a separatist movement and an al-Qaeda affiliate has transformed the conflict in northern Mali, shifting the military balance and deepening divisions over how, if at all, the war can end.

When the Azawad Liberation Front (FLA) and Jama’at Nusrat al-Islam wal-Muslimin (JNIM) launched a joint offensive on April 25, 2026, the conflict entered a phase unlike any before.

A war that had long pitted the Malian state against multiple armed groups gave way to a coordinated campaign stretching from Kidal and Anefis to Tilemsi, Gao and Sevare, posing the most serious challenge to the Malian army in years and to Russia’s Africa Corps, the Kremlin-backed force that replaced the Wagner Group in Mali.

Since then, the fighting has been marked by simultaneous assaults, ambushes, drone strikes and attacks on military convoys, with all sides claiming significant battlefield gains.

Bamako says it is working to restore state authority and dismantle what it calls a “terrorist alliance” between the FLA and JNIM.

The FLA says it remains committed to independence for Azawad, the name separatists use for northern Mali, while JNIM portrays the war as part of a campaign to “liberate” Mali and overthrow the government, which it accuses of relying on Russian forces.

More significant than the offensive itself, however, is the unprecedented military cooperation between a nationalist separatist movement and an al-Qaeda affiliate.

Their political ambitions remain fundamentally different, yet their cooperation has already reshaped the conflict and could have far-reaching implications for security across the Sahel.



The partnership emerged after the collapse of the 2015 Algiers Peace Agreement, which sought to end years of fighting between Bamako and northern armed groups through greater decentralisation and political representation, but whose implementation repeatedly faltered.

Successive military coups after 2020 reshaped Mali’s political leadership and security strategy. The Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS) suspended Mali and imposed sanctions, while Russia deepened its military role by deploying the Wagner Group in late 2021.

After Russia folded the Wagner Group’s operations into the state-controlled Africa Corps, renewed fighting left neither the government nor northern armed groups able to impose a lasting settlement.

How the alliance took shape

On paper, cooperation between the FLA and JNIM appears unlikely. The FLA traces its roots to northern separatist movements that declared the independence of Azawad during the 2012 rebellion, a claim never recognised by the Malian state or the international community.

It presents itself as a secular nationalist movement seeking independence for Azawad, while JNIM seeks to overthrow governments it considers illegitimate and establish governance based on its interpretation of Islamic law.

Yet senior officials from both groups told Al Jazeera those ideological differences have been set aside to confront a common enemy.

Colonel Mohamed Issa, a senior FLA officer, said the movement remained committed to an independent Azawad, arguing that previous peace agreements repeatedly collapsed because successive governments in Bamako failed to honour them.

Negotiations, he said, would only be acceptable if they recognised Azawad’s right to separate.

Issa rejected suggestions of an ideological alliance, describing the relationship as a battlefield arrangement against a common enemy.

He said the JNIM-affiliated fighters operating alongside the FLA were exclusively Azawadis rather than members of the group’s wider regional network, arguing they were motivated primarily by defending their communities against the Malian army and what he described as Russian “mercenaries”.

Suleiman, a senior JNIM field commander who requested that only his first name be used for security reasons, described the relationship in broader terms.

He said the group approved operational coordination with the FLA after internal consultations because fighters on both sides largely came from “one people” caught up in the same conflict and because their liberation goals had become “relatively unified”.



He also claimed the FLA had accepted Islamic legal arbitration by local religious scholars, one of JNIM’s core objectives, a point the FLA itself did not raise. Bamako, meanwhile, has described the relationship as a “JNIM/FLA terrorist alliance” that threatens Mali’s sovereignty.

The differing accounts illustrate both the strength and the fragility of the arrangement. For now, shared battlefield interests appear to outweigh ideological differences. Whether that remains true as the conflict evolves is far less certain.

A shifting balance of power

The partnership has altered not only the battlefield but the way the war is fought.

FLA officials say working alongside JNIM has enabled both groups to divide responsibilities and pool expertise in attacks on military bases and supply convoys.

Bamako disputes casualty figures released by the armed groups and insists its forces retain the initiative. Even so, the conflict has become markedly more sophisticated, with simultaneous attacks across distant locations, engagements lasting several days and ambushes targeting reinforcements before they reach the front lines.

Drones have assumed an increasingly prominent role, serving not only as reconnaissance platforms but increasingly as strike weapons against vehicles and military positions. Malian forces, backed by Russia’s Africa Corps, continue to rely heavily on air power, yet months of sustained fighting suggest neither side has secured a decisive advantage.

The war economy

Long-established financing and trafficking networks continue to sustain both sides.

JNIM sources describe a funding model built on regional commercial networks, organised zakat collections and resources accumulated over years, including proceeds linked to earlier al-Qaeda kidnapping-for-ransom operations.

The FLA says it relies primarily on donations organised by tribal leaders, traders and community associations.

Officials from both groups also acknowledged that individuals linked to the movements participate in illicit economies, including trafficking across the Sahara, although the extent to which those activities finance the war remains difficult to verify.

Weapons have proved as important as funding. Arms have flowed across the Sahel since the collapse of Libya in 2011, providing armed groups with a steady source of equipment.

The latest fighting has opened another supply channel: weapons and military vehicles captured from Malian forces now form an increasingly important part of both groups’ arsenals.

Can either side win?

There is little to suggest the conflict is nearing an end.

The Malian army retains a clear advantage in air power, backed by Russia’s Africa Corps. Yet the FLA and JNIM continue to mount coordinated operations across much of northern Mali.

The military standoff reflects a wider political deadlock. Bamako remains committed to preserving Mali’s territorial integrity, the FLA insists on independence for Azawad and JNIM continues to seek the overthrow of the government.



None has shifted position since the latest fighting began, and nothing on the battlefield has yet forced any of them to do so.

Those competing objectives also cast doubt on how long the two groups can continue fighting together. Their partnership rests on a common enemy rather than a shared political vision, making its future uncertain.

A war without an endgame

Three months into the latest offensive, northern Mali remains locked in a conflict with no obvious end in sight. The partnership between the FLA and JNIM has reshaped the military landscape, while Bamako continues to reject any outcome that could weaken Mali’s territorial integrity.

What began as a confrontation between the state and separate armed movements has evolved into a conflict shaped by competing visions of sovereignty, separatism, rule by al-Qaeda-linked armed groups and the involvement of external powers.

Unless those competing ambitions – territorial unity, independence and regime change – are addressed alongside the fighting, a negotiated settlement is likely to remain elusive.

Whatever happens next, the partnership forged in April 2026 has already changed the course of the war in northern Mali. Whether it endures or fractures under the weight of its competing ambitions, it has created a new military and political reality whose consequences are likely to extend well beyond Mali’s borders.

World.title: Macron calls crisis meeting as wildfires threaten Bordeaux and heatwave looms
World.content:
French President Emmanuel Macron will a hold a crisis cabinet meeting on Monday as wildfires close in on the south-western city of Bordeaux.

Another heatwave is set to complicate efforts to tackle the expanding blaze, which is about 15km (9 miles) from Bordeaux, mayor Thomas Cazenave said. Earlier he said there were no plans to evacuate the population of about 850,000.

Wildfires have raged across Europe over the past week, primarily in France and Spain, where more than 330,000 people have been evacuated across both countries.

Macron said on Saturday that France would "rebuild" and his government would "be there for as long as is needed".

Tens of thousands of people have already been evacuated from Bordeaux's surrounding region, with France's Interior Minister Laurent NuÃ±ez saying the situation remained "very unfavourable" and the fire was "moving erratically" towards the city.

Weather forecasts for the country warned that temperatures could spike to 40C in some areas from Tuesday.

World.title: Netanyahu accuses NYC Mayor Mamdani of 'fomenting hate' after arrest threat
World.content:
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said he planned to attend the UN General Assembly in New York City this autumn, despite the city's mayor, Zohran Mamdani, making threats to arrest him.

Mamdani walked back that threat last week, acknowledging he lacked the legal power to arrest Netanyahu on a warrant issued by the International Criminal Court, the world's top war-crimes court.

The Israeli leader told Fox News on Sunday that he was "not concerned" about Mamdani's previous pledge and accused the mayor of "fomenting hate".

"He's supposed to be the mayor of all New Yorkers, Jews, Christians, Muslims, everyone, but he's trying to turn one group against the other," Netanyahu said.

Netanyahu referenced a pair of stabbings in New York on Thursday, in which a suspect stabbed a Jewish man and an Asian man just blocks apart.

The suspect allegedly shouted the phrase "Allahu akbar" while committing the stabbings, according to police. He has been charged with hate crimes relating to each victim.

Both men survived the attacks, which drew condemnations from the city's Jewish and Asian American leaders.

In the aftermath, Netanyahu said Jewish New Yorkers were "afraid right now."

The mayor's office did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
