World.title: Runaway train in Hunter Valley 'worst-case scenario' for rail safety
World.content:
Questions continue to be asked about how a fully laden coal train was allowed to roll without a crew for several kilometres through the NSW Hunter Valley.

An expert in transport management says the runaway train could have caused an extremely serious accident.

The ABC has been told the Pacific National coal train began rolling downhill with no-one on board during a crew change in the early hours of Saturday morning at Camberwell, between Singleton and Muswellbrook.

University of Sydney senior lecturer in Transport Management, Geoffrey Clifton, told ABC Newcastle Breakfast such incidents were "quite rare" outside of a maintenance setting.

"The worst-case scenario you can have on the network is a runaway train for obvious reasons," he said.

" The question is why wasn't there enough braking power … either the brakes failed, or there weren't enough brakes put on in the first place. "

The train stopped near a level crossing at Glennies Creek. (ABC Upper Hunter: Courtney Yeandle)

Australian Rail Track Corporation documents show Pacific National coal trains operating on the Hunter Valley line are typically between 1.296 and 1.541 kilometres long, and include between 82 and 96 wagons.

The unstaffed train travelled through at least one level crossing, but Steve Muscat, a director and principal engineer at consultancy Rail Confidence, told ABC Newcastle Mornings the boom gates would have come down.

"Thankfully they are automated and activated by electrical track signals," he said.

"It certainly would have activated."

Experts say level crossings would have been activated by a runaway train. (ABC Upper Hunter: Courtney Yeandle)

Dr Clifton said coal trains had a brake on each carriage that connected with one control system.

"It's possible that the brakes failed somewhere along the line, which would lead to a runaway train," he said.

"It's also possible that the brakes weren't applied properly and that's where the investigation's going to look."

The Office of the National Rail Safety Regulator (ONRSR) said in a statement it was investigating the incident.

"The ONRSR has … deployed a team of rail safety officers, investigators and rolling stock specialists to the Hunter Valley where a fully loaded coal train has been involved in a runaway incident," it said.

"In addition to assessing and inspecting the scene, ONRSR is seeking information and documentation from the rail transport operator."

Pacific National, which hauls coal between the Hunter Valley and the Port of Newcastle, said in a statement it was taking the incident "extremely seriously".

Pacific National hauls coal from mines in the Hunter Valley. (ABC Rural)

The company said it would be inappropriate to comment on the incident or speculate on the potential cause.

Muswellbrook Shire Mayor Jeff Drayton said he would be meeting with employees to discuss the incident.

"At this stage, it's unclear if it was a human or mechanical error, or a combination of both," he said.

"Investigations are ongoing."

The ABC has been told the train travelled at speeds in excess of 60 kilometres per hour before coming to a stop several kilometres away at Glennies Creek.

Geoffrey Clifton says the train was likely stopped by a slight incline in the track. (ABC Upper Hunter: Courtney Yeandle)

Dr Clifton said the natural incline of the track was likely to have eventually brought the train to a standstill.

"It would've gone until something stopped it, usually another hill or if it triggers a derailing point," he said.

"If something goes wrong on the track,s it can be quite serious, which is why the [ONRSR] is going to be investigating this very closely.

World.title: How Victorian Labor's leadership challenge could play out
World.content:
Victorian Labor MPs are pushing to topple their leader quickly and cleanly this week, but it might not be a simple process.

Premier Jacinta Allan has declared she will fight it out, and that act could force the party through a month-long process involving a vote of the membership.

Here's how we got here, and how a leadership challenge could play out.

How did Labor get here?

Ms Allan has been struggling in the polls.

Victorian premier's future in doubt A delegation of Labor ministers and MPs has met with Jacinta Allan to urge her to step down, but the Victorian premier has vowed to fight any leadership challenge.

With the November election just four months away, she's been under intense pressure over alleged corruption in the state's taxpayer-funded infrastructure program.

The premier has refused calls to launch a royal commission, but a growing cohort of MPs believe the government must launch an inquiry to subdue the public backlash.

A cross-factional delegation of nine ministers and MPs on Monday told Ms Allan she had lost majority support of the caucus and urged her to step down.

Deputy Premier Ben Carroll has since declared his intention to run for the leadership.

Could Jacinta Allan step aside?

Ms Allan is so far refusing to resign, backed in by her supporters including senior ministers.

She wrote to state Labor secretary Steve Staikos on Monday morning, asking the party to prepare for a contested leadership ballot.

"I also wish to formally notify you of my intention to be a candidate for the leadership of the state parliamentary Labor Party, in the event that an election is required," Ms Allan wrote.

This would be a diabolical and drawn-out result for the party, and a pathway that agitators were hoping to avoid.

Her resignation would allow Mr Carroll to fill the vacancy.

Jacinta Allan has told Victorian Labor she's not going anywhere. (ABC News: Danielle Bonica)

In the event that Ms Allan does not step aside, a spill motion is expected to be moved at Tuesday's caucus meeting in parliament at 10am.

More than half the parliamentary party would need to vote together to spill the leadership.

What happens if there is a contested leadership ballot?

While a leader typically won't contest a spill if it gets up convincingly, Ms Allan has vowed to throw her hat in the ring.

That would force the party to put the ballot out to the entire membership over four weeks.

Nominations would open within 24 hours and close three days later, though caucus can vary the nomination period if more than 80 per cent of MPs agree.

Those nominating for leader would need signatures backing them from at least 20 per cent of caucus, and could spend the next four weeks in campaign mode to win over the membership.

Ben Carroll says he told Jacinta Allan in person about his intention to run for her position. (ABC News)

In the meantime, Labor MPs would elect an interim leader who cannot be a candidate in the ballot.

The count would be declared by the party's administrative committee.

Given Labor is in government, with a state election just four months away, this is widely viewed as a nightmare scenario.

Is a coup guaranteed?

Ms Allan's internal backers insist she will fight on like she declared, and that the claims she has lost support remain untested.

One of her supporters described the move against her as a game of Russian roulette.

Supporters were hoping to see moves against her fall apart.

But with a delegation informing her that she no longer enjoyed majority support and her deputy declaring his intentions, MPs expect the challenge to go ahead.

Jacinta Allan has been told she no longer enjoys the support of the majority of her MPs. (ABC News)

It is not guaranteed that Ms Allan would lose a spill motion, given support remains untested, but MPs broadly believe she no longer has the numbers.

MPs have also received calls in an attempt to shore up an emphatic result against Ms Allan to show her she must step aside.

There is a lingering belief among agitators that losing a spill motion could convince her to spare the party, despite her insistence she will fight it out.

Ben Carroll says fellow MPs encouraged him to nominate for the leadership. (AAP: Joel Carrett)

MPs had earlier encouraged Mr Carroll to contest.

"It is clear that the premier has lost the majority of our caucus," Mr Carroll said in a statement on Monday morning.

"As such, I have since visited the premier to inform her that I will be nominating for the leadership of the Labor Party.

"This decision is not easy, but the stakes at the upcoming election are simply too high."

World.title: Yung Filly tells rape trial 'vibes were good' between him and alleged victim
World.content:
Warning: This story contains details some readers may find distressing.

UK social media celebrity and rapper Yung Filly has said the "vibes were good" between himself and a young fan he is accused of raping and violently assaulting at his Perth hotel, and that he "fancied her".

The content creator and musician, whose real name is Andres Felipe Valencia Barrientos, is on trial accused of assaulting the young fan after a nightclub concert in Perth's northern suburbs in September 2024.

The woman, who had just turned 20 at the time, alleges Mr Barrientos raped her multiple times and repeatedly assaulted her, including trying to choke her, after she went back to his hotel room in Perth's CBD.

The 30-year-old denies all 10 charges against him.

Andres Felipe Valencia Barrientos denied putting his hand down the alleged victim's pants while at the Hillarys venue. (ABC News: David Weber)

The young fan testified she had consensual sex with Mr Barrientos, before the encounter turned violent and she told him to stop.

Complainant approached accused

Taking the witness stand this morning, Mr Barrientos said he "fancied" the complainant when she approached him at the concert venue, Bar1 in Hillarys, by leaning over the barrier separating the VIP area from the dance floor.

She later gained access to the VIP area and they began chatting, the court heard.

Yung Filly started out as a YouTube sensation and went on to establish a successful music career. (Facebook: Yung Filly)

Speaking in a loud, confident voice with a strong east London accent, Mr Barrientos initially denied any physical contact had taken place between the pair in the VIP area, but then said "I recall putting my hand on her waist".

However, he denied he had put his hands down her pants and touched her breast.

"That did not happen," he said in response to questioning from his barrister, David Edwardson KC.

How starstruck fan's dream unravelled into UK celebrity's rape trial He is a famous YouTuber. She was a young fan with a 'celebrity crush'. Here's a recap of the first week of Yung Filly's rape trial.

He said the "vibes were good" when they arrived at the hotel, although his security guard had taken the young woman's phone off her, which he said was "standard practice" to "ensure our privacy".

In a dramatic start to the day's testimony, a juror was discharged on medical grounds, and security was markedly increased in the court after what Judge Linda Black said was a "breach" of court protocols published on social media that had been brought to her attention over the weekend.

Only those approved by the judge were allowed to enter the main courtroom, which included media, and family members and friends of both Mr Barrientos and the complainant present.

A second courtroom was established with a live stream of court proceedings to accommodate others who had come to watch Mr Barrientos testify, including a large contingent of Yung Filly fans, many of them young men.

Guards checked people's phones before entry, and Judge Black assured the jury "everyone in the video courtroom will have security watching them carefully".

Mr Barrientos is expected to continue his testimony for much of the rest of the day.

World.title: 'The diggers have arrived': Works begin at Hobart's $1.13b stadium site
World.content:
The Tasmanian government says plans for a new Hobart stadium have reached a significant milestone with the start of preparatory earthworks at Macquarie Point.

The stadium is a key requirement for the entry of the Tasmania Devils into the AFL competition.

Jeremy Rockliff had a go on the tools at the commencement of works at the site. (ABC News: Mitchell Woolnough)

The project, which was approved by parliament last year, has polarised the community because of its $1.13 billion price tag and its location in the heart of Hobart's historic CBD.

While construction of the facility is still a year away, trucks have started shifting huge amounts of soil from the site to local waste facilities.

An image posted to Jeremy Rockliff's social media welcoming the start of earthworks. (Facebook: Jeremy Rockliff)

"There's about 100,000 cubic metres to be moved off this site," Hazell Bros managing director Geoffrey Hazell said.

" So, there should be a truck leaving here every eight minutes. "

An render of what the stadium is expected to look like when finished. (Supplied: Cox Architecture)

Premier Jeremy Rockliff described the occasion as a "new era of economic opportunity for Tasmania".

"Clearly the diggers have arrived, the builders are here and [it's] time to get on with the job," Mr Rockliff said.

"And it's so important for not only … bringing to life a four-decade-old dream when it comes to our own Tasmanian team … but also the significant opportunity economically [for] our visitor economy and all associated with such a significant event here today."

An artist's impression of the indoor playing area at the Macquarie Point stadium, during a football match. (Supplied: MPDC)

The Tasmania Devils club, which recently selected Ken Hinkley as its inaugural coach, will enter the AFL in 2028.

The stadium is not expected to be completed until late 2030, meaning the Devils will initially play Hobart-based games at Bellerive Oval.

Loading...

Two firms are currently vying for the right to build the stadium: Besix Watpac and Constructure Joint Venture, a collaboration between WeBuild and China Construction Oceania.

Both firms are expected to submit their bids to the Macquarie Point Development Corporation (MPDC) next month.

"They'll tell us their team, their capacity, their experience, their methodology, and they'll give us a target price for delivering this exciting project," MPDC chief executive Anne Beach said.

A preferred contractor is then likely to be chosen in October.

"We'll go through a pretty hefty assessment process and then we'll move into what we refer to as stage two, and that is when the price is locked down and a lot more local engagement is just cemented," Ms Beach said.

The final contract is expected to be signed at the end of the year.

An artist's impression of the Macquarie Point stadium entry gate 1 and retail precinct. (Supplied: Mac Point Site Master Plan Report)

WeBuild charges 'not a reason for us to not proceed'

WeBuild has come under scrutiny in recent months following revelations it is facing charges interstate relating to alleged workplace safety breaches.

SafeWork NSW has launched two separate criminal proceedings against the Italian infrastructure firm in the NSW Industrial Court alleging it put several workers at risk of death or serious injury.

WeBuild has pleaded not guilty to the charges.

Treasurer Eric Abetz (left) was at the site for the occasion. (ABC News: Mitchell Woolnough)

An artist's impression of Macquarie Point stadium entry gate 4 in Hobart. (Supplied: Mac Point Site Master Plan Report)

The Tasmanian Greens and independent MP Kristie Johnston have previously said WeBuild should have disclosed the charges during the expression of interest process, and that it should not have been selected as a tenderer.

Ms Beach said today WeBuild had declared all it was required to and that there was no reason to remove it from the process.

"The things that have been raised are allegations … are untested before the court," she said.

"They are not a reason for us to not proceed with a qualified party for a project in a different jurisdiction for a different project and they're untested in the court.

"So we're comfortable that we've gone through a thorough assessment process."

World.title: Alan Jones ‘anxious to have his day in court’ as push for trial delay abandoned
World.content:
NationalNSWCourts Alan Jones ‘anxious to have his day in court’ as push for trial delay abandoned Clare Sibthorpe July 27, 2026 — 3:03pm Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Remove items from your saved list to add more. Share A A A

Alan Jones’ defence team has abandoned a push to delay his indecent assault and sexual touching trial as he is “anxious to have his day in court”. Last week, Local Court Judge Glenn Walsh said the former broadcaster’s lawyers had filed a motion seeking either a temporary halt in the proceedings, known as a stay, or an order that certain evidence from devices seized from the former broadcaster’s apartment was inadmissible in the trial slated to start on August 3. Alan Jones faces 22 charges relating to six complainants. Sam Mooy The motion sought a stay “until the Office of the Director of Public Prosecutions identifies by reference to items, dates and times the data from devices seized on 18 November 2024 from the accused’s home that is relied upon”. However, as pretrial arguments continued on Monday, defence barrister Gabrielle Bashir, SC, told Downing Centre Local Court they would no longer press ahead with the motion, saying the issue could be dealt with in the trial.



“In relation to the devices … the prosecution are declining to identify the subject matter,” Bashir said. “That is something that will be able to be dealt with in the case of proceedings. So your honour, it’s not our intention to move on that motion, which also was always a stay in relation to identification of the evidence.” Bashir said Jones was “anxious to have his day in court”. Alan Jones’ barrister Gabrielle Bashir, SC, and instructing solicitor Bryan Wrench at an earlier court appearance for Jones. Clare Sibthorpe “We want to start on August 3. I think all of the parties are moving for that to happen.”



Jones has pleaded not guilty to 22 charges of indecent assault and sexual touching relating to six complainants spanning from 2003 to 2020. Related Article Courts Dispute over seized devices may delay Alan Jones trial The 85-year-old is accused of committing the 22 crimes at his harbourside apartment, his farm at Fitzroy Falls in the Southern Highlands, and a lower north shore restaurant, among other venues in Sydney. In a pretrial decision last week the judge ruled in favour of the Crown and will allow prosecutors to rely on types of circumstantial evidence known as tendency and coincidence in the trial. Prosecutors will seek to prove Jones engaged in a pattern of behaviour when acting on his alleged sexual interest in “significantly younger” men.



But the judge made clear Jones “has the presumption of innocence” and “it is the prosecution that bear the onus of proof throughout, beyond reasonable doubt, for each element of each offence as charged”. The Crown expects to call 76 witnesses but that number could grow, the court earlier heard. Strike Force Bonnefin was established to investigate the former teacher and Wallabies coach following a major investigation by The Sydney Morning Herald and The Age. Jones’ trial is scheduled to run from August 3 until potentially December. Start the day with a summary of the day’s most important and interesting stories, analysis and insights.

World.title: What to stream this week: Our favourite romcom returns, plus five more picks
World.content:
What to stream this week (clockwise from top left): President Curtis; The Devil’s Mouth; Good Fortune; The Dink; Colin From Accounts; and The Bombing of Pan Am 103.

Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Remove items from your saved list to add more. Share A A A

This week’s picks include the bittersweet final season of homegrown hit Colin From Accounts, plus Aaron Chen’s pickleball comedy The Dink, a sombre retelling of The Bombing of Pan Am and Keanu Reeves’ angelic turn in Good Fortune. Colin from Accounts (Binge) ★★★★ It’s bittersweet that Colin from Accounts’ third season is its last. The hit Australian romcom, created by and starring real-life couple Patrick Brammall and Harriet Dyer, has captured hearts around the world for good reason. A sharp balance of rom and com, it’s been distinct and charming right from its first moments – a meet-cute for chaotic Sydney doctor in training Ash (Dyer) and craft brewery owner Gordon (Brammall) involving a nipple flash, a car accident and a shared $12,000 vet bill for a stray border terrier. Related Article Streaming ‘There’s been dumb luck’: Patrick Brammall on Colin, Hollywood haters and what’s next As a relationship formed around their new wheel-assisted dog (the show’s namesake), Colin from Accounts had an ease to its punchlines and cringe comedy thanks to a lived-in chemistry, plus a delightful balance of sweetness and acidity. Any one of those qualities can be hard to come by in the streaming era’s take on comedy, which tends to lean either absurd or overtly dramatic. The only thing more rare is a show going out on its own terms, which is why it’s difficult to be too upset that Brammall and Dyer announced that “creatively, it feels like the right time” for the series to end. Patrick Brammall and Harriet Dyer return for the final season of Colin From Accounts. Binge



So where to for Ash and Gordon? Season three picks up in the aftermath of Gordon’s impromptu drunken proposal at Ash’s friend’s wedding on a crowded dance floor. While I’m sworn to secrecy on specifics, it’s safe to say that the gesture wasn’t received well, and we reunite with the couple at a very different place and time in their lives. Across the four of eight episodes offered for review, Ash and Gordon find themselves – separately and together – questioning what their magnetic hold on each other means. Is it a sign they’re meant to be? Or the result of two broken and bruised people seeing themselves in the other? Harriet Dyer as Ashley and Genevieve Hegney as Chiara in Colin From Accounts. Don’t worry, comedy is still at the forefront. Neither Ash’s friend Megan (Emma Harvie) and her new-age partner Rumi (scene-stealer Virginia Gay) or Gordon’s brewery mates (Genevieve Hegney and Michael Logo) have any time for their moping. Other supporting characters remain as eccentric as ever, including Justin Rosniak as Gordon’s ocker brother, and Ash’s overbearing, manosphere-influencer mum (Helen Thomson). Related Article ★★★★

Review This intoxicating new ABC crime drama will seriously do your head in New characters slot in well. Thomas Cocquerel (All Her Fault, The Gilded Age) plays a handsome golden retriever type who loves pickleball and forgets to shower after shifts at the fish market. “He doesn’t smell great,” says Rosniak’s character. “But at least he’s boring and licks his fingers a lot. And yes, Colin is here, too – the same scraggly, scarred and quirky dog who captured Gordon and Ash’s hearts in the first place. Sounds familiar.



The Dink ★★ (Apple TV) What’s going on with this onslaught of Hollywood comedies about past-their-prime sports pros? Starring Jake Johnson (New Girl) as an ex-tennis star who finds a new joy in pickleball, The Dink is the sixth one in that vein in the last year. Aaron Chen (left) and Jake Johnson in The Dink. At least it’s centred on a fresh sport. Both Chad Powers and The Fall and Rise of Reggie Dinkins tackle gridiron, while golf’s gone overdrive with Happy Gilmore 2, Stick and, just last week, Will Ferrell’s laugh-free Netflix series The Hawk. Related Article Streaming The 30 best movies to stream on Netflix right now Much like the gentle pickleball lob it’s named after, The Dink plods along lightly, pleasant enough but subdued. Johnson plays Dusty, an arrogant middle-aged tennis instructor who was briefly a star in his teens before a disastrous showdown with Andy Roddick. His ego is reliant on two sources: a constant belittling of any pickleball players, and his sycophantic, nerdy co-worker, played by Australian comedian Aaron Chen and The Dink’s most reliable source of laughs. But when his doctor (producer Ben Stiller) recommends he take up pickleball as rehab after a wrist injury, Dusty takes to the small court and meets 70-something divorcee Candace (Mary Steenburgen), and an intriguing relationship blossoms. Their dynamic is by far The Dink’s most interesting element, but it’s all in the purpose of a big, whatever showdown with Roddick (as himself).



Connor Swindells as Detective Sergeant Ed McCusker in The Bombing of Pan Am 103. The Bombing of Pan Am 103 ★★ (Netflix) On December 21, 1988, a plane exploded above the small Scottish town of Lockerbie, killing 270 people, including 11 residents. This six-part fictionalisation, led by Connor Swindells, recreates the UK’s deadliest terrorist attack to date, capturing the immense, awful scale of the flames, debris and destruction over the town. This is the second TV drama about Lockerbie in as many years, following the filing of fresh charges against a third suspect in 2020. While affecting, this sombre series lacks drama or tension. It has little to offer beyond recognition of pain and tragedy. Perhaps that’s enough. The Devil’s Mouth. The Devil’s Mouth ★★ (Amazon Prime Video) Led by a trio of Gen Z stars – Lana Condor (To All The Boys trilogy), Gavin Casalegno (The Summer I Turned Pretty) and Kathryn Newton (Freaky) – this new sharksploitation traps its group of vacationing friends with a vicious shark in an underwater Thai cave. It’s a solid 40 minutes before waters turn red, as The Devil’s Mouth (named after the cave’s jagged, skin-scraping rock formations) sets up traumas and tensions. The devil’s in the details, which this bland horror largely lacks – especially in its muddy underwater scenes, ugly in all the wrong ways. President Curtis.

World.title: ‘I fancied her’: British YouTuber denies raping, assaulting Perth woman after show
World.content:
Breaking NationalWACourts ‘I fancied her’: British YouTuber denies raping, assaulting Perth woman after show Rebecca Peppiatt July 27, 2026 — 2:43pm Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Remove items from your saved list to add more. Share A A A

British YouTube star and influencer Yung Filly has taken to the witness stand to defend allegations he assaulted and raped a young fan after a performance in Perth two years ago. The 30-year-old Londoner, whose real name is Andres Felipe Valencia Barrientos, has been on trial in Perth’s District Court for the last week, with the court hearing evidence from a woman alleging he bit, slapped, strangled and raped her in a hotel room in September 2024. Youtuber Andres Felipe Valencia Barrientos, known as “Yung Filly”, pictured in 2024. Zac Goodwin/PA Images via Getty Images Barrientos denies the allegations, and on Monday told the jury he engaged in consensual sex with the then 20-year-old woman after inviting her back to his hotel room. The comedian and musician told the jury he described himself as an influencer and artist before detailing events during a performance in Perth at the start of his first-ever tour that led to his arrest and 10 charges, including multiple counts of rape and assault.



Barrientos told the jury he asked the woman, “do you want to come home with me?” in the VIP area of Bar1 nightclub in Hillarys after he had been on stage. Related Article Courts Jury shown footage of Yung Filly leaving Perth gig with fan he’s accused of raping He said the pair spoke, he couldn’t remember what was said, but that he recalls “complimenting” her. “I fancied her,” he said. “We got chatting and that was it.” Asked if there was any physical contact between the pair, Barrientos told his lawyer David Edwardson that he recalled putting his hand on her waist.



In her evidence a week ago, the woman claimed Barrientos – who she described as her “idol” – put his hands down the back of her pants and groped her breast during the interaction. “I did not,” Barrientos said on Monday in response to the allegations. “Never happened.” “The vibes were good, she had a real good energy about her,” he said. He then claimed the woman later got into the car with him after he left the venue and went with him to his room at the Intercontinental Hotel on Hay Street. Last week, the woman told the court she thought she was going to an after-party when she left the concert with Barrientos.



She alleged the pair engaged in consensual sex at the Intercontinental Hotel, before it allegedly turned violent. Related Article Graphic content

Courts UK rapper Yung Filly goes on trial accused of sexually assaulting fan after Perth show The woman claimed she “squirmed” to try and stop Barrientos from hurting her and repeatedly told him he was hurting her. “I kept saying, ‘You’re hurting me’,” she told the court. “When he was biting me I was trying to tap him, saying I was tapping out. Each time I said something he would hurt me more.



“Then he told me to stop saying no.” She also alleged that Barrientos penetrated her anally without her consent. Barrientos has pleaded not guilty to 10 charges including sexual penetration without consent, assault occasioning bodily harm and impeding another person’s breathing. World.title: ‘Arsonist shutting down a fire escape’: Forrest fires up on AI, global warming deniers in Perth speech
World.content:
NationalWAGlobal warming ‘Arsonist shutting down a fire escape’: Forrest fires up on AI, global warming deniers in Perth speech Michael Philipps July 27, 2026 — 2:41pm Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Remove items from your saved list to add more. Share A A A

Fortescue executive chairman Andrew Forrest has compared politicians who deny global warming to “arsonists wanting to shut down a fire escape”, claiming the science and technology is available to decarbonise the resources industry economically. The FMG boss also warned it would be “naive to extinction” if nations did not collaborate to govern the growth of artificial intelligence. Andrew Forrest speaking at Boao Forum in Perth on Monday. Photo Ross Swanborough Speaking at the Boao Forum in Perth on Monday, Forrest said while AI would be vital to the green energy transition, it also has great potential to harm. “AI is just part of nature. Its downside is as big as its upside,” he warned delegates. “Its danger is as big as its reward.



“Governance for human safety and collaboration between nations is key with AI. “America, China, Australia – everywhere – let’s collaborate on the governance and human safety of AI. “There’s never been a more powerful nor dangerous invention.” Forrest’s comments come less than two weeks after Prime Minister Anthony Albanese announced plans to ensure data centre operators paid for new energy projects to power their developments, and after research showed most Australians supported the measure. “We want AI to support and create good jobs, not replace them,” Albanese declared at a speech at Sydney University earlier this month.



Forrest added his voice to the prime minister’s comments, warning of the “rush for energy” that would come with the advent of AI – “abundant, if possible, green energy, but any damn energy if you can’t get it”. Related Article Mining Australia’s miners were racing to decarbonise. Why are some tapping the brakes? “Such is that rush, that unseemly haste, that dangerous crusade into more global warming,” he said. “If we don’t cool our artificial intelligence factory data centre jets and say, ‘Hold it’. “You’re big enough and ugly enough and powerful enough to make your own energy. That has to be green. To make your own water, that has to be green.



“Let’s head off that spectre of global warming danger, called data centres and the proliferation of AI tapping into the national grids of everyone, and ask them to stand on their own two very powerful legs.” Forrest also called on greater collaboration between nations to prepare for the green energy transition. “We all know that resources, technology alone, won’t determine who succeeds,” he said. “Prosperity and partnership will belong to those who are prepared to build, those who are prepared to build together. “We must concentrate on skills. We do not subjugate our children’s brains to artificial intelligence.



“Build their skills, even though there’s an easy way out for academic laziness. “The subjugation of our own intelligence to computers must never happen.” Forrest said the economic and technical solutions to global warming and the green energy transition are available, but questioned if the corporate and political leadership was there to match it. “Don’t ask companies to decarbonise when you get a carbon credit … for $37 a ton, but you get a diesel fuel rebate for nearly $200 a ton,” he said. “Don’t turn around and ask the big end of town to decarbonise when you’re literally paying them $170 a ton … and saying it’s policy which is responsible.



“We need to lean forward, accept the fact that global warming is upon us. “If you deny, like some politicians have, this is like an arsonist wanting to shut down a fire escape. You are a big part of the problem, but economics are not with you.” Start the day with a summary of the day’s most important and interesting stories, analysis and insights.

World.title: Dalaroo set for 20,000m West African gold drill
World.content:
Sponsored BusinessCompaniesBulls N' Bears Dalaroo set for 20,000m West African gold drill Brought to you by BULLS N’ BEARS Murray Ward July 27, 2026 — 2:29pm Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Remove items from your saved list to add more. Share A A A

Dalaroo Metals is poised to unleash a massive 20,000-metre maiden drilling campaign at its Gold Ridge prospect, part of the Bondoukou gold project in the West African nation of Côte d’Ivoire. The company says final operational planning is underway, with drill pad preparation slated to kick off in the coming week and the drill rods to start spinning in early August. Final site planning at the Wilfred target ahead of Dalaroo Metals initial 10,000 metre RC drilling project at its Bondoukou gold project in Côte d’Ivoire. The campaign will be in three stages, starting with a 10,000m reverse circulation (RC) drilling program. Phase one will focus on the Wilfred target, the largest of three priority targets the company has identified along a seven-kilometre gold corridor. First RC holes are planned to reach depths between 100m and 150m testing a host of geological and geochemical targets. Dalaroo says it has chosen RC drilling for the discovery phase because of its faster drilling rate and lower cost. This allows it to test a bigger number of targets to home in on what it considers high priority zones.



‘The RC program is to systematically test Wilfred, identify the strongest areas of mineralisation and hone in on the target zones.’ Dalaroo Metals chief executive officer John Morgan The results from this phase will guide a more targeted follow-up diamond drilling campaign with phases two and three planned to include another 10,000m of diamond drilling across all three of the company’s main targets at Gold Ridge, Wilfred, Mag and Ali. The company’s exploration activities have expanded the Gold Ridge target from a concept into a major seven-kilometre gold-in-soil anomalous corridor. The campaign has been backed by a wealth of exploration data, including soil and auger geochem, geological mapping, rock-chip sampling and the pinpointing of historical artisanal workings. The company’s next steps include the start of drill pad preparation at Wilfred, pegging the final phase-one drill-hole locations and mobilising the RC rig to site. Dalaroo Metals chief executive officer John Morgan said: “Our decision to initially concentrate drilling at Wilfred is deliberate and technically driven. Wilfred is the largest of the three priority targets and provides the scale, geological setting and supporting exploration datasets required for a substantial first-phase drilling program.”



Whilst the imminent West African drill campaign is the main event, Dalaroo holds a diverse portfolio of projects across Greenland and Western Australia. In southern Greenland, the company recently wrapped up its largest-ever field program at its Blue Lagoon rare earths project. The work already completed has upgraded the project from an early-stage concept into what the company says is a well-defined regional rare earth system, with four new prospects identified. More than 200 samples from that program are currently in the lab with upcoming results expected to provide hefty news flow. Adding another string to its bow, in Western Australia, Dalaroo holds the Lyons River and neighbouring Watheroo projects in the Gascoyne province where it was awarded a government co-funding grant for drilling after confirming the discovery of a gold system there in April. But with drill pad preparations about to get underway for a 20,000m program at Bondoukou, the company has a firm eye on operations in Côte d’Ivoire. The country is regarded globally as a tier one mining jurisdiction forming part of the highly endowed Birimian greenstone belt of West Africa. And now Dalaroo is about to get a serious look at what might lurk beneath the surface under its feet on land that hosts some of the world’s largest gold deposits. Is your ASX-listed company doing something interesting? Contact: mattbirney@bullsnbears.com.au

Socialite and former reality television star Brynne Edelsten will no longer face drug trafficking charges after indicating she will instead plead guilty to possession offences.

The 43-year-old faced Melbourne Magistrates’ Court on Monday morning for a brief hearing in which her lawyer confirmed the case had been resolved.

Brynne Edelsten outside Melbourne Magistrates’ Court on Monday. AAP

World.title: Victorian politics is a mess. Who on earth can you vote for in this state?
World.content:
PoliticsVictoriaPolitical leadership Opinion Victorian politics is a mess. Who on earth can you vote for in this state? Michael Bachelard Senior writer, The Age July 27, 2026 — 2:12pm

July 27, 2026 — 2:12pm Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Remove items from your saved list to add more. Share A A A

Whether or not Jacinta Allan emerges victorious from the leadership spasm now racking her party, we Victorians will confront a serious question: who the hell can we vote for in four months’ time? Under Allan’s leadership, Labor has overseen malfeasance of extraordinary proportions – direct links between ministerial offices and the CFMEU, and from there to standover men, bikies, and an estimated $15 billion in excess costs to the taxpayer. Victorian Premier Jacinta Allan’s leadership is under threat. Penny Stephens Thanks primarily to reporting in The Age, everyone can see this steaming pile of scandal looming over Allan, no matter how hard she denies its existence. The proudest boast of the Andrews government – that it built things – is now hopelessly tainted by corruption. Allan wants to “grind it out”, defying calls for a royal commission that she says will not bring about cultural change. Add another trailer-load to the heap, Jacinta. You don’t want a royal commission because either you know what it will dig up and it will implicate your government, or you don’t know, and what’s buried there terrifies you.



Meanwhile, this government has become so paranoid and centrally controlled that ministers are rarely let out to speak, and when they are, it’s with talking points crafted so narrowly by the premier’s private office that they end up saying nothing. If Allan wins this leadership bout, or stares down her opponents, only the most rusted-on true believer could vote Labor in November, and even if she is replaced by her deputy, Ben Carroll, serious questions remain about the party that’s led us since 2014. Leader in waiting? Education Minister Ben Carroll earlier this month. Ruby Alexander Only the immediate announcement of a royal commission with full powers and the opening of public hearings into the Big Build scandal before the election could, possibly, allow us to take another look. Any other inquiry held under this state’s usual modus operandi (“trust us and shut up”) will fall short. Allan’s proposed solution of a crime commission is of this kind. Our current so-called anti-corruption commission, IBAC, shows why.



Eight years ago, in 2018, it launched a probe into a suspicious deal made between the firefighters’ union and Daniel Andrews. Andrews was interviewed, but in private – not for the only time during his premiership. Nothing of his evidence, or that of the man he allegedly did the deal with, union secretary Peter Marshall, has emerged publicly. Operating under weak laws and a statewide culture of secrecy, IBAC took four years to reach its conclusions, and another four years fighting to release them. Eight years after voters could have benefited from a public airing of these allegations, we are still waiting to know what Labor did in our name. Meanwhile we re-elected them, in a landslide, and in ignorance. Operation Richmond centred on dealings between Daniel Andrews’ government and the United Firefighters Union under Peter Marshall. Marija Ercegovac IBAC is a Potemkin village of an anti-corruption commission – it looks like one at a glance but behind the facade there’s nothing. For the $100 billion Big Build, this is not good enough. Only a credible royal commissioner with the power to demand documents, compel witnesses and air it all in public can do the Herculean work of mucking out Labor’s Augean stable.





The last time Victoria rejected Labor, we picked Ted Baillieu as premier. He served for a brief, indolent and scandal-plagued term (anyone remember MP Geoff Shaw?) before being replaced by Denis Napthine. Related Article Exclusive

Building Bad Allan’s wrong: Top crime fighters insist royal commission only solution Their two main achievements in government were to legislate for a hollowed-out anti-corruption commission and allow Labor time to reset and appoint Daniel Andrews as leader. This year there is a third choice – of sorts – One Nation, and 22 per cent of Victorians seem to be making it, according to The Age’s Resolve poll. It’s a party with no state leader, no candidates and who knows what policies except for “I don’t like it.” Jess Wilson and Jacinta Allan are effectively campaigning against an empty chair and ceding more than one-fifth of the primary vote to it. Allan’s approval rating is minus 42, her likeability minus 36.



How have her party’s once-powerful factions tolerated it for so long? This is shaping as a classic pox-on–both-your-houses election. But if the pox kills off all our genuine governing options, then what kind of zombies will be left holding power for the next four years? That is what causes me to wake up in fright. Michael Bachelard is a senior writer. The Opinion newsletter is a weekly wrap of views that will challenge, champion and inform your own. Sign up here.

World.title: Alan Jones ‘anxious to have his day in court’ as push for trial delay abandoned
World.content:
NationalNSWCourts Alan Jones ‘anxious to have his day in court’ as push for trial delay abandoned Clare Sibthorpe July 27, 2026 — 3:03pm Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Remove items from your saved list to add more. Share A A A

Alan Jones’ defence team has abandoned a push to delay his indecent assault and sexual touching trial as he is “anxious to have his day in court”. Last week, Local Court Judge Glenn Walsh said the former broadcaster’s lawyers had filed a motion seeking either a temporary halt in the proceedings, known as a stay, or an order that certain evidence from devices seized from the former broadcaster’s apartment was inadmissible in the trial slated to start on August 3. Alan Jones faces 22 charges relating to six complainants. Sam Mooy The motion sought a stay “until the Office of the Director of Public Prosecutions identifies by reference to items, dates and times the data from devices seized on 18 November 2024 from the accused’s home that is relied upon”. However, as pretrial arguments continued on Monday, defence barrister Gabrielle Bashir, SC, told Downing Centre Local Court they would no longer press ahead with the motion, saying the issue could be dealt with in the trial.



“In relation to the devices … the prosecution are declining to identify the subject matter,” Bashir said. “That is something that will be able to be dealt with in the case of proceedings. So your honour, it’s not our intention to move on that motion, which also was always a stay in relation to identification of the evidence.” Bashir said Jones was “anxious to have his day in court”. Alan Jones’ barrister Gabrielle Bashir, SC, and instructing solicitor Bryan Wrench at an earlier court appearance for Jones. Clare Sibthorpe “We want to start on August 3. I think all of the parties are moving for that to happen.”



Jones has pleaded not guilty to 22 charges of indecent assault and sexual touching relating to six complainants spanning from 2003 to 2020. Related Article Courts Dispute over seized devices may delay Alan Jones trial The 85-year-old is accused of committing the 22 crimes at his harbourside apartment, his farm at Fitzroy Falls in the Southern Highlands, and a lower north shore restaurant, among other venues in Sydney. In a pretrial decision last week the judge ruled in favour of the Crown and will allow prosecutors to rely on types of circumstantial evidence known as tendency and coincidence in the trial. Prosecutors will seek to prove Jones engaged in a pattern of behaviour when acting on his alleged sexual interest in “significantly younger” men.



But the judge made clear Jones “has the presumption of innocence” and “it is the prosecution that bear the onus of proof throughout, beyond reasonable doubt, for each element of each offence as charged”. The Crown expects to call 76 witnesses but that number could grow, the court earlier heard. Strike Force Bonnefin was established to investigate the former teacher and Wallabies coach following a major investigation by The Sydney Morning Herald and The Age. Jones’ trial is scheduled to run from August 3 until potentially December. Start the day with a summary of the day’s most important and interesting stories, analysis and insights.

It’s a solid 40 minutes before waters turn red, as The Devil’s Mouth (named after the cave’s jagged, skin-scraping rock formations) sets up traumas and tensions. The devil’s in the details, which this bland horror largely lacks – especially in its muddy underwater scenes, ugly in all the wrong ways. President Curtis.

World.title: ‘I fancied her’: British YouTuber denies raping, assaulting Perth woman after show
World.content:
Breaking NationalWACourts ‘I fancied her’: British YouTuber denies raping, assaulting Perth woman after show Rebecca Peppiatt July 27, 2026 — 2:43pm Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Remove items from your saved list to add more. Share A A A

British YouTube star and influencer Yung Filly has taken to the witness stand to defend allegations he assaulted and raped a young fan after a performance in Perth two years ago. The 30-year-old Londoner, whose real name is Andres Felipe Valencia Barrientos, has been on trial in Perth’s District Court for the last week, with the court hearing evidence from a woman alleging he bit, slapped, strangled and raped her in a hotel room in September 2024. Youtuber Andres Felipe Valencia Barrientos, known as “Yung Filly”, pictured in 2024. Zac Goodwin/PA Images via Getty Images Barrientos denies the allegations, and on Monday told the jury he engaged in consensual sex with the then 20-year-old woman after inviting her back to his hotel room. The comedian and musician told the jury he described himself as an influencer and artist before detailing events during a performance in Perth at the start of his first-ever tour that led to his arrest and 10 charges, including multiple counts of rape and assault.



Barrientos told the jury he asked the woman, “do you want to come home with me?” in the VIP area of Bar1 nightclub in Hillarys after he had been on stage. Related Article Courts Jury shown footage of Yung Filly leaving Perth gig with fan he’s accused of raping He said the pair spoke, he couldn’t remember what was said, but that he recalls “complimenting” her. “I fancied her,” he said. “We got chatting and that was it.” Asked if there was any physical contact between the pair, Barrientos told his lawyer David Edwardson that he recalled putting his hand on her waist.



In her evidence a week ago, the woman claimed Barrientos – who she described as her “idol” – put his hands down the back of her pants and groped her breast during the interaction. “I did not,” Barrientos said on Monday in response to the allegations. “Never happened.” “The vibes were good, she had a real good energy about her,” he said. He then claimed the woman later got into the car with him after he left the venue and went with him to his room at the Intercontinental Hotel on Hay Street. Last week, the woman told the court she thought she was going to an after-party when she left the concert with Barrientos.



She alleged the pair engaged in consensual sex at the Intercontinental Hotel, before it allegedly turned violent. Related Article Graphic content

Courts UK rapper Yung Filly goes on trial accused of sexually assaulting fan after Perth show The woman claimed she “squirmed” to try and stop Barrientos from hurting her and repeatedly told him he was hurting her. “I kept saying, ‘You’re hurting me’,” she told the court. “When he was biting me I was trying to tap him, saying I was tapping out. Each time I said something he would hurt me more.



“Then he told me to stop saying no.” She also alleged that Barrientos penetrated her anally without her consent. Barrientos has pleaded not guilty to 10 charges including sexual penetration without consent, assault occasioning bodily harm and impeding another person’s breathing. National Sexual Assault, Domestic Family Violence Counselling Service 1800RESPECT (1800 737 732). World.title: ‘Arsonist shutting down a fire escape’: Forrest fires up on AI, global warming deniers in Perth speech
World.content:
NationalWAGlobal warming ‘Arsonist shutting down a fire escape’: Forrest fires up on AI, global warming deniers in Perth speech Michael Philipps July 27, 2026 — 2:41pm Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Remove items from your saved list to add more. Share A A A

Fortescue executive chairman Andrew Forrest has compared politicians who deny global warming to “arsonists wanting to shut down a fire escape”, claiming the science and technology is available to decarbonise the resources industry economically. The FMG boss also warned it would be “naive to extinction” if nations did not collaborate to govern the growth of artificial intelligence. Andrew Forrest speaking at Boao Forum in Perth on Monday. Photo Ross Swanborough Speaking at the Boao Forum in Perth on Monday, Forrest said while AI would be vital to the green energy transition, it also has great potential to harm. “AI is just part of nature. Its downside is as big as its upside,” he warned delegates. “Its danger is as big as its reward.



“Governance for human safety and collaboration between nations is key with AI. “America, China, Australia – everywhere – let’s collaborate on the governance and human safety of AI. “There’s never been a more powerful nor dangerous invention.” Forrest’s comments come less than two weeks after Prime Minister Anthony Albanese announced plans to ensure data centre operators paid for new energy projects to power their developments, and after research showed most Australians supported the measure. “We want AI to support and create good jobs, not replace them,” Albanese declared at a speech at Sydney University earlier this month.



Forrest added his voice to the prime minister’s comments, warning of the “rush for energy” that would come with the advent of AI – “abundant, if possible, green energy, but any damn energy if you can’t get it”. Related Article Mining Australia’s miners were racing to decarbonise. Why are some tapping the brakes? “Such is that rush, that unseemly haste, that dangerous crusade into more global warming,” he said. “If we don’t cool our artificial intelligence factory data centre jets and say, ‘Hold it’. “You’re big enough and ugly enough and powerful enough to make your own energy. That has to be green. To make your own water, that has to be green.



“Let’s head off that spectre of global warming danger, called data centres and the proliferation of AI tapping into the national grids of everyone, and ask them to stand on their own two very powerful legs.” Forrest also called on greater collaboration between nations to prepare for the green energy transition. “We all know that resources, technology alone, won’t determine who succeeds,” he said. “Prosperity and partnership will belong to those who are prepared to build, those who are prepared to build together. “We must concentrate on skills. We do not subjugate our children’s brains to artificial intelligence.



“Build their skills, even though there’s an easy way out for academic laziness. “The subjugation of our own intelligence to computers must never happen.” Forrest said the economic and technical solutions to global warming and the green energy transition are available, but questioned if the corporate and political leadership was there to match it. “Don’t ask companies to decarbonise when you get a carbon credit … for $37 a ton, but you get a diesel fuel rebate for nearly $200 a ton,” he said. “Don’t turn around and ask the big end of town to decarbonise when you’re literally paying them $170 a ton … and saying it’s policy which is responsible.



“We need to lean forward, accept the fact that global warming is upon us. “If you deny, like some politicians have, this is like an arsonist wanting to shut down a fire escape. You are a big part of the problem, but economics are not with you.” Start the day with a summary of the day’s most important and interesting stories, analysis and insights.

World.title: Dalaroo set for 20,000m West African gold drill
World.content:
Sponsored BusinessCompaniesBulls N' Bears Dalaroo set for 20,000m West African gold drill Brought to you by BULLS N’ BEARS Murray Ward July 27, 2026 — 2:29pm Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Remove items from your saved list to add more. Share A A A

Dalaroo Metals is poised to unleash a massive 20,000-metre maiden drilling campaign at its Gold Ridge prospect, part of the Bondoukou gold project in the West African nation of Côte d’Ivoire. The company says final operational planning is underway, with drill pad preparation slated to kick off in the coming week and the drill rods to start spinning in early August. Final site planning at the Wilfred target ahead of Dalaroo Metals initial 10,000 metre RC drilling project at its Bondoukou gold project in Côte d’Ivoire. The campaign will be in three stages, starting with a 10,000m reverse circulation (RC) drilling program. Phase one will focus on the Wilfred target, the largest of three priority targets the company has identified along a seven-kilometre gold corridor. First RC holes are planned to reach depths between 100m and 150m testing a host of geological and geochemical targets. Dalaroo says it has chosen RC drilling for the discovery phase because of its faster drilling rate and lower cost. This allows it to test a bigger number of targets to home in on what it considers high priority zones.



‘The RC program is to systematically test Wilfred, identify the strongest areas of mineralisation and hone in on the target zones.’ Dalaroo Metals chief executive officer John Morgan The results from this phase will guide a more targeted follow-up diamond drilling campaign with phases two and three planned to include another 10,000m of diamond drilling across all three of the company’s main targets at Gold Ridge, Wilfred, Mag and Ali. The company’s exploration activities have expanded the Gold Ridge target from a concept into a major seven-kilometre gold-in-soil anomalous corridor. The campaign has been backed by a wealth of exploration data, including soil and auger geochem, geological mapping, rock-chip sampling and the pinpointing of historical artisanal workings. The company’s next steps include the start of drill pad preparation at Wilfred, pegging the final phase-one drill-hole locations and mobilising the RC rig to site. Dalaroo Metals chief executive officer John Morgan said: “Our decision to initially concentrate drilling at Wilfred is deliberate and technically driven. Wilfred is the largest of the three priority targets and provides the scale, geological setting and supporting exploration datasets required for a substantial first-phase drilling program.”



Whilst the imminent West African drill campaign is the main event, Dalaroo holds a diverse portfolio of projects across Greenland and Western Australia. In southern Greenland, the company recently wrapped up its largest-ever field program at its Blue Lagoon rare earths project. The work already completed has upgraded the project from an early-stage concept into what the company says is a well-defined regional rare earth system, with four new prospects identified. More than 200 samples from that program are currently in the lab with upcoming results expected to provide hefty news flow. Adding another string to its bow, in Western Australia, Dalaroo holds the Lyons River and neighbouring Watheroo projects in the Gascoyne province where it was awarded a government co-funding grant for drilling after confirming the discovery of a gold system there in April. But with drill pad preparations about to get underway for a 20,000m program at Bondoukou, the company has a firm eye on operations in Côte d’Ivoire. The country is regarded globally as a tier one mining jurisdiction forming part of the highly endowed Birimian greenstone belt of West Africa. And now Dalaroo is about to get a serious look at what might lurk beneath the surface under its feet on land that hosts some of the world’s largest gold deposits. Socialite and former reality television star Brynne Edelsten will no longer face drug trafficking charges after indicating she will instead plead guilty to possession offences.

The 43-year-old faced Melbourne Magistrates’ Court on Monday morning for a brief hearing in which her lawyer confirmed the case had been resolved.

Brynne Edelsten outside Melbourne Magistrates’ Court on Monday. AAP

The American-born former wife of late businessman and deregistered doctor Geoffrey Edelsten originally faced nine charges, including one count of trafficking a commercial quantity of methamphetamine.
